At the moment of rebirth-linking... (5)

Avitakkaavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (6)

Dependent on a state without applied and sustained thought, states with applied and sustained thought and states without applied thought but with sustained thought only arise... Dependent on the base, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking... (6)

(Paṭhamaghaṭanāyaṃ sampuṇṇā satta pañhā kātabbā.)

(In the first combination, the seven questions are to be completed.)

52. Avitakkavicāramattañca avitakkaavicārañca dhammaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicāro dhammo uppajjati…pe… vitakkañca vatthuñca paccayā savitakkasavicārā khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe….

52. Dependent on a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only and a state without applied and sustained thought, a state with applied and sustained thought arises... Dependent on applied thought and the base, aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking...

Avitakkavicāramattañca avitakkaavicārañca dhammaṃ paccayā avitakkavicāramatto dhammo uppajjati…pe… avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca paccayā avitakkavicāramattā adhipati, avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā avitakkavicāramattā [V 2.0040] adhipati, vipākaṃ avitakkavicāramattaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vicārañca paccayā…pe… vipākaṃ avitakkavicāramattaṃ ekaṃ khandhañca vatthuñca paccayā tayo khandhā…pe….

Dependent on a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only and a state without applied and sustained thought, a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only arises... Dependent on aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought only and on sustained thought, predominance factors without applied thought but with sustained thought only arise; dependent on aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought only and the base, predominance factors without applied thought but with sustained thought only arise; dependent on one resultant aggregate without applied thought but with sustained thought only and on sustained thought... dependent on one resultant aggregate without applied thought but with sustained thought only and the base, three aggregates arise...

(Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pañca pañhā kātabbā. Yattha [T 2.0046] avitakkavicāramattaṃ āgacchati tattha vipākaṃ kātabbaṃ. Naadhipatimūlake sattatiṃsa pañhā kātabbā.)

(At the moment of rebirth-linking, five questions are to be formulated. Where 'without applied thought but with sustained thought only' occurs, 'resultant' should be understood. In the section rooted in non-predominance, thirty-seven questions are to be formulated.)

Naanantarapaccayādi

Non-Immediacy Condition, etc.

53. Naanantarampi naanantarepi (ka.) nasamanantarampi naaññamaññampi naupanissayampi satta pañhā rūpaṃyeva. Napurejāte sattatiṃsa paṭiccavārapaccanīyasadisaṃ. Napacchājāte sattatiṃsa[M 2.0034], naāsevanepi sadisaṃ. Yattha avitakkavicāramattopi āgacchati, tattha vipākā kātabbā.

53. In non-immediacy, non-contiguity, non-mutuality, and non-support conditions, the seven questions concern only material form. In non-pre-nascence condition, thirty-seven are similar to the negative of the conditional occurrence section. In non-post-nascence condition, thirty-seven; similarly in non-repetition condition. Wherever even a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only occurs, there resultants are to be included.

Nakammapaccayo

Non-Kamma Condition

54. Savitakkasavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicāro dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – savitakkasavicāre khandhe paccayā savitakkasavicārā cetanā. (1)

54. Dependent on a state with applied and sustained thought, a state with applied and sustained thought arises by non-kamma condition. That is, dependent on the aggregates with applied and sustained thought, volition with applied and sustained thought arises. (1)

Avitakkavicāramattaṃ dhammaṃ paccayā avitakkavicāramatto dhammo…pe… avitakkavicāramatte khandhe paccayā avitakkavicāramattā cetanā. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo…pe… vitakkaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicārā cetanā. (2)

Dependent on a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only, a state without applied thought but with sustained thought only arises…pe… dependent on the aggregates without applied thought but with sustained thought only, volition without applied thought but with sustained thought only arises. Dependent on a state with applied and sustained thought…pe… dependent on applied thought, volition with applied and sustained thought arises. (2)

Avitakkaavicāraṃ dhammaṃ paccayā avitakkaavicāro dhammo…pe… avitakkaavicārā cetanā…pe… (paripuṇṇaṃ kātabbaṃ) savitakkasavicāro…pe… vatthuṃ paccayā savitakkasavicārā cetanā. Avitakkavicāramatto…pe… vicāraṃ paccayā avitakkavicāramattā cetanā. Vatthuṃ paccayā avitakkavicāramattā cetanā. (3)

Dependent on a state without applied and sustained thought, a state without applied and sustained thought arises…pe… volition without applied and sustained thought…pe… (this should be completed in full). Dependent on a state with applied and sustained thought…pe… dependent on the physical base, volition with applied and sustained thought arises. Dependent on a state with only sustained thought…pe… dependent on sustained thought, volition with only sustained thought arises. Dependent on the physical base, volition with only sustained thought arises. (3)

55. Savitakkasavicārañca avitakkaavicārañca dhammaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicāro dhammo…pe… savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā savitakkasavicārā cetanā. (1)

55. Dependent on a state with applied and sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought, a state with applied and sustained thought arises…pe… dependent on the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and the physical base, volition with applied and sustained thought arises. (1)

Avitakkavicāramattañca [V 2.0041] avitakkaavicārañca dhammaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicāro dhammo…pe… vitakkañca vatthuñca paccayā savitakkasavicārā cetanā. (1)

Dependent on a state with only sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought, a state with applied and sustained thought arises…pe… dependent on applied thought and the physical base, volition with applied and sustained thought arises. (1)

Avitakkavicāramattañca avitakkaavicārañca dhammaṃ paccayā avitakkavicāramatto dhammo…pe… avitakkavicāramatte [T 2.0047] khandhe ca vicārañca paccayā avitakkavicāramattā cetanā. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā avitakkavicāramattā cetanā. (2)

Dependent on a state with only sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought, a state with only sustained thought arises…pe… dependent on the aggregates with only sustained thought and sustained thought, volition with only sustained thought arises. Dependent on the aggregates with only sustained thought and the physical base, volition with only sustained thought arises. (2)

Savitakkasavicārañca avitakkavicāramattañca dhammaṃ paccayā savitakkasavicāro dhammo…pe… savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca paccayā savitakkasavicārā cetanā. (1)

At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots with applied and sustained thought are a condition for kamma-originated material phenomena by way of root condition. (3)

Savitakkasavicāro [M 2.0039] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ [T 2.0051] khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (4)

At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots with applied and sustained thought are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena by way of root condition. (4)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārā hetū vitakkassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā hetū vitakkassa kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought and for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of root condition. Savitakkasavicāro [V 2.0047] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkaavicārā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

69. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati; pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati; savitakkasavicārā [T 2.0053] jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhati. Ariyā pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

69. A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. After giving alms, undertaking the precepts, or performing the Uposatha observance, one reviews that; one reviews past good deeds. Having emerged from a jhāna with applied and sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, one reviews the fruition. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements, review the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements previously practiced. They contemplate the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self; they relish them and delight in them. Taking that as object, lust arises…pe… grief arises. Taking the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati; taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati; savitakkasavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhati; taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Ariyā pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe aniccato dukkhato [M 2.0041] anattato vipassanti assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. (2)

A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of object condition. After giving alms, undertaking the precepts, or performing the Uposatha observance, one reviews that; taking that as object, applied thought arises. One reviews past good deeds; having emerged from a jhāna with applied and sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, one reviews the fruition; taking that as object, applied thought arises. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements, review the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements previously practiced. They contemplate the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relish them, and delight in them; taking that as object, applied thought arises. Taking the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as object, applied thought arises. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cetopariyañāṇena savitakkasavicāracittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti; savitakkasavicārā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa[T 2.0054], pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe ārabbha avitakkaavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. With the knowledge of others' minds, one knows the mind of one who possesses a mind with applied and sustained thought. The aggregates with applied and sustained thought are a condition by way of object for the knowledge of others' minds, for the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, and for the knowledge of the future. Taking the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as object, aggregates without applied and sustained thought arise. (3)

Savitakkasavicāro [V 2.0049] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati; savitakkasavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhati; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Ariyā pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (4)

A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for both a state with applied and sustained thought and a state without applied thought but with only sustained thought by way of object condition. After giving a gift, undertaking the precepts, or performing the Uposatha observance, one reviews that; taking that as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. One reviews past good deeds; having emerged from a jhāna with applied and sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, one reviews the fruition; taking that as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. Noble ones review the abandoned defilements, review the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements previously practiced. They contemplate the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relish them, and delight in them; taking that as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. Taking the aggregates with applied and sustained thought as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (4)

70. Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhati; taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha vitakko [T 2.0055] uppajjati. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. (1)

70. A state without applied thought but with only sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought but with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought but with only sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, one reviews the fruition; taking that as object, applied thought arises. One contemplates the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; taking that as object, applied thought arises. Taking the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as object, applied thought arises. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca aniccato dukkhato anattato [M 2.0042] vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A state without applied thought but with only sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. Having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought but with only sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, one reviews the fruition; taking that as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. One contemplates the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; taking that as object, lust arises…pe… grief arises. Taking the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cetopariyañāṇena avitakkavicāramattacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Avitakkavicāramattā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa [V 2.0050] ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha avitakkaavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A state without applied thought but with only sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. With the knowledge of others' minds, one knows the mind of one who possesses a mind without applied thought but with only sustained thought. The aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought are a condition by way of object for the knowledge of others' minds, for the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, and for the knowledge of the future. Taking the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as object, aggregates without applied and sustained thought arise. (3)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhati; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Avitakkavicāramatte [T 2.0056] khandhe ca vitakkañca aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (4)

A state without applied thought but with only sustained thought is a condition for both a state with applied and sustained thought and a state without applied thought but with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Having emerged from a jhāna without applied thought but with only sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, one reviews the fruition; taking that as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. One contemplates the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; taking that as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. Taking the aggregates without applied thought but with only sustained thought and applied thought as object, aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (4)

71. Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ avitakkaavicārassa maggassa phalassa vicārassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena avitakkaavicāracittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicārā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha avitakkaavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

71. A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. Nibbāna is a condition by way of object for the path, fruition, and sustained thought, which are without applied and sustained thought. One sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear element, and with the knowledge of others' minds knows the mind of one who possesses a mind without applied and sustained thought. The base of infinite space is a condition by way of object for the base of infinite consciousness…pe… the base of nothingness is a condition by way of object for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. The form base is a condition by way of object for eye-consciousness…pe… the tangible base is a condition by way of object for body-consciousness. The aggregates without applied and sustained thought are a condition by way of object for the knowledge of supernormal powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, and for the knowledge of the future. Taking the aggregates without applied and sustained thought and sustained thought as object, aggregates without applied and sustained thought arise. (1)

Avitakkaavicāro [M 2.0043] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā avitakkaavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. Ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ [T 2.0057] gotrabhussa vodānassa savitakkasavicārassa maggassa phalassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Sotaṃ… ghānaṃ [V 2.0051]… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied and sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, review the fruition; taking that as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. Noble ones review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition by way of object condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path with applied and sustained thought, for fruition, and for adverting. One contemplates the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes it, and delights in it; taking that as object, lust arises…pe… grief arises. The ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… forms… sounds… smells… tastes… tangibles… the physical basis… one contemplates the aggregates without applied and sustained thought and sustained thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; taking that as object, lust arises…pe… grief arises. Taking the aggregates without applied and sustained thought and sustained thought as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. (2)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā avitakkaavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti; taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa phalassa vitakkassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato…pe… vatthuṃ… avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. (3)

A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied and sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, review the fruition; taking that as object, applied thought arises. Noble ones review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition by way of object condition for the path with only sustained thought, for fruition, and for applied thought. One contemplates the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self…pe… the physical basis… one contemplates the aggregates without applied and sustained thought and sustained thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; taking that as object, applied thought arises. Taking the aggregates without applied and sustained thought and sustained thought as object, applied thought arises. (3)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa phalassa vicārassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena [T 2.0058] paccayo. (4)

A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought and for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. Nibbāna is a condition by way of object condition for the path with only sustained thought, for fruition, and for sustained thought. (4)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā avitakkaavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa vitakkassa ca vodānassa vitakkassa ca savitakkasavicārassa maggassa vitakkassa ca savitakkasavicārassa phalassa vitakkassa ca āvajjanāya vitakkassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena [M 2.0044] paccayo. Cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Sotaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbaṃ… vatthuṃ… avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (5)

A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought and for a state with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied and sustained thought, from the path, or from the fruition, review the fruition; taking that as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. Noble ones review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition by way of object condition for change-of-lineage and for applied thought, for purification and for applied thought, for the path with applied and sustained thought and for applied thought, for the fruition with applied and sustained thought and for applied thought, and for adverting and for applied thought. One contemplates the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes it, and delights in it; taking that as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. The ear…pe… tangibles… the physical basis… one contemplates the aggregates without applied and sustained thought and sustained thought as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, relishes them, and delights in them; taking that as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (5)

72. Avitakkavicāramatto [V 2.0052] ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

72. A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought are conditions for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates with only sustained thought and sustained thought, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. (2)

A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought are conditions for a state with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates with only sustained thought and sustained thought, applied thought arises. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa [T 2.0059] dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro ca cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha avitakkaavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought are conditions for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. The aggregates with only sustained thought and sustained thought are conditions by way of object condition for the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of recollecting past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and the knowledge of the future. Taking as object the aggregates with only sustained thought and sustained thought, the aggregates without applied and sustained thought arise. (3)

Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (4)

A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought are conditions for a state with applied and sustained thought and for a state with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates with only sustained thought and sustained thought, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (4)

73. Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

73. A state with applied and sustained thought and a state with only sustained thought are conditions for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought arise. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. (2)

A state with applied and sustained thought and a state with only sustained thought are conditions for a state with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought, applied thought arises. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro [M 2.0045] ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa[V 2.0053], yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha avitakkaavicārā [T 2.0060] khandhā uppajjanti. (3)

States with initial thought and sustained thought, and states without initial thought but with only sustained thought, are a condition for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of object condition. The aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought, and initial thought, are a condition by way of object for the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of past lives, the knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their actions, and the knowledge of the future. Taking as object the aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought and initial thought, aggregates without initial thought and without sustained thought arise. (3)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (4)

States with initial thought and sustained thought, and states without initial thought but with only sustained thought, are a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought and for a state without initial thought but with only sustained thought by way of object condition. Taking as object the aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought and initial thought, aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought and initial thought arise. (4)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

74. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati. Savitakkasavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkasavicārā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

74. A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought by way of dominance condition—as object dominance or co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on that, making it predominant; having previously performed meritorious deeds, one reflects on them, making them predominant. Having emerged from a jhāna with initial thought and sustained thought, having emerged from a path, having emerged from a fruition, one reflects on the fruition, making it predominant. One savors and delights in the aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought, making them predominant; making that predominant, lust arises, or wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati. Savitakkasavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti[T 2.0061]; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkasavicārā adhipati vitakkassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without initial thought but with only sustained thought by way of dominance condition—as object dominance or co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on that, making it predominant; making that predominant, initial thought arises. Having previously performed meritorious deeds, one reflects on them, making them predominant. Having emerged from a jhāna with initial thought and sustained thought, having emerged from a path, having emerged from a fruition, they reflect on the fruition, making it predominant; making that predominant, initial thought arises. One savors and delights in the aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought, making them predominant; making that predominant, initial thought arises. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for initial thought by way of dominance condition. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro [M 2.0046] dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati [V 2.0054] – savitakkasavicārā adhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (3)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkasavicārā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought and for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (4)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkasavicārā adhipati vitakkassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without initial thought but with only sustained thought, and for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought, by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for initial thought and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (5)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā, uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ [T 2.0062] katvā paccavekkhati, savitakkasavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Savitakkasavicāre khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkasavicārā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (6)

A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought and for a state without initial thought but with only sustained thought by way of dominance condition—as object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on that, making it predominant; making that predominant, aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought and initial thought arise. Having previously performed meritorious deeds, one reflects on them, making them predominant; having emerged from a jhāna with initial thought and sustained thought, having emerged from a path, having emerged from a fruition, one reflects on the fruition, making it predominant; making that predominant, aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought and initial thought arise. One savors and delights in the aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought, making them predominant; making that predominant, aggregates with initial thought and sustained thought and initial thought arise. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates and for initial thought by way of dominance condition. (6)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – savitakkasavicārā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (7)

A state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought, for a state without initial thought but with only sustained thought, and for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant state with initial thought and sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates, for initial thought, and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dominance condition. (7)

75. Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo [V 2.0055] – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – avitakkavicāramattā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā [M 2.0047] vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – avitakkavicāramattā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

75. A state with only sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of dominance condition—as object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: Having emerged from a jhāna with only sustained thought, having emerged from a path, having emerged from a fruition, one reflects on the fruition, making it dominant; making that dominant, initial thought arises. One savors and delights in the aggregates with only sustained thought and in initial thought, making them dominant; making that dominant, initial thought arises. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant factor with only sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of dominance condition.

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena [T 2.0063] paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – avitakkavicāramattā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

A state with only sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Having emerged from a jhāna with only sustained thought, having emerged from a path, having emerged from a fruition, one reflects on the fruition, making it dominant; making that dominant, aggregates with initial and sustained thought arise. One savors and delights in the aggregates with only sustained thought and in initial thought, making them dominant; making that dominant, lust arises, wrong view arises.

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – avitakkavicāramattā adhipati vicārassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with only sustained thought is a condition for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant factor with only sustained thought is a condition for sustained thought and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition.

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – avitakkavicāramattā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state with only sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought and for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant factor with only sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates, for sustained thought, and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition.

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – avitakkavicāramattā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (5)

A state with only sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought and for a state with only sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Having emerged from a jhāna with only sustained thought, having emerged from a path, having emerged from a fruition, one reflects on the fruition, making it dominant; making that dominant, aggregates with initial and sustained thought and initial thought arise. One savors and delights in the aggregates with only sustained thought and in initial thought, making them dominant; making that dominant, aggregates with initial and sustained thought and initial thought arise.

76. Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena [T 2.0064][V 2.0056] paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – nibbānaṃ avitakkaavicārassa maggassa phalassa vicārassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – avitakkaavicārā adhipati [M 2.0048] sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

76. A state without initial thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition—as object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: Nibbāna is a condition by way of dominance condition for the path without initial and sustained thought, for the fruition, and for sustained thought. Co-nascence dominance: A dominant factor without initial thought and without sustained thought is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition.

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā avitakkaavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti, ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa vodānassa savitakkasavicārassa maggassa phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

A state without initial thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial thought and sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without initial and sustained thought, having emerged from paths, having emerged from fruitions, reflect on the fruition, making it dominant; making that dominant, aggregates with initial and sustained thought arise. Noble ones reflect on Nibbāna, making it dominant; Nibbāna is a condition by way of dominance condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path with initial and sustained thought, and for the fruition. One savors and delights in the eye, making it dominant; making that dominant, lust arises, wrong view arises. The ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… forms… sounds… odors… tastes… tangibles… the physical basis… One savors and delights in the aggregates without initial and sustained thought and in sustained thought, making them dominant; making that dominant, lust arises, wrong view arises.

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā avitakkaavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā, maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati, ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti[T 2.0065]; nibbānaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa phalassa vitakkassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. (3)

A state without initial thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without initial and sustained thought, having emerged from paths, having emerged from fruitions, reflect on the fruition, making it dominant; making that dominant, initial thought arises. Noble ones reflect on Nibbāna, making it dominant; Nibbāna is a condition by way of dominance condition for the path with only sustained thought, for the fruition, and for initial thought. The eye… the physical basis… One savors and delights in the aggregates without initial and sustained thought and in sustained thought, making them dominant; making that dominant, initial thought arises.

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – nibbānaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa phalassa vicārassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state without initial thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought and for a state without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Nibbāna is a condition by way of dominance condition for the path with only sustained thought, for the fruition, and for sustained thought.

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā avitakkaavicārā jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā[V 2.0057], maggā vuṭṭhahitvā, phalā vuṭṭhahitvā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti, ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti; nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa vitakkassa ca vodānassa vitakkassa ca savitakkasavicārassa maggassa [M 2.0049] vitakkassa ca savitakkasavicārassa phalassa vitakkassa ca adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… vatthuṃ… avitakkaavicāre khandhe ca vicārañca garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (5)

A state without applied thought and without sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought, and for a state with only sustained thought, by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Noble ones, having emerged from jhānas without applied thought and without sustained thought, having emerged from paths, having emerged from fruitions, review the fruition, esteeming it highly; esteeming it highly, the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought and applied thought arise. Noble ones review Nibbāna, esteeming it highly; Nibbāna is a predominance condition for the applied thought of change-of-lineage, for the applied thought of purification, for the applied thought of the path with applied thought and sustained thought, and for the applied thought of the fruition with applied thought and sustained thought. Having esteemed the eye highly…and so on…the base… Having esteemed highly the aggregates without applied thought and without sustained thought, and sustained thought, one savors and delights in them; esteeming them highly, the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (5)

77. Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – avitakkavicāramatte [T 2.0066] khandhe ca vicārañca garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

77. A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied thought and without sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Having esteemed highly the aggregates with only sustained thought, and sustained thought, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought arise. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. (2)

A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied thought and without sustained thought are a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Having esteemed highly the aggregates with only sustained thought, and sustained thought, applied thought arises. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – avitakkavicāramatte khandhe ca vicārañca garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. (3)

A state with only sustained thought and a state without applied thought and without sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought, and for a state with only sustained thought, by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Having esteemed highly the aggregates with only sustained thought, and sustained thought, the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (3)

78. Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

78. A state with applied thought and sustained thought and a state with only sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Having esteemed highly the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought, aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought arise. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā vitakko uppajjati. (2)

A state with applied thought and sustained thought and a state with only sustained thought are a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Having esteemed highly the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought, applied thought arises. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro [V 2.0058] ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – savitakkasavicāre khandhe ca vitakkañca garuṃ katvā savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti[T 2.0067]. (3)

A state with applied thought and sustained thought and a state with only sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought, and for a state with only sustained thought, by way of the predominance condition. Object predominance: Having esteemed highly the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought, and applied thought, the aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought and applied thought arise. (3)

Anantarapaccayo

The Contiguity Condition

79. Savitakkasavicāro [M 2.0050] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkasavicārā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu savitakkasavicārassa maggassa… vodānaṃ savitakkasavicārassa maggassa… savitakkasavicāro maggo savitakkasavicārassa phalassa… savitakkasavicāraṃ phalaṃ savitakkasavicārassa phalassa… anulomaṃ savitakkasavicārāya phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

79. A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the contiguity condition—preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for succeeding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the contiguity condition. Conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage… Conformity is a condition for purification… Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path with applied thought and sustained thought… Purification is a condition for the path with applied thought and sustained thought… The path with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the fruition with applied thought and sustained thought… The fruition with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the fruition with applied thought and sustained thought… Conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition with applied thought and sustained thought by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkasavicārā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa vitakkassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Savitakkasavicāraṃ cuticittaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa upapatticittassa…pe… savitakkasavicārā khandhā avitakkavicāramattassa vuṭṭhānassa vitakkassa ca…pe… avitakkavicāramattassa jhānassa parikammaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa jhānassa… gotrabhu avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa… vodānaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa… anulomaṃ avitakkavicāramattāya phalasamāpattiyā vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with only sustained thought by way of the contiguity condition—preceding aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for succeeding applied thought by way of the contiguity condition. The death consciousness with applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the rebirth consciousness with only sustained thought… The aggregates with applied thought and sustained thought are a condition for the emergence with only sustained thought, and for applied thought… The preliminary work for the jhāna with only sustained thought is a condition for the jhāna with only sustained thought… Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path with only sustained thought… Purification is a condition for the path with only sustained thought… Conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition with only sustained thought, and for applied thought, by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāraṃ cuticittaṃ avitakkaavicārassa upapatticittassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo – āvajjanā pañcannaṃ viññāṇānaṃ anantarapaccayena [T 2.0068] paccayo. Savitakkasavicārā khandhā avitakkaavicārassa vuṭṭhānassa vicārassa ca…pe… dutiyassa jhānassa parikammaṃ dutiye jhāne vicārassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Tatiyassa jhānassa parikammaṃ [V 2.0059] …pe… catutthassa jhānassa parikammaṃ…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanassa parikammaṃ…pe… viññāṇañcāyatanassa parikammaṃ…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ…pe… dibbassa cakkhussa parikammaṃ…pe… dibbāya sotadhātuyā parikammaṃ…pe… iddhividhañāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… cetopariyañāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇassa parikammaṃ…pe… gotrabhu avitakkaavicārassa maggassa vicārassa ca… vodānaṃ avitakkaavicārassa maggassa [M 2.0051] vicārassa ca… anulomaṃ avitakkaavicārāya phalasamāpattiyā vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of contiguity condition—the death consciousness with initial application and sustained application is a condition for the rebirth consciousness without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition; adverting is a condition for the five sense-consciousnesses by way of contiguity condition. The aggregates with initial application and sustained application are a condition for emergence without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application… The preliminary work for the second jhāna is a condition for sustained application in the second jhāna by way of contiguity condition. The preliminary work for the third jhāna… the preliminary work for the fourth jhāna… the preliminary work for the base of infinite space… the preliminary work for the base of infinite consciousness… the preliminary work for the base of nothingness… the preliminary work for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… the preliminary work for the divine eye… the preliminary work for the divine ear element… the preliminary work for the knowledge of psychic powers… the preliminary work for the knowledge of others’ minds… the preliminary work for the knowledge of past lives… the preliminary work for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings… the preliminary work for the knowledge of the future… Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application… Purification is a condition for the path without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application… Conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. (3)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāraṃ cuticittaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa upapatticittassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Savitakkasavicārā khandhā avitakkavicāramattassa vuṭṭhānassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattassa jhānassa parikammaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa jhānassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Gotrabhu avitakkavicāramattassa [T 2.0069] maggassa vicārassa ca… vodānaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa maggassa vicārassa ca… anulomaṃ avitakkavicāramattāya phalasamāpattiyā vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state with initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of contiguity condition—the death consciousness with initial application and sustained application is a condition for the rebirth consciousness that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. The aggregates with initial application and sustained application are a condition for the emergence of a state that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. The preliminary work for the jhāna that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for the jhāna that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for sustained application… Purification is a condition for the path that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for sustained application… Conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition that is merely with sustained application without initial application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. (4)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā savitakkasavicārā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa vitakkassa ca… anulomaṃ vodānassa vitakkassa ca… gotrabhu savitakkasavicārassa maggassa vitakkassa ca… vodānaṃ savitakkasavicārassa maggassa vitakkassa ca… savitakkasavicāro maggo savitakkasavicārassa phalassa vitakkassa ca… savitakkasavicāraṃ phalaṃ savitakkasavicārassa phalassa vitakkassa ca… anulomaṃ savitakkasavicārāya phalasamāpattiyā vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state with initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state with initial application and sustained application and for a state that is merely with sustained application without initial application by way of contiguity condition—earlier aggregates with initial application and sustained application are a condition for later aggregates with initial application and sustained application and for initial application by way of contiguity condition. Conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage and for initial application… Conformity is a condition for purification and for initial application… Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path with initial application and sustained application and for initial application… Purification is a condition for the path with initial application and sustained application and for initial application… The path with initial application and sustained application is a condition for the fruition with initial application and sustained application and for initial application… The fruition with initial application and sustained application is a condition for the fruition with initial application and sustained application and for initial application… Conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition with initial application and sustained application and for initial application by way of contiguity condition. (5)

80. Avitakkavicāramatto [V 2.0060] dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vitakko pacchimassa pacchimassa vitakkassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā avitakkavicāramattā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramatto maggo avitakkavicāramattassa phalassa… avitakkavicāramattaṃ phalaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa phalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

80. A state that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for a state that is merely with sustained application without initial application by way of contiguity condition—earlier initial application is a condition for later initial application by way of contiguity condition. Earlier aggregates that are merely with sustained application without initial application are a condition for later aggregates that are merely with sustained application without initial application by way of contiguity condition. The path that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for the fruition that is merely with sustained application without initial application… The fruition that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for the fruition that is merely with sustained application without initial application by way of contiguity condition. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto [T 2.0070][M 2.0052] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vitakko pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattaṃ cuticittaṃ savitakkasavicārassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattā khandhā savitakkasavicārassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for a state with initial application and sustained application by way of contiguity condition—earlier initial application is a condition for later aggregates with initial application and sustained application by way of contiguity condition. The death consciousness that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for the rebirth consciousness with initial application and sustained application by way of contiguity condition. The life-continuum that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for adverting by way of contiguity condition. The aggregates that are merely with sustained application without initial application are a condition for the emergence of a state with initial application and sustained application by way of contiguity condition. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā avitakkavicāramattā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa vicārassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattaṃ cuticittaṃ vitakko ca avitakkaavicārassa upapatticittassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattā khandhā vitakko ca avitakkaavicārassa vuṭṭhānassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is merely with sustained application without initial application is a condition for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of contiguity condition—earlier aggregates that are merely with sustained application without initial application are a condition for the later sustained application by way of contiguity condition. The death consciousness that is merely with sustained application without initial application and initial application are a condition for the rebirth consciousness without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. The aggregates that are merely with sustained application without initial application and initial application are a condition for the emergence of a state without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application by way of contiguity condition. (3)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā avitakkavicāramattā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramatto maggo avitakkavicāramattassa phalassa vicārassa ca… avitakkavicāramattaṃ phalaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa phalassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena [T 2.0071] paccayo. (4)

A state with sustained application only is a condition for a state with sustained application only and for a state without initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition—earlier aggregates with sustained application only are a condition for later aggregates with sustained application only and for sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. The path with sustained application only is a condition for the fruition with sustained application only and for sustained application… The fruition with sustained application only is a condition for the fruition with sustained application only and for sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. (4)

Avitakkavicāramatto [V 2.0061] dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vitakko pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattaṃ cuticittaṃ savitakkasavicārassa upapatticittassa vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkavicāramattā khandhā savitakkasavicārassa vuṭṭhānassa vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state with sustained application only is a condition for a state with initial application and sustained application and for a state with sustained application only by way of the contiguity condition—earlier initial application is a condition for later aggregates with initial application and sustained application and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. The death consciousness with sustained application only is a condition for the rebirth consciousness with initial application and sustained application and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. The life-continuum with sustained application only is a condition for adverting and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. The aggregates with sustained application only are a condition for the emergence with initial application and sustained application and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. (5)

81. Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicāro pacchimassa pacchimassa vicārassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Purimā purimā avitakkaavicārā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ [M 2.0053] avitakkaavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicāro maggo avitakkaavicārassa phalassa… avitakkaavicāraṃ phalaṃ avitakkaavicārassa phalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ avitakkaavicārāya phalasamāpattiyā vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

81. A state without initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state without initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition—the preceding sustained application is a condition for the subsequent sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. The preceding aggregates without initial application and sustained application are a condition for the subsequent aggregates without initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. The path without initial application and sustained application is a condition for the fruit without initial application and sustained application… the fruit without initial application and sustained application is a condition for the fruit without initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the fruition-attainment without initial application and sustained application and for sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – avitakkaavicāraṃ cuticittaṃ vicāro ca savitakkasavicārassa [T 2.0072] upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicāraṃ bhavaṅgaṃ vicāro ca āvajjanāya anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicārā khandhā vicāro ca savitakkasavicārassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ savitakkasavicārāya phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state without initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state with initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition—the death consciousness without initial application and sustained application and sustained application are conditions for the rebirth consciousness with initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. The life-continuum without initial application and sustained application and sustained application are conditions for adverting by way of the contiguity condition. The aggregates without initial application and sustained application and sustained application are conditions for the emergence with initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the fruition-attainment with initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicāro pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicāraṃ cuticittaṃ vicāro ca avitakkavicāramattassa upapatticittassa vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicārā khandhā vicāro ca avitakkavicāramattassa vuṭṭhānassa vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Nirodhā [V 2.0062] vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ avitakkavicāramattāya phalasamāpattiyā vitakkassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state without initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state with sustained application only by way of the contiguity condition—the preceding sustained application is a condition for the subsequent aggregates with sustained application only by way of the contiguity condition. The death consciousness without initial application and sustained application and sustained application are conditions for the rebirth consciousness with sustained application only and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. The aggregates without initial application and sustained application and sustained application are conditions for the emergence with sustained application only and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the fruition-attainment with sustained application only and for initial application by way of the contiguity condition. (3)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicāro pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicāraṃ cuticittaṃ avitakkavicāramattassa upapatticittassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Avitakkaavicārā khandhā avitakkavicāramattassa vuṭṭhānassa vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. Nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa [T 2.0073] nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ avitakkavicāramattāya phalasamāpattiyā vicārassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state without initial application and sustained application is a condition for both a state with sustained application only and a state without initial application and sustained application by way of the contiguity condition—the preceding sustained application is a condition for the subsequent aggregates with sustained application only and for sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. The death consciousness without initial application and sustained application is a condition for the rebirth consciousness with sustained application only and for sustained application by way of the contiguity condition. The aggregates without initial application and sustained application are conditions for the emergence with sustained application only and for sustained application by way of the contiguity condition.
