(Savitakkasavicāramūlakā satta pañhā iminā kāraṇena vibhajitabbā.)

For this reason, the seven questions rooted in states with initial and sustained application should be analyzed.

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A state without initial application, with sustained application only, is a condition for a state without initial application, with sustained application only, by way of the faculty condition. Faculties without initial application, with sustained application only, are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the faculty condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto [V 2.0100] dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena [T 2.0125] paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā indriyā vicārassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state without initial application, with sustained application only, is a condition for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of the faculty condition. Faculties without initial application, with sustained application only, are a condition for sustained application and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the faculty condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A state without initial application, with sustained application only, is a condition for a state without initial application, with sustained application only, and for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of the faculty condition. Faculties without initial application, with sustained application only, are a condition for the associated aggregates, for sustained application, and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the faculty condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on. (3)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – avitakkaavicārā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa [M 2.0089] …pe… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa indriyapaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state without initial application and without sustained application is a condition for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of the faculty condition. Faculties without initial application and without sustained application are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the faculty condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…and so on… The eye faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness…and so on… The body faculty is a condition for body-consciousness by way of the faculty condition. The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-originated material phenomena by way of the faculty condition. (1)

Jhānapaccayo

Jhāna Condition

121. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (7)

121. A state with initial and sustained application is a condition for a state with initial and sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. Jhāna factors with initial and sustained application are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (7)

(Savitakkasavicāramūlakā satta pañhā iminā kāraṇena vibhajitabbā.)

For this reason, the seven questions rooted in states with initial and sustained application should be analyzed.

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (5)

A state with only sustained application is a condition for a state with only sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. Jhāna factors with only sustained application are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (5)

(Avitakkavicāramattamūlakā [T 2.0126] pañca pañhā iminā kāraṇena vibhajitabbā.)

For this reason, the five questions rooted in states with only sustained application should be analyzed.

Avitakkaavicāro [V 2.0101] dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – avitakkaavicārāni jhānaṅgāni sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Vicāro cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vicāro kaṭattārūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Vicāro vatthussa jhānapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state without initial and sustained application is a condition for a state without initial and sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. Jhāna factors without initial and sustained application are a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. Sustained application is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained application is a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. Sustained application is a condition for the base by way of the jhāna condition. (1)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state without initial and sustained application is a condition for a state with only sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. Sustained application is a condition for the aggregates with only sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained application is a condition for the aggregates with only sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. (2)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state without initial and sustained application is a condition for a state with only sustained application and for a state without initial and sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. Sustained application is a condition for the aggregates with only sustained application and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained application is a condition for the aggregates with only sustained application and for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. (3)

A state with only sustained application and a state without initial and sustained application are conditions for a state with only sustained application and for a state without initial and sustained application by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, jhāna factors with only sustained application and sustained application are conditions for the associated aggregates and kamma-produced material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. Jhāna factors with initial and sustained application and initial application are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the jhāna condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārāni [T 2.0128] jhānaṅgāni vitakko ca sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ jhānapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

The path factors without initial and sustained application are conditions for the associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of the path condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking... (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa maggapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārāni maggaṅgāni vitakko ca sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A state with initial and sustained application and a state with only sustained application are conditions for a state with initial and sustained application by way of the path condition. The path factors with initial and sustained application and initial application are conditions for the associated aggregates by way of the path condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking... (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa maggapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārāni maggaṅgāni [T 2.0129] vitakko ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state with applied and sustained thought and a state with mere sustained thought are conditions for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of path condition. The path factors with applied and sustained thought and applied thought are conditions for mind-originated material phenomena by way of path condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa maggapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārāni maggaṅgāni vitakko ca sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ maggapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A state with applied and sustained thought and a state with mere sustained thought are conditions for a state with applied and sustained thought and for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of path condition. The path factors with applied and sustained thought and applied thought are conditions for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of path condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (3)

Sampayuttapaccayo

Association Condition

124. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ [M 2.0092] sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

124. A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate with applied and sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates are conditions for the other two aggregates…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārā khandhā vitakkassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of association condition. The aggregates with applied and sustained thought are conditions for applied thought by way of association condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca [V 2.0104] sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought and for a state with mere sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate with applied and sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates and for applied thought by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates are conditions for the other two aggregates and for applied thought…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (3)

125. Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ [T 2.0130] khandhānaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

125. A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate with mere sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates are conditions for the other two aggregates…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – vitakko savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. Applied thought is a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā vicārassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. The aggregates with mere sustained thought are conditions for sustained thought by way of association condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (3)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (4)

A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state with mere sustained thought and for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate with mere sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates and for sustained thought by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates are conditions for the other two aggregates and for sustained thought…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (4)

126. Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – avitakkaavicāro eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

126. A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate without applied and sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates are conditions for the other two aggregates…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (1)

Avitakkaavicāro [M 2.0093] dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state without applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of association condition. Sustained thought is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought by way of association condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto [V 2.0105] ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa [T 2.0131] dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vicāro ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vicāro ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A state with mere sustained thought and a state without applied and sustained thought are conditions for a state with mere sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate with mere sustained thought and sustained thought are conditions for the other three aggregates by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates and sustained thought are conditions for the other two aggregates…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa sampayuttapaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho ca vitakko ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ sampayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vitakko ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

A state with applied and sustained thought and a state with mere sustained thought are conditions for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of association condition. One aggregate with applied and sustained thought and applied thought are conditions for the other three aggregates by way of association condition…etc. Two aggregates and applied thought are conditions for the other two aggregates…etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking…etc. (1)

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

127. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

127. A state with applied and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of dissociation condition—co-arising and post-arising. Co-arising: The aggregates with applied and sustained thought are conditions for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought are conditions for kamma-born materiality by way of dissociation condition. Post-arising: The aggregates with applied and sustained thought are conditions for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, vitakko cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramattā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vitakko kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vitakko ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of dissociation condition—co-arising and post-arising. Co-arising: The aggregates with mere sustained thought are conditions for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition; applied thought is a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates with mere sustained thought are conditions for kamma-born materiality by way of dissociation condition; applied thought is a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of dissociation condition. Post-arising: The aggregates with mere sustained thought and applied thought are conditions for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

128. Avitakkaavicāro [T 2.0132] dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā [M 2.0094] – avitakkaavicārā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ [V 2.0106] rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vicāro cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkaavicārā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vicāro kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; vicāro vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo; vatthu vicārassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, vatthu avitakkaavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkaavicārā khandhā ca vicāro ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

128. A state without initial application and without sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for a state without initial application and without sustained application—co-arising, pre-arising, and post-arising. Co-arising: The aggregates without initial application and without sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for mind-originated materiality; sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for mind-originated materiality. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates without initial application and without sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for kamma-born materiality; sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for kamma-born materiality; the aggregates are a condition by way of dissociation for the physical base, and the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates; sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for the physical base, and the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for sustained application. Pre-arising: The eye-base is a condition by way of dissociation for eye-consciousness… the body-base is a condition by way of dissociation for body-consciousness; the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates without initial application and without sustained application and for sustained application. Post-arising: The aggregates without initial application and without sustained application and sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for this pre-arisen body. (1)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state without initial application and without sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application—co-arising and pre-arising. Co-arising: At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application. Pre-arising: The physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application. (2)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena [T 2.0133] paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state without initial application and without sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for a state with sustained application only, without initial application—co-arising and pre-arising. Co-arising: At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and for initial application. Pre-arising: The physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and for initial application. (3)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state without initial application and without sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for a state with sustained application only, without initial application, and for a state without initial application and without sustained application—co-arising and pre-arising. Co-arising: At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and for sustained application. Pre-arising: The physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and for sustained application. (4)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ [V 2.0107] khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state without initial application and without sustained application is a condition by way of dissociation for a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application and for a state with sustained application only, without initial application—co-arising and pre-arising. Co-arising: At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application and for initial application. Pre-arising: The physical base is a condition by way of dissociation for the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application and for initial application. (5)

129. Avitakkavicāramatto [M 2.0095] ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro [T 2.0134] ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

129. A state with sustained application only, without initial application, and a state without initial application and without sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for a state without initial application and without sustained application—co-arising and post-arising. Co-arising: The aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for mind-originated materiality. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for kamma-born materiality. Post-arising: The aggregates with sustained application only, without initial application, and sustained application are a condition by way of dissociation for this pre-arisen body. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application and a state with sustained application only, without initial application, are a condition by way of dissociation for a state without initial application and without sustained application—co-arising and post-arising. Co-arising: The aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application and initial application are a condition by way of dissociation for mind-originated materiality. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application and initial application are a condition by way of dissociation for kamma-born materiality. Post-arising: The aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application and initial application are a condition by way of dissociation for this pre-arisen body. (1)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

130. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

130. A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state accompanied by initial application and sustained application by way of presence condition—one aggregate accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for the other three aggregates by way of presence condition… two aggregates are a condition for the other two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (1)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicārā khandhā vitakkassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state with sustained application only, without initial application, by way of presence condition—the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition for initial application by way of presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

Savitakkasavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ[V 2.0108], pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state accompanied by initial application and sustained application is a condition for a state without initial application and without sustained application by way of presence condition—co-arising, post-arising. Co-arising: The aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of presence condition. Post-arising: The aggregates accompanied by initial application and sustained application are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of presence condition. (3)

(Savitakkasavicāramūlake avasesā [T 2.0135] pañhā sahajātapaccayasadisā.)

The remaining questions rooted in states accompanied by initial application and sustained application are similar to those for the co-arising condition.

131. Avitakkavicāramatto [M 2.0096] dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

131. A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition—one aggregate with mere sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates by way of the presence condition… two aggregates are conditions for the other two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – vitakko savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (2)

A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition—applied thought is a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā vicārassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Vitakko cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramattā khandhā vicārassa kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; vitakko kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vitakko ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with mere sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought and without sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, post-nascently. Co-nascently, the aggregates with mere sustained thought are a condition for sustained thought and for mind-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. Applied thought is a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates with mere sustained thought are a condition for sustained thought and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition; applied thought is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. Post-nascently, the aggregates with mere sustained thought and applied thought are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the presence condition. (3)

(Avitakkavicāramattamūlakā pañca pañhā. Avasesā sahajātapaccayasadisā.)

Five questions are rooted in mere sustained thought. The remaining are similar to the co-nascent condition.

132. Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – avitakkaavicāro eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā [T 2.0136] dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… vicāro cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe [V 2.0109] avitakkaavicāro eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… khandhā vatthussa atthipaccayena paccayo, vatthu khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; vicāro vatthussa atthipaccayena paccayo, vatthu vicārassa atthipaccayena paccayo; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… mahābhūtā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ upādārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo; bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ…pe… mahābhūtā kaṭattārūpānaṃ upādārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā [M 2.0097] saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo, cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Vatthu avitakkaavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkaavicārā khandhā ca vicāro ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

132. A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently, post-nascently, as nutriment, as faculty. Co-nascently, one aggregate without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates and for mind-produced materiality by way of the presence condition… two aggregates are a condition for the other two aggregates… sustained thought is a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for the other three aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition… the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of the presence condition, the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates by way of the presence condition; sustained thought is a condition for the physical basis by way of the presence condition, the physical basis is a condition for sustained thought by way of the presence condition; one great element is a condition for the other three great elements by way of the presence condition… the great elements are a condition for mind-produced materiality, kamma-produced materiality, and derived materiality by way of the presence condition; externally… nutriment-produced… temperature-produced… for non-percipient beings, one great element is a condition for the other three great elements… the great elements are a condition for kamma-produced materiality and derived materiality by way of the presence condition. Pre-nascently, one sees forms with the divine eye, hears sounds with the divine ear element; the visible form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of the presence condition; the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of the presence condition. The physical basis is a condition for the aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought and for sustained thought by way of the presence condition. Post-nascently, the aggregates without applied thought and sustained thought and sustained thought are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the presence condition. Physical nutriment is a condition for this body by way of the presence condition. The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. (1)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu [T 2.0137] savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently, at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition. Pre-nascently, one sees the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self, enjoys it, and delights in it. Based on that, lust arises… sorrow arises. The ear… nose… tongue… body… forms… sounds… smells… tastes… touches… one sees the physical basis as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self… sorrow arises. The physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition. (2)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha [V 2.0110] vitakko uppajjati. Sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha vitakko uppajjati. Vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently, sustained thought is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained thought is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought and for applied thought by way of the presence condition. Pre-nascently, one sees the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self, enjoys it, and delights in it. Based on that, applied thought arises. The ear… nose… tongue… body… forms… sounds… smells… tastes… touches… one sees the physical basis as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self, enjoys it, and delights in it. Based on that, applied thought arises. The physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought and for applied thought by way of the presence condition. (3)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca [T 2.0138] rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vicāro avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ [M 2.0098] kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu avitakkavicāramattānaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for both a state with mere sustained thought and a state without applied thought and sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently, sustained thought is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought and for mind-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, sustained thought is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought and for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought and for sustained thought by way of the presence condition. Pre-nascently, the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with mere sustained thought and for sustained thought by way of the presence condition. (4)

Avitakkaavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātaṃ – paṭisandhikkhaṇe vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca uppajjanti. Vatthu savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state without applied thought and sustained thought is a condition for both a state with applied and sustained thought and a state with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently, at the moment of rebirth-linking, the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and for applied thought by way of the presence condition. Pre-nascently, one discerns the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self, enjoys and delights in it. Taking that as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. The ear… nose… tongue… body…pe… the physical basis is discerned as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self, one enjoys and delights in it. Taking that as object, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and applied thought arise. The physical basis is a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and for applied thought by way of the presence condition. (5)

133. Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vatthu ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicāro [T 2.0139] eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vatthu ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

133. States with applied and sustained thought and states without applied and sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently: one aggregate with applied and sustained thought and the physical basis are a condition for the three aggregates by way of the presence condition… etc… two aggregates and the physical basis are a condition for the two aggregates by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate with applied and sustained thought and the physical basis are a condition for the three aggregates by way of the presence condition… etc… two aggregates and the physical basis are a condition for the two aggregates by way of the presence condition. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro [V 2.0111] ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vatthu ca vitakkassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vatthu ca vitakkassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

States with applied and sustained thought and states without applied and sustained thought are a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently: the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and the physical basis are a condition for applied thought by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and the physical basis are a condition for applied thought by way of the presence condition. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā [M 2.0099] – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

States with applied and sustained thought and states without applied and sustained thought are a condition for a state without applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, post-nascently, as nutriment, and as faculty. Co-nascently: the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and the great elements are a condition for mind-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and the great elements are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. Post-nascently: the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and physical nutriment are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of the presence condition. Post-nascently: the aggregates with applied and sustained thought and the life faculty of materiality are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of the presence condition. (3)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa ca avitakkavicāramattassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho [T 2.0140] ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vatthu ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ vitakkassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (4)

States with applied and sustained thought and states without applied and sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought and a state with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently: one aggregate with applied and sustained thought and the physical basis is a condition for the three aggregates and for applied thought by way of the presence condition… etc… two aggregates and the physical basis are a condition for the two aggregates and for applied thought by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… etc. (4)

134. Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vitakko ca vatthu ca savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakko ca vatthu ca savitakkasavicārānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

134. States with mere sustained thought and states without applied and sustained thought are a condition for a state with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently: applied thought and the physical basis are a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, applied thought and the physical basis are a condition for the aggregates with applied and sustained thought by way of the presence condition. (1)

Avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vicāro ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vicāro ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ… avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vatthu ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vicāro ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena [V 2.0112] paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vicāro ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā ca vatthu ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

States with mere sustained thought and states without applied and sustained thought are a condition for a state with mere sustained thought by way of the presence condition: co-nascently, pre-nascently. Co-nascently: one aggregate with mere sustained thought and sustained thought are a condition for the three aggregates by way of the presence condition… etc… two aggregates and sustained thought are a condition for the two aggregates by way of the presence condition; one aggregate with mere sustained thought and the physical basis is a condition for the three aggregates by way of the presence condition… etc… two aggregates and the physical basis are a condition for the two aggregates by way of the presence condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate with mere sustained thought and sustained thought is a condition for the three aggregates by way of the presence condition… etc… two aggregates and sustained thought are a condition for the two aggregates by way of the presence condition… etc. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one aggregate with mere sustained thought and the physical basis is a condition for the three aggregates… etc… two aggregates and the physical basis are a condition for the two aggregates by way of the presence condition. (2)

Avitakkavicāramatto [T 2.0141] ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā [M 2.0100] – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajāto – vitakko ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vatthu ca vicārassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe vitakko ca mahābhūtā ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vatthu ca vicārassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vicāro ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vitakko ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – avitakkavicāramattā khandhā ca vitakko ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

States merely with sustained thought and states without initial thought and without sustained thought are a condition for states without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of presence—as co-arising, as pre-arising, as post-arising, as nutriment, and as faculty. Co-arising: the aggregates merely with sustained thought and sustained thought are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence. Co-arising: the aggregates merely with sustained thought and the great elements are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence. Co-arising: initial thought and the great elements are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence. Co-arising: the aggregates merely with sustained thought and the basis are a condition for sustained thought by way of presence. At the moment of relinking, the aggregates merely with sustained thought and sustained thought are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence. At the moment of relinking, the aggregates merely with sustained thought and the great elements are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence. At the moment of relinking, initial thought and the great elements are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence. At the moment of relinking, the aggregates merely with sustained thought and the basis are a condition for sustained thought by way of presence. Post-arising: the aggregates merely with sustained thought and sustained thought are a condition for this pre-arising body by way of presence. Post-arising: the aggregates merely with sustained thought, initial thought, and physical nutriment are a condition for this pre-arising body by way of presence. Post-arising: the aggregates merely with sustained thought, initial thought, and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence. (3)

Avitakkavicāramatto [T 2.0142] ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkavicāramattassa ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vicāro ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vicāro ca…pe… avitakkavicāramatto eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ vicārassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vatthu ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (4)

States merely with sustained thought and states without initial thought and without sustained thought are a condition for states merely with sustained thought and for states without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of presence—as co-arising and as pre-arising. Co-arising: one aggregate merely with sustained thought and sustained thought are a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence… etc… two aggregates and sustained thought… etc… one aggregate merely with sustained thought and the basis are a condition for the three aggregates and for sustained thought by way of presence… etc… two aggregates and the basis… etc… at the moment of relinking… etc. (4)

135. Savitakkasavicāro [V 2.0113] ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho ca vitakko ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vitakko ca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

135. States with initial and sustained thought and states merely with sustained thought are a condition for states with initial and sustained thought by way of presence—one aggregate with initial and sustained thought and initial thought are a condition for the three aggregates by way of presence… etc… two aggregates and initial thought… etc… at the moment of relinking… etc. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko [M 2.0101] ca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

States with initial and sustained thought and states merely with sustained thought are a condition for states without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of presence—as co-arising and as post-arising. Co-arising: the aggregates with initial and sustained thought and initial thought are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence. At the moment of relinking, the aggregates with initial and sustained thought and initial thought are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence. Post-arising: the aggregates with initial and sustained thought and initial thought are a condition for this pre-arising body by way of presence. (2)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa [T 2.0143] ca avitakkaavicārassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho ca vitakko ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca vitakko ca dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (3)

States with initial and sustained thought and states merely with sustained thought are a condition for states with initial and sustained thought and for states without initial thought and without sustained thought by way of presence—one aggregate with initial and sustained thought and initial thought are a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence… etc… two aggregates and initial thought are a condition for the two aggregates… etc… at the moment of relinking… etc. (3)

136. Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – savitakkasavicāro eko khandho ca vitakko ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

136. States with initial and sustained thought, states merely with sustained thought, and states without initial thought and without sustained thought are a condition for states with initial and sustained thought by way of presence—as co-arising and as pre-arising. Co-arising: one aggregate with initial and sustained thought, initial thought, and the basis are a condition for the three aggregates by way of presence… etc… at the moment of relinking… etc. (1)

Savitakkasavicāro ca avitakkavicāramatto ca avitakkaavicāro ca dhammā avitakkaavicārassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa [V 2.0114] atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – savitakkasavicārā khandhā ca vitakko ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

States with initial and sustained thought, states merely with sustained thought, and states without initial and sustained thought are a condition for states without initial and sustained thought by way of presence—as co-arising, as post-arising, as nutriment, and as faculty. Co-arising: the aggregates with initial and sustained thought, initial thought, and the great elements are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence. At the moment of relinking… etc. Post-arising: the aggregates with initial and sustained thought, initial thought, and physical nutriment are a condition for this pre-arising body by way of presence. Post-arising: the aggregates with initial and sustained thought, initial thought, and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence. (2)

Natthivigatāvigatapaccayā

Absence, Disappearance, and Non-Disappearance Conditions

137. Savitakkasavicāro dhammo savitakkasavicārassa dhammassa natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo.

137. A state with initial and sustained thought is a condition for a state with initial and sustained thought by way of the absence condition… by way of the disappearance condition.

(Natthipaccayañca [T 2.0144] vigatapaccayañca anantarasadisaṃ, avigataṃ atthisadisaṃ.)

(The absence condition and the disappearance condition are similar to the contiguity condition; the non-disappearance condition is similar to the presence condition.)

Hetuyā [M 2.0102] ekādasa, ārammaṇe ekavīsa, adhipatiyā tevīsa, anantare pañcavīsa, samanantare pañcavīsa, sahajāte tiṃsa, aññamaññe aṭṭhavīsa, nissaye tiṃsa, upanissaye pañcavīsa, purejāte pañca, pacchājāte pañca, āsevane ekavīsa, kamme ekādasa, vipāke ekavīsa, āhāre ekādasa, indriye ekādasa, jhāne ekavīsa, magge soḷasa, sampayutte ekādasa, vippayutte nava, atthiyā tiṃsa, natthiyā pañcavīsa, vigate pañcavīsa, avigate tiṃsa.

By way of root condition, eleven; by way of object condition, twenty-one; by way of dominance condition, twenty-three; by way of contiguity condition, twenty-five; by way of immediate contiguity condition, twenty-five; by way of co-nascence condition, thirty; by way of mutuality condition, twenty-eight; by way of support condition, thirty; by way of decisive support condition, twenty-five; by way of pre-nascence condition, five; by way of post-nascence condition, five; by way of repetition condition, twenty-one; by way of kamma condition, eleven; by way of result condition, twenty-one; by way of nutriment condition, eleven; by way of faculty condition, eleven; by way of jhāna condition, twenty-one; by way of path condition, sixteen; by way of association condition, eleven; by way of dissociation condition, nine; by way of presence condition, thirty; by way of absence condition, twenty-five; by way of disappearance condition, twenty-five; by way of non-disappearance condition, thirty.

(Ghaṭanā kusalattikasadisāyeva. Pañhāvāragaṇanaṃ evaṃ asammohantena gaṇetabbaṃ.)

The arrangement is similar to the wholesome triad. The counting of the question section should be done thus, without confusion.

The Non-Root Dyad.

147. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe ekavīsa, adhipatiyā tevīsa, anantare pañcavīsa, samanantare pañcavīsa, sahajāte tiṃsa, aññamaññe aṭṭhavīsa, nissaye tiṃsa, upanissaye pañcavīsa, purejāte pañca, pacchājāte pañca, āsevane ekavīsa, kamme ekādasa, vipāke ekavīsa, āhāre ekādasa, indriye ekādasa, jhāne ekavīsa, magge soḷasa, sampayutte ekādasa, vippayutte nava, atthiyā tiṃsa, natthiyā pañcavīsa, vigate pañcavīsa, avigate tiṃsa.

147. By non-root condition, in the object mode, twenty-one; in the predominance mode, twenty-three; in the proximity mode, twenty-five; in the contiguity mode, twenty-five; in the co-nascence mode, thirty; in the mutuality mode, twenty-eight; in the dependence mode, thirty; in the decisive support mode, twenty-five; in the pre-nascence mode, five; in the post-nascence mode, five; in the repetition mode, twenty-one; in the kamma mode, eleven; in the result mode, twenty-one; in the nutriment mode, eleven; in the faculty mode, eleven; in the jhāna mode, twenty-one; in the path mode, sixteen; in the association mode, eleven; in the dissociation mode, nine; in the presence mode, thirty; in the absence mode, twenty-five; in the disappearance mode, twenty-five; in the non-disappearance mode, thirty.

(Paccanīyānulomaṃ iminā kāraṇena vibhajitabbaṃ.)

(The negative-affirmative mode should be analyzed in this manner.)

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

The Negative-Affirmative Mode.

Vitakkattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Triad of Applied Thought is concluded.

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition.

1. Pītisahagataṃ [T 2.0152][M 2.0108][V 2.0121] dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – pītisahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā, tayo khandhe paṭicca eko khandho, dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pītisahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (1)

1. A state accompanied by joy, dependent on a state accompanied by joy, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy, three aggregates arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (1)

Pītisahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – pītisahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagatā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pītisahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagatā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (2)

A state accompanied by happiness, dependent on a state accompanied by joy, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy, three aggregates accompanied by happiness arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy, three aggregates accompanied by happiness arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (2)

Pītisahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato ca sukhasahagato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – pītisahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā ca sukhasahagatā ca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pītisahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā ca sukhasahagatā ca tayo khandhā [V 2.0122] …pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (3)

States accompanied by joy and happiness, dependent on a state accompanied by joy, arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy, three aggregates accompanied by joy and happiness arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy, three aggregates accompanied by joy and happiness arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (3)

2. Sukhasahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sukhasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca dve khandhā, dve khandhe [T 2.0153] paṭicca eko khandho. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe sukhasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. (1)

2. A state accompanied by happiness, dependent on a state accompanied by happiness, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by happiness, two aggregates arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by happiness, two aggregates arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. (1)

Sukhasahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – sukhasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe sukhasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (2)

A state accompanied by joy, dependent on a state accompanied by happiness, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by happiness, three aggregates accompanied by joy arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by happiness, three aggregates accompanied by joy arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (2)

Sukhasahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato ca sukhasahagato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – sukhasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā ca sukhasahagatā ca dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe sukhasahagataṃ [M 2.0109] ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā ca sukhasahagatā ca dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. (3)

States accompanied by joy and happiness, dependent on a state accompanied by happiness, arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by happiness, two aggregates accompanied by joy and happiness arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by happiness, two aggregates accompanied by joy and happiness arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. (3)

3. Upekkhāsahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca upekkhāsahagato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – upekkhāsahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

3. A state accompanied by equanimity, dependent on a state accompanied by equanimity, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by equanimity, two aggregates arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on… (1)

Pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (1)

A state accompanied by joy, dependent on a state accompanied by joy and happiness, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy and happiness, three aggregates accompanied by joy arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy and happiness, three aggregates accompanied by joy arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (1)

Pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagato dhammo uppajjati [T 2.0154] hetupaccayā – pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagatā dve khandhā, dve khandhe [V 2.0123] paṭicca eko khandho. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca sukhasahagatā dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. (2)

A state accompanied by happiness, dependent on a state accompanied by joy and happiness, arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy and happiness, two aggregates accompanied by happiness arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy and happiness, two aggregates accompanied by happiness arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. (2)

Pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato ca sukhasahagato ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā ca sukhasahagatā ca dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe pītisahagatañca sukhasahagatañca ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca pītisahagatā ca sukhasahagatā ca dve khandhā, dve khandhe paṭicca eko khandho. (3)

States accompanied by joy and happiness, dependent on a state accompanied by joy and happiness, arise by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy and happiness, two aggregates accompanied by joy and happiness arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate accompanied by joy and happiness, two aggregates accompanied by joy and happiness arise; dependent on two aggregates, one aggregate arises. (3)

Ārammaṇapaccayādi

Object-condition, and so on.

4. Pītisahagataṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca pītisahagato dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā… adhipatipaccayā… (paṭisandhikkhaṇe natthi) anantarapaccayā… samanantarapaccayā… sahajātapaccayā… aññamaññapaccayā… nissayapaccayā… upanissayapaccayā… purejātapaccayā… (purejāte paṭisandhikkhaṇe natthi) āsevanapaccayā… (āsevane vipākaṃ natthi) kammapaccayā… vipākapaccayā… āhāra…pe… indriya… jhāna… magga… sampayutta… vippayutta… atthi… natthi… vigata… avigatapaccayā.

4. A state accompanied by joy arises dependent on a state accompanied by joy by way of object condition… dominance condition… (not present at the moment of rebirth-linking) immediate condition… contiguity condition… co-nascence condition… reciprocity condition… support condition… decisive support condition… pre-nascence condition… (in pre-nascence, not present at the moment of rebirth-linking) repetition condition… (in repetition, result is not present) kamma condition… result condition… nutriment condition… faculty condition… jhāna condition… path condition… association condition… dissociation condition… presence condition… absence condition… disappearance condition… non-disappearance condition.

5. Hetuyā [T 2.0155][M 2.0110] dasa, ārammaṇe dasa, adhipatiyā dasa, anantare samanantare sahajāte aññamaññe nissaye upanissaye purejāte āsevane kamme vipāke āhāre indriye jhāne magge sampayutte vippayutte atthiyā natthiyā vigate avigate sabbattha dasa.

5. By way of root condition, ten; by way of object condition, ten; by way of dominance condition, ten; by way of immediate condition, by way of contiguity condition, by way of co-nascence condition, by way of reciprocity condition, by way of support condition, by way of decisive support condition, by way of pre-nascence condition, by way of repetition condition, by way of kamma condition, by way of result condition, by way of nutriment condition, by way of faculty condition, by way of jhāna condition, by way of path condition, by way of association condition, by way of dissociation condition, by way of presence condition, by way of absence condition, by way of disappearance condition, by way of non-disappearance condition—in all cases, ten.
