Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

75. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

75. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of the root condition—roots to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for their associated aggregates by way of the root condition. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā hetū cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development by way of the root condition—roots to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the root condition. (2)

Dassanena [V 2.0240] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ [T 2.0286] khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of the root condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—the roots to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of the root condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena. (3)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo… tīṇi.

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development... three.

76. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo…pe….

76. A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development by way of the root condition... and so on.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of the root condition—delusion accompanied by doubt is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of the root condition. (2)

Nevadassanena [M 2.0213] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development by way of the root condition—delusion accompanied by restlessness is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of the root condition. (3)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (4)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of the root condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—delusion accompanied by doubt is a condition by way of the root condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena. (4)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (5)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of the root condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—delusion accompanied by restlessness is a condition by way of the root condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena. (5)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

77. Dassanena [V 2.0241] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetuko [T 2.0287] rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Diṭṭhiṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Vicikicchaṃ ārabbha vicikicchā uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati. (1)

77. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of the object condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing—one savors and delights in attachment with a root to be abandoned by seeing; taking that as object, attachment with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises. One savors and delights in wrong view; taking that as object, attachment with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises. Taking doubt as object, doubt arises, wrong view arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises. Taking displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing as object, displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, and doubt arises. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā dassanena pahātabbahetuke pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti, dassanena pahātabbahetuke khandhe aniccato…pe… cetopariyañāṇena…pe… dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā [M 2.0214] cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya mohassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of the object condition for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—noble ones reflect upon the defilements with roots to be abandoned by seeing that have been abandoned; they know the defilements previously accumulated; they contemplate the aggregates with roots to be abandoned by seeing as impermanent… and so on… by means of the knowledge of others' minds… and so on… the aggregates with roots to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of the object condition for the knowledge of others' minds, for the knowledge of recollection of past lives, for the knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their actions, for the knowledge of the future, and for advertence and delusion. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetuke khandhe ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (3)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—dependent on the aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing, aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion arise. (3)

78. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa [T 2.0288] dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Uddhaccaṃ ārabbha uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ [V 2.0242] domanassaṃ uppajjati. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati. (1)

78. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development: one savors and delights in lust with a root to be abandoned by development; dependent on that, lust with a root to be abandoned by development arises, restlessness arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by development arises. Dependent on restlessness, restlessness arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by development arises. Dependent on displeasure with a root to be abandoned by development, displeasure with a root to be abandoned by development arises, and restlessness arises. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Uddhaccaṃ ārabbha diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati. (2)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing: one savors and delights in lust with a root to be abandoned by development; dependent on that, lust with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises. Dependent on restlessness, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises. Dependent on displeasure with a root to be abandoned by development, displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, and doubt arises. (2)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti, bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe aniccato…pe… cetopariyañāṇena…pe… bhāvanāya [M 2.0215] pahātabbahetukā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa[T 2.0289], yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya mohassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development: noble ones reflect on defilements with a root to be abandoned by development that have been abandoned, reflect on defilements that have been suppressed, know defilements previously accumulated, contemplate the aggregates with a root to be abandoned by development as impermanent… and so on… by means of mind-penetrating knowledge… and so on… the aggregates with a root to be abandoned by development are a condition by way of object-condition for mind-penetrating knowledge, for the knowledge of recollecting past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their actions, for the knowledge of the future, and for advertence and for delusion. (3)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (4)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—dependent on the aggregates with a root to be abandoned by development, aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion arise. (4)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ārabbha uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (5)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—dependent on the aggregates with a root to be abandoned by development, aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion arise. (5)

79. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa [V 2.0243] dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā…(vitthāretabbaṃ dassanattikasadisaṃ) āvajjanāya mohassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

79. A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—having given a gift… (to be expanded similarly to the triad concerning seeing) it is a condition by way of object-condition for advertence and for delusion. (1)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā… (yathā dassanattikaṃ). (2)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing—having given a gift… (as in the triad concerning seeing). (2)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā… (yathā dassanattikaṃ). (3)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development—having given a gift… (as in the triad concerning seeing). (3)

Nevadassanena [T 2.0290] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cakkhuṃ ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. Sotaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (4)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—dependent on the eye, aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion arise. Dependent on the ear… and so on… the base… dependent on the aggregates with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development, aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion arise. (4)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca [M 2.0216] dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuke khandhe ārabbha uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (5)

A phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by development and for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—dependent on the eye… and so on… the base… dependent on the aggregates with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development, aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion arise. (5)

80. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

80. Phenomena with a root to be abandoned by seeing and with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing—dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and on delusion, aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing arise. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (2)

Phenomena with a root to be abandoned by seeing and with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object-condition for a phenomenon with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development—dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and on delusion, aggregates with a root that is neither to be abandoned by seeing nor by development and delusion arise. (2)

Dassanena [T 2.0291][V 2.0244] pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – vicikicchāsahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (3)

Phenomena whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and phenomena whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Aggregates accompanied by doubt, and delusion, arise, having as object aggregates accompanied by doubt, and delusion. (3)

81. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (1)

81. Phenomena whose root is to be abandoned by development and phenomena whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing. Aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by seeing arise, having as object aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā uppajjanti. (2)

Phenomena whose root is to be abandoned by development and phenomena whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development. Aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development arise, having as object aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion. (2)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha [M 2.0217] nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (3)

Phenomena whose root is to be abandoned by development and phenomena whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Aggregates whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, and delusion, arise, having as object aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion. (3)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena [T 2.0292] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (4)

Phenomena whose root is to be abandoned by development and phenomena whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Aggregates accompanied by doubt, and delusion, arise, having as object aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion. (4)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uddhaccasahagate khandhe ca mohañca ārabbha uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. (5)

Phenomena whose root is to be abandoned by development and phenomena whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of object for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development and for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion, arise, having as object aggregates accompanied by restlessness, and delusion. (5)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

82. Dassanena [V 2.0245] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo (dassanattikasadisaṃ, dasa pañhā).

82. A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of dominance for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing (similar to the triad of seeing, ten questions).

Anantarapaccayo

Contiguity Condition

83. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ dassanena pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

83. A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of contiguity for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing. Preceding aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of contiguity for succeeding aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by seeing. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa mohassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of contiguity for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt are a condition by way of contiguity for succeeding delusion; aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of contiguity for emergence. (2)

Dassanena [T 2.0293] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa [M 2.0218] anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of contiguity for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt are a condition by way of contiguity for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion. (3)

84. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

84. A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of contiguity for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development. Preceding aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development are a condition by way of contiguity for succeeding aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa mohassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of contiguity for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Preceding aggregates accompanied by restlessness are a condition by way of contiguity for succeeding delusion; aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development are a condition by way of contiguity for emergence. (2)

Bhāvanāya [V 2.0246] pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of contiguity for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by development and for a phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Preceding aggregates accompanied by restlessness are a condition by way of contiguity for succeeding aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion. (3)

85. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicikicchāsahagato [T 2.0294] uddhaccasahagato moho pacchimassa pacchimassa vicikicchāsahagatassa uddhaccasahagatassa mohassa anantarapaccayena paccayo; purimā purimā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa…pe… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

85. A phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Preceding delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a contiguity condition for succeeding delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness; preceding aggregates with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation are a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation; adaptation for change-of-lineage... adaptation for purification... for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a contiguity condition for the attainment of fruition. (1)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicikicchāsahagato [M 2.0219] moho pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā dassanena pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision. Preceding delusion accompanied by doubt is a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt; adverting is a contiguity condition for aggregates with a cause to be abandoned by vision. (2)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo uddhaccasahagato moho pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation. Preceding delusion accompanied by restlessness is a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by restlessness; adverting is a contiguity condition for aggregates with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation. (3)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo vicikicchāsahagato moho pacchimānaṃ [T 2.0295] pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision and for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Preceding delusion accompanied by doubt is a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion; adverting is a contiguity condition for aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion. (4)

Nevadassanena [V 2.0247] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimo purimo uddhaccasahagato moho pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo; āvajjanā uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation is a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation and for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Preceding delusion accompanied by restlessness is a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion; adverting is a contiguity condition for aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion. (5)

86. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

86. Both a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision and a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation are a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision. Preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca pacchimassa pacchimassa mohassa anantarapaccayena [M 2.0220] paccayo; vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Both a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision and a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation are a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a contiguity condition for succeeding delusion; aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a contiguity condition for emergence. (2)

Dassanena [T 2.0296] pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

Both a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision and a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation are a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision and for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation. Preceding aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a contiguity condition for succeeding aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion. (3)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (dassanena sadisaṃ gamanaṃ).

Both a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation and a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation are a contiguity condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation... (three, the exposition is similar to that for vision).

Samanantarapaccayādi

Immediacy Condition, etc.

87. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo… (anantarasadisaṃ) sahajātapaccayena paccayo… (saṃkhittaṃ. Paṭiccavāre [V 2.0248] sahajātasadisaṃ) aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… (saṃkhittaṃ. Paṭiccavāre aññamaññasadisaṃ) nissayapaccayena paccayo… (saṃkhittaṃ. Paccayavāre nissayavārasadisaṃ. Visuṃ ghaṭanā natthi).

87. A phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision is a condition for a phenomenon with a cause to be abandoned by vision by immediacy condition... (similar to contiguity condition)... by conascence condition... (in brief; similar to conascence in the Dependent Origination section)... by mutuality condition... (in brief; similar to mutuality in the Dependent Origination section)... by support condition... (in brief; similar to the support section in the Condition section. There is no separate exposition).

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition.

88. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, 51anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ dosaṃ… mohaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo… doso… moho… [T 2.0297] diṭṭhi… patthanā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

88. A state with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of decisive support condition: by way of object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support...pe... By way of natural decisive support: relying on lust with a root to be abandoned by seeing, one kills a living being...pe... or splits the Saṅgha. Relying on hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing, one kills a living being...pe... or splits the Saṅgha. Lust... hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for lust...pe... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Dassanena [M 2.0221] pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ dosaṃ… mohaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo…pe… patthanā… saddhāya…pe… paññāya… kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa phalasamāpattiyā mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: by way of immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support...pe... By way of natural decisive support: relying on lust with a root to be abandoned by seeing, one gives a gift...pe... or produces an attainment. Relying on hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing, one gives a gift...pe... or produces an attainment. Lust...pe... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for faith...pe... for wisdom... for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for fruition-attainment, and for delusion by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo… doso… moho… diṭṭhi… patthanā vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: by way of immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support...pe... By way of natural decisive support: lust... hatred... delusion... wrong view... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for the aggregates associated with doubt and for delusion by way of decisive support condition. (3)

89. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena [V 2.0249] paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo… doso… moho… māno… patthanā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa [T 2.0298] rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… mānassa… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

89. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo…pe… patthanā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa rāgassa… dosassa… mohassa… diṭṭhiyā… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Sakabhaṇḍe chandarāgo parabhaṇḍe [M 2.0222] chandarāgassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Sakapariggahe chandarāgo parapariggahe chandarāgassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with a root to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of decisive support condition: by way of object decisive support, natural decisive support...pe... By way of natural decisive support: relying on lust with a root to be abandoned by cultivation, one kills a living being...pe... or splits the Saṅgha. Relying on hatred... delusion... conceit... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by cultivation, one kills a living being...pe... or splits the Saṅgha. Lust...pe... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for lust... for hatred... for delusion... for wrong view... for aspiration with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of decisive support condition. Desire for one's own property is a condition for desire for others' property by way of decisive support condition. Desire for one's own belongings is a condition for desire for others' belongings by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ rāgaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ dosaṃ… mohaṃ… mānaṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo…pe… patthanā saddhāya…pe… paññāya… kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa phalasamāpattiyā mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with a root to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: by way of immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support...pe... By way of natural decisive support: relying on lust with a root to be abandoned by cultivation, one gives a gift...pe... or produces an attainment. Relying on hatred... delusion... conceit... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by cultivation, one gives a gift...pe... or produces an attainment. Lust...pe... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for faith...pe... for wisdom... for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for fruition-attainment, and for delusion by way of decisive support condition. (3)

Bhāvanāya [T 2.0299] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo…pe… patthanā vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (4)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa [V 2.0250] ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo…pe… patthanā uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state with a root to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by cultivation and for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: by way of immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support...pe... By way of natural decisive support: lust...pe... aspiration with a root to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for the aggregates associated with restlessness and for delusion by way of decisive support condition. 90. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ… mohaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saddhā…pe… moho saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

90. A state with a cause to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state with a cause to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... and so on. Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one gives a gift... and so on... produces an attainment. Relying on virtue... and so on... wisdom... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... climate... food... lodging... delusion, one gives a gift... and so on. Faith... and so on... delusion is a condition for faith... and so on... for fruition-attainment, and for delusion by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Nevadassanena [M 2.0223] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – saddhaṃ [T 2.0300] upanissāya diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ… mohaṃ upanissāya pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ moho ca dassanena pahātabbahetukassa rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one grasps a wrong view. Relying on virtue... and so on... wisdom... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... and so on... lodging... delusion, one kills a living being... and so on... splits the Saṅgha. Faith... and so on... lodging, and delusion are a condition by way of decisive support condition for lust... and so on... for aspiration with a cause to be abandoned by seeing. (2)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Natural decisive support: relying on faith, one generates conceit... and so on... relying on delusion, one generates conceit. Faith... and so on... lodging, and delusion are a condition by way of decisive support condition for lust... and so on... for aspiration with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation. (3)

Natural decisive support: faith... and so on... wisdom... bodily pleasure... bodily pain... and so on... lodging, and delusion are a condition by way of decisive support condition for the aggregates associated with doubt and for delusion. (4)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe….
