Natural decisive support: the aggregates associated with restlessness, and delusion, are a condition for lust... and so on... for aspiration with a cause to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho [M 2.0225] ca saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

States whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation and states whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation are a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion are a condition for faith... for the attainment of fruition and for delusion by way of decisive support condition.

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (4)

States whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation and states whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation are a condition for states whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing and for states whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition. Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion are a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion by way of decisive support condition.

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko [T 2.0303] ca dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (5)

States whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation and states whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation are a condition for states whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation and for states whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of decisive support condition: contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion are a condition for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion by way of decisive support condition.

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

93. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ [V 2.0253] – cakkhuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati, sotaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati; dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

93. A state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one discerns the eye as impermanent... one discerns the ear... one discerns the base as impermanent...; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds. The visible object is a condition for eye-consciousness... the tangible object is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness... the base is a condition for the aggregates whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation and for delusion by way of pre-nascence condition.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo…pe… diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati[M 2.0226]. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu dassanena pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena [T 2.0304] paccayo. (2)

A state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one savors and delights in the eye... the base. Dependent on that, lust whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing arises... wrong view... doubt... grief whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing arises. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for the aggregates whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing by way of pre-nascence condition.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, uddhaccaṃ uppajjati, bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one savors and delights in the eye... the base. Dependent on that, lust whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation arises, restlessness arises, grief whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation arises. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for the aggregates whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing and for a state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: dependent on the eye... the base, the aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion arise. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion by way of pre-nascence condition.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ ārabbha uddhaccasahagatā [V 2.0254] khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu [T 2.0305] uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca purejātapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation and for a state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: dependent on the eye... the base, the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion arise. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion by way of pre-nascence condition.

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

94. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

94. A state whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of post-nascence condition. Subsequently arisen aggregates whose cause is to be abandoned by seeing are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition.

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā bhāvanāya [M 2.0227] pahātabbahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation is a condition for a state whose cause is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by cultivation by way of post-nascence condition. Subsequently arisen aggregates whose cause is to be abandoned by cultivation are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of subsequent-arising for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Subsequently arisen aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of subsequent-arising for this pre-arisen body. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

Phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing and phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are conditions by way of subsequent-arising for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Subsequently arisen aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition by way of subsequent-arising for this pre-arisen body. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko [T 2.0306] ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

Phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by development and phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are conditions by way of subsequent-arising for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Subsequently arisen aggregates accompanied by agitation and delusion are a condition by way of subsequent-arising for this pre-arisen body. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

95. Dassanena [V 2.0255] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ dassanena pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

95. A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of repetition for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing. Earlier and earlier aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of repetition for later and later aggregates whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā pacchimassa pacchimassa mohassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of repetition for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Earlier and earlier aggregates accompanied by doubt are a condition by way of repetition for later and later delusion. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ [M 2.0228] pacchimānaṃ vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca āsevanapaccayena paccayo.

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of repetition for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Earlier and earlier aggregates accompanied by doubt are a condition by way of repetition for later and later aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion.

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa (saṃkhittaṃ) tīṇi.

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development (abbreviated). (Three ways).

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo…pe…. (Āsevanamūlake vuṭṭhānassapi āvajjanāyapi pahātabbaṃ, sattarasa pañhā paripuṇṇā, anantarasadisā).

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development...and so on... (In the Repetition Root Section, [the analysis] is also to be applied to emergence and attention. The seventeen questions are complete, similar to the Proximity section.)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

96. Dassanena [T 2.0307] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

96. A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing. Volition whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for the associated aggregates. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā dassanena pahātabbahetukā cetanā mohassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – dassanena [V 2.0256] pahātabbahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—simultaneously arisen and at different moments. Simultaneously arisen, volition whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for delusion and for mind-originated materiality. At different moments, volition whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Volition whose roots are to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of kamma for the associated aggregates, for delusion, and for mind-originated materiality. (3)

97. Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

97. A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development. Volition whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of kamma for the associated aggregates. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā cetanā mohassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Volition whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of kamma for delusion and for mind-originated materiality. (2)

Bhāvanāya [T 2.0308][M 2.0229] pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned by development and for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Volition whose roots are to be abandoned by development is a condition by way of kamma for the associated aggregates, for delusion, and for mind-originated materiality. (3)

98. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

98. A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of kamma for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—simultaneously arisen and at different moments. Simultaneously arisen, volition whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of kamma for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality. At the moment of rebirth-linking...and so on... At different moments, volition whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of kamma for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced materiality. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Result Condition

99. Nevadassanena [V 2.0257] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo (pavattipaṭisandhi) vipākā khandhā vatthussa…pe….

99. A phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of result condition for a phenomenon whose roots are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development (during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking)—the resultant aggregates are a condition for the physical basis…and so on….

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment Condition

100. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

100. A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing. Nutriments whose root is to be abandoned by seeing are a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for the associated aggregates. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā āhārā [T 2.0309] mohassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Nutriments whose root is to be abandoned by seeing are a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for delusion and for mind-originated materiality. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetukā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Nutriments whose root is to be abandoned by seeing are a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for the associated aggregates, for delusion, and for mind-originated materiality. (3)

Bhāvanāya [M 2.0230] pahātabbahetuko dhammo… tīṇi (dassanena sadisaṃ).

A state whose root is to be abandoned by development… three (similar to the preceding).

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo.

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Nutriments whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality. At the moment of rebirth-linking… physical nutriment is a condition, by way of nutriment condition, for this body.

Indriyapaccayādi

Faculty Condition, etc.

101. Dassanena [V 2.0258] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo… tīṇi (āhārasadisaṃ. Moho kātabbo).

101. A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of faculty condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing… three (similar to the nutriment condition; delusion is to be included).

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo… tīṇi.

A state whose root is to be abandoned by development… three.

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo… [T 2.0310] maggapaccayena paccayo… (ime sahetukā kātabbā) sampayuttapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavāre sampayuttavārasadisaṃ).

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of faculty condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Faculties whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition, by way of faculty condition, for the associated aggregates… the eye faculty for eye-consciousness… the body faculty for body-consciousness… the material life faculty is a condition for materiality produced by kamma, by way of faculty condition… by way of jhāna condition… by way of path condition… (these are to be understood as with roots) by way of association condition (similar to the association section in the Dependent Origination analysis).

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

102. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (dassanattikasadisaṃ).

102. A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, post-nascence (similar to the triad pertaining to seeing).

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (dassanattikasadisaṃ).

A state whose root is to be abandoned by development is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, post-nascence (similar to the triad pertaining to seeing).

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (dassanattikasadisaṃ). Pacchājātā – nevadassanena [M 2.0231] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa…pe…. (1)

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence (similar to the triad pertaining to seeing). Post-nascence—aggregates whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development, and delusion, are a condition for this pre-nascent body… (1)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu dassanena pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe…. (2)

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing. Pre-nascence—the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by seeing… (2)

Nevadassanena [V 2.0259] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe…. (3)

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development. Pre-nascence—the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates whose root is to be abandoned by development… (3)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa [T 2.0311] ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Pre-nascence—the physical basis is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion. (4)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned by development and for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Pre-nascence—the physical basis is a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion. (5)

103. Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

103. A state whose root is to be abandoned by seeing and a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are conditions, by way of dissociation condition, for a state whose root is to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, post-nascence. Co-nascence—the aggregates accompanied by doubt, and delusion, are a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for mind-originated materiality. Post-nascence—the aggregates accompanied by doubt, and delusion, are a condition, by way of dissociation condition, for this pre-nascent body. (1)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ…pe…. Pacchājātā – uddhaccasahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state with a root to be abandoned by development and a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of dissociation condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, post-nascence. Co-nascently: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion are a condition by way of dissociation condition for mind-originated material phenomena… Post-nascently: the aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion are a condition by way of dissociation condition for this pre-nascent body. (1)

Atthipaccayādi

The Condition of Presence, etc.

104. Dassanena [T 2.0312][M 2.0232] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe…. (1)

104. A state with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing: one aggregate with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of presence condition for the three aggregates… (1)

Dassanena [V 2.0260] pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā mohassa cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, post-nascence. Co-nascently: aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of presence condition for mind-originated material phenomena. Co-nascently: aggregates accompanied by doubt are a condition by way of presence condition for delusion and mind-originated material phenomena. Post-nascently: aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing are a condition by way of presence condition for this pre-nascent body. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – dassanena pahātabbahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Vicikicchāsahagato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe…. (3)

A state with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development: one aggregate with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition by way of presence condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena. One aggregate accompanied by doubt is a condition by way of presence condition for the three aggregates, for delusion, and for mind-originated material phenomena… (3)

Bhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo… tīṇi.

A state with a root to be abandoned by development… three.

105. Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – nevadassanena [T 2.0313] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… asaññasattānaṃ…pe…. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… vatthu nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā [M 2.0233] khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo; kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ…pe…. (1)

105. A state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty. Co-nascently: one aggregate with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of presence condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena… Delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness is a condition by way of presence condition for mind-originated material phenomena. At the moment of re-linking… for non-percipient beings… Pre-nascently: the eye… the base… as impermanent… with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds; the visible form base is a condition by way of presence condition for eye-consciousness… the tangible object base is a condition by way of presence condition for body-consciousness… the eye-base… the body-base… the base is a condition by way of presence condition for aggregates with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development and for delusion. Post-nascently: aggregates with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development and delusion are a condition by way of presence condition for this pre-nascent body; physical nutriment is a condition by way of presence condition for this body… the material life-faculty is a condition by way of presence condition for karma-produced materiality… (1)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena [V 2.0261] paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati; taṃ ārabbha dassanena pahātabbahetuko rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā uppajjati, dassanena pahātabbahetukaṃ domanassaṃ uppajjati, vatthu dassanena pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing—co-nascence, pre-nascence. Co-nascently: delusion accompanied by doubt is a condition by way of presence condition for the associated aggregates. Pre-nascently: one relishes and delights in the eye… the base; taking that as object, greed with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, displeasure with a root to be abandoned by seeing arises; the base is a condition by way of presence condition for aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing. (2)

Nevadassanena [T 2.0314] nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ assādeti abhinandati…pe… vatthu bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by development—co-nascence, pre-nascence. Co-nascently: delusion accompanied by restlessness is a condition by way of presence condition for the associated aggregates. Pre-nascently: the eye… the base… one relishes and delights in the base… the base is a condition by way of presence condition for aggregates with a root to be abandoned by development. (3)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ ārabbha vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti…pe… vatthuṃ ārabbha…pe… vatthu vicikicchāsahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (4)

A state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of presence condition for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—co-nascence, pre-nascence. Co-nascently: delusion accompanied by doubt is a condition by way of presence condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena. Pre-nascently: taking the eye as object, aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion arise… taking the base as object… the base is a condition by way of presence condition for the aggregates accompanied by doubt and for delusion. (4)

Nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko dhammo bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – uddhaccasahagato moho sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ ārabbha uddhaccasahagatā [M 2.0234] khandhā ca moho ca uppajjanti…pe… vatthuṃ ārabbha…pe… vatthu uddhaccasahagatānaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo. (5)

A state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development is a condition by way of presence for a state with a root to be abandoned by development and for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—by way of co-nascence, by way of pre-nascence. By way of co-nascence: delusion accompanied by restlessness is a condition by way of presence for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena. By way of pre-nascence: having the eye as a basis, aggregates accompanied by restlessness and delusion arise…pe… having the base as a basis…pe… the base is a condition by way of presence for aggregates accompanied by restlessness and for delusion. (5)

106. Dassanena [T 2.0315] pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – dassanena pahātabbahetuko eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo [V 2.0262] …pe… dve khandhā…pe… vicikicchāsahagato eko khandho ca moho ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe…. (1)

106. States with a root to be abandoned by seeing and states with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of presence for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing—by way of co-nascence, by way of pre-nascence. By way of co-nascence: one aggregate with a root to be abandoned by seeing and the base are a condition by way of presence for the three aggregates… two aggregates… one aggregate accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition by way of presence for the three aggregates… two aggregates… (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātā – vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca vatthu ca mohassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – vicikicchāsahagatā khandhā ca moho ca purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – dassanena pahātabbahetukā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

States with a root to be abandoned by seeing and states with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of presence for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—by way of co-nascence, by way of pre-nascence, by way of post-nascence, by way of nutriment, by way of faculty. By way of co-nascence: aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing and the great elements are a condition by way of presence for mind-originated material phenomena. By way of co-nascence: aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition by way of presence for mind-originated material phenomena. By way of co-nascence: aggregates accompanied by doubt and the base are a condition by way of presence for delusion. By way of post-nascence: aggregates accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition by way of presence for this pre-arisen body. By way of post-nascence: aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing and physical nutriment are a condition by way of presence for this body. By way of post-nascence: aggregates with a root to be abandoned by seeing and the material life-faculty are a condition by way of presence for karma-produced materiality. (2)

Dassanena [T 2.0316] pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – vicikicchāsahagato eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ mohassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… vicikicchāsahagato eko khandho ca moho ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā ca moho ca…pe…. (3)

States with a root to be abandoned by seeing and states with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of presence for a state with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a state with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development—by way of co-nascence, by way of pre-nascence. By way of co-nascence: one aggregate accompanied by doubt and the base are a condition by way of presence for the three aggregates and for delusion… two aggregates… one aggregate accompanied by doubt and delusion are a condition by way of presence for the three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena… two aggregates and delusion… (3)

Bhāvanāya [M 2.0235] pahātabbahetuko ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuko ca dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ. Tisso pañhā, dassanena nayena vibhajitabbā, “uddhacca”nti niyāmetabbaṃ) natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo… avigatapaccayena paccayo….

States with a root to be abandoned by development and states with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development are a condition by way of presence for a state with a root to be abandoned by development (abbreviated. The three questions should be analyzed in the same way as for the section on seeing, and should be determined with 'restlessness'); by way of absence condition… by way of disappearance condition… by way of non-disappearance condition….

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Conformity to Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

Suddhaṃ

Pure.

107. Hetuyā [V 2.0263] ekādasa, ārammaṇe ekavīsa, adhipatiyā dasa, anantare sattarasa, samanantare sattarasa, sahajāte sattarasa, aññamaññe ekādasa, nissaye sattarasa, upanissaye ekavīsa, purejāte pañca, pacchājāte pañca, āsevane sattarasa, kamme satta, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre satta, indriye satta, jhāne satta, magge satta, sampayutte ekādasa, vippayutte nava, atthiyā sattarasa, natthiyā sattarasa, vigate sattarasa, avigate sattarasa (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

107. By way of root condition, eleven; by way of object condition, twenty-one; by way of dominance condition, ten; by way of contiguity condition, seventeen; by way of immediate contiguity condition, seventeen; by way of co-nascence condition, seventeen; by way of mutuality condition, eleven; by way of dependence condition, seventeen; by way of decisive support condition, twenty-one; by way of pre-nascence condition, five; by way of post-nascence condition, five; by way of repetition condition, seventeen; by way of kamma condition, seven; by way of result condition, one; by way of nutriment condition, seven; by way of faculty condition, seven; by way of jhāna condition, seven; by way of path condition, seven; by way of association condition, eleven; by way of dissociation condition, nine; by way of presence condition, seventeen; by way of absence condition, seventeen; by way of disappearance condition, seventeen; by way of non-disappearance condition, seventeen (thus should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

Direct Order.

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Negative Section

108. Dassanena [T 2.0317] pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

108. A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition. (2)

Dassanena pahātabbahetuko dhammo dassanena pahātabbahetukassa ca nevadassanena nabhāvanāya pahātabbahetukassa ca dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing is a condition for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned by seeing and for a phenomenon with a root to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of decisive support condition. (3)

(Idhāpi sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ atthi. Ye te pañhā na likhitā, te pāḷiyaṃ gaṇentānaṃ byañjanena na samenti. Te pāḷiyaṃ na likhitā gaṇanā pākaṭā honti. Yadi saṃsayo uppajjati, anulome atthipaccaye pekkhitabbaṃ.)

(Here too, conascence and prenascence exist. Those questions that are not written down do not accord with the letter for those reckoning in the Pāli. Though they are not written in the Pāli, the reckoning becomes manifest. If doubt arises, one should look to the presence condition in the positive method.)

Nahetuyā [V 2.0267] ekavīsa, naārammaṇe naadhipatiyā naanantare nasamanantare nasahajāte naaññamaññe nanissaye naupanissaye napurejāte [M 2.0239] napacchājāte naāsevane nakamme navipāke naāhāre naindriye najhāne namagge nasampayutte navippayutte noatthiyā nonatthiyā novigate noavigate sabbattha ekavīsa (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

113. By non-root condition, twenty-one; by non-object condition, by non-predominance condition, by non-proximity condition, by non-contiguity condition, by non-conascence condition, by non-mutuality condition, by non-dependence condition, by non-decisive support condition, by non-prenascence condition, by non-postnascence condition, by non-repetition condition, by non-kamma condition, by non-result condition, by non-nutriment condition, by non-faculty condition, by non-jhāna condition, by non-path condition, by non-association condition, by non-dissociation condition, by non-presence condition, by non-absence condition, by non-disappearance condition, by non-nondisappearance condition: in all cases, twenty-one (thus it should be counted).

Nahetupaccayā [V 2.0268] ārammaṇe ekavīsa, adhipatiyā dasa, anantare sattarasa, samanantare sattarasa, sahajāte sattarasa, aññamaññe ekādasa, nissaye sattarasa, upanissaye ekavīsa, purejāte pañca, pacchājāte pañca, āsevane sattarasa, kamme satta, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre satta, indriye satta, jhāne satta, magge satta, sampayutte ekādasa, vippayutte nava, atthiyā sattarasa, natthiyā sattarasa, vigate sattarasa, avigate sattarasa (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

115. By non-root condition: with object condition, twenty-one; with predominance condition, ten; with proximity condition, seventeen; with contiguity condition, seventeen; with conascence condition, seventeen; with mutuality condition, eleven; with dependence condition, seventeen; with decisive support condition, twenty-one; with prenascence condition, five; with postnascence condition, five; with repetition condition, seventeen; with kamma condition, seven; with result condition, one; with nutriment condition, seven; with faculty condition, seven; with jhāna condition, seven; with path condition, seven; with association condition, eleven; with dissociation condition, nine; with presence condition, seventeen; with absence condition, seventeen; with disappearance condition, seventeen; with nondisappearance condition, seventeen (thus it should be counted).

Dassanenapahātabbahetukattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

10. Ācayagāmittikaṃ

10. The Triad on States Leading to Accumulation

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. Conditional Section

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Conditional Affirmative

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. Analysis Section

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

1. Ācayagāmiṃ [T 2.0323][M 2.0240][V 2.0269] dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – ācayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (1)

1. A state that leads to accumulation arises in dependence on a state that leads to accumulation by root condition: dependent on one aggregate that leads to accumulation, three aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (1)

Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline arises in dependence on a state that leads to accumulation by root condition: dependent on the aggregates that lead to accumulation, mind-originated matter arises. (2)

Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – ācayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (3)

States that lead to accumulation and states that lead neither to accumulation nor to decline arise in dependence on a state that leads to accumulation by root condition: dependent on one aggregate that leads to accumulation, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. (3)

2. Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca apacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – apacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (1)

2. A state that leads to decline arises in dependence on a state that leads to decline by root condition: dependent on one aggregate that leads to decline, three aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. (1)

Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (2)

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline arises in dependence on a state that leads to decline by root condition: dependent on the aggregates that lead to decline, mind-originated matter arises. (2)

Apacayagāmiṃ [V 2.0270] dhammaṃ paṭicca apacayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – apacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ. (3)

States that lead to decline and states that lead neither to accumulation nor to decline arise in dependence on a state that leads to decline by root condition: dependent on one aggregate that leads to decline, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-originated matter arise. (3)

3. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [T 2.0324] dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā…pe… dve mahābhūte paṭicca dve mahābhūtā; mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

3. A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline arises in dependence on a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline by root condition: dependent on one aggregate that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline, three aggregates and kamma-born matter arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe… dependent on the aggregates, the base; dependent on the base, the aggregates; dependent on one great element, three great elements …pe… dependent on two great elements, two great elements; dependent on the great elements, mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. (1)

Ācayagāmiñca [M 2.0241] nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline arises in dependence on a state that leads to accumulation and a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline by root condition: dependent on the aggregates that lead to accumulation and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises. (1)

Apacayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline arises in dependence on a state that leads to decline and a state that leads neither to accumulation nor to decline by root condition: dependent on the aggregates that lead to decline and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

4. Ācayagāmiṃ [V 2.0271] dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – ācayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

4. An accumulating state arises dependent on an accumulating state by object condition. Dependent on one accumulating aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca apacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – apacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

A declining state arises dependent on a declining state by object condition. Dependent on one declining aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [T 2.0325] dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by object condition. Dependent on one neither-accumulating-nor-declining aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… dependent on the base, the aggregates arise. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Predominance Condition

5. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā… tīṇi.

5. An accumulating state arises dependent on an accumulating state by predominance condition… three.

Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca apacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā… tīṇi.

A declining state arises dependent on a declining state by predominance condition… three.

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo… ekaṃ (paṭisandhi natthi); ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca tayo mahābhūtā…pe… mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state… one (rebirth-linking is not included); dependent on one great element, three great elements arise…pe… dependent on the great elements, mind-originated form and derived form arise. (1)

Ācayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on an accumulating state and a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by predominance condition. Dependent on the accumulating aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated form arises. (1)

Apacayagāmiñca [M 2.0242] nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a declining state and a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by predominance condition. Dependent on the declining aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated form arises. (1)

Anantarapaccayādi

Immediacy Condition, etc.

6. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca, ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati anantarapaccayā… samanantarapaccayā [V 2.0272]… sahajātapaccayā (sabbepi mahābhūtā kātabbā)… aññamaññapaccayā (cittasamuṭṭhānampi kaṭattārūpampi upādārūpampi natthi)… nissayapaccayā… upanissayapaccayā… purejātapaccayā… āsevanapaccayā… kammapaccayā… vipākapaccayā… āhārapaccayā… indriyapaccayā… jhānapaccayā… maggapaccayā… sampayuttapaccayā… [T 2.0326] vippayuttapaccayā… atthipaccayā… natthipaccayā… vigatapaccayā… avigatapaccayā….

6. An accumulating state arises dependent on an accumulating state by immediacy condition… by contiguity condition… by co-nascence condition (all the great elements should be included)… by mutuality condition (mind-originated form, kamma-produced form, and derived form are not included)… by dependence condition… by strong dependence condition… by pre-nascence condition… by repetition condition… by kamma condition… by result condition… by nutriment condition… by faculty condition… by jhāna condition… by path condition… by association condition… by dissociation condition… by presence condition… by absence condition… by disappearance condition… by non-disappearance condition.

1. The Positive Exposition of Conditions

Suddhaṃ

Pure

7. Hetuyā nava, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā nava, anantare tīṇi, samanantare tīṇi, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe tīṇi, nissaye nava, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte tīṇi, āsevane tīṇi, kamme nava, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre nava, indriye nava, jhāne nava, magge nava, sampayutte tīṇi, vippayutte nava, atthiyā nava, natthiyā tīṇi, vigate tīṇi, avigate nava (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

7. By root condition, nine; by object condition, three; by predominance condition, nine; by immediacy condition, three; by contiguity condition, three; by co-nascence condition, nine; by mutuality condition, three; by dependence condition, nine; by strong dependence condition, three; by pre-nascence condition, three; by repetition condition, three; by kamma condition, nine; by result condition, one; by nutriment condition, nine; by faculty condition, nine; by jhāna condition, nine; by path condition, nine; by association condition, three; by dissociation condition, nine; by presence condition, nine; by absence condition, three; by disappearance condition, three; by non-disappearance condition, nine (thus it should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

1. Section on Analysis

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

8. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

8. An accumulating state arises dependent on an accumulating state by non-root condition. Dependent on the doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied and restlessness-accompanied delusion arises. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ [M 2.0243][V 2.0273] dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by non-root condition. Dependent on one rootless neither-accumulating-nor-declining aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated form arise…pe… dependent on two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking…pe… dependent on the aggregates, the base arises; dependent on the base, the aggregates arise; dependent on one great element…pe… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… for non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element…pe…. (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayo

Non-Object Condition

9. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo [T 2.0327] uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

9. A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on an accumulating state by non-object condition. Dependent on accumulating aggregates, mind-originated form arises. (1)

Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a declining state by non-object condition. Dependent on declining aggregates, mind-originated form arises. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ…pe…. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by non-object condition. Dependent on neither-accumulating-nor-declining aggregates, mind-originated form arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… dependent on the aggregates, the base arises…pe… one great element…pe… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… for non-percipient beings…pe…. (1)

Ācayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on an accumulating state and a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by non-object condition. Dependent on accumulating aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated form arises. (1)

Apacayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A neither-accumulating-nor-declining state arises dependent on a declining state and a neither-accumulating-nor-declining state by non-object condition. Dependent on declining aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated form arises. (1)

Naadhipatipaccayo

Non-predominance condition

10. Ācayagāmiṃ [V 2.0274] dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā… tīṇi.

10. An accumulating state arises dependent on an accumulating state by non-predominance condition… three.

Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca apacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca apacayagāmī adhipati. (1)

A state leading to decline arises dependent on a state leading to decline, not by the dominance condition. Dependent on aggregates leading to decline, there is dominance leading to decline. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ [M 2.0244] dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ ekaṃ [T 2.0328] khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā; ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

A state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises dependent on a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, not by the dominance condition—dependent on one aggregate that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, three aggregates and mind-produced materiality… two aggregates… at the moment of rebirth-linking… dependent on aggregates, the base; dependent on the base, aggregates; one great element… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… for non-percipient beings, one great element… and so on. (1)

Ācayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

A state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises dependent on a state that leads to accumulation and a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, not by the dominance condition—mind-produced materiality arises dependent on aggregates that lead to accumulation and the great elements. (1)

Naanantarapaccayādi

Not by Contiguity Condition, etc.

11. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naanantarapaccayā… nasamanantarapaccayā… naaññamaññapaccayā… naupanissayapaccayā… napurejātapaccayā (kusalattikasadisā satta pañhā)… napacchājātapaccayā.

11. Dependent on a state that leads to accumulation, a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises—not by the contiguity condition… not by the immediate contiguity condition… not by the mutuality condition… not by the decisive support condition… not by the prenascent condition (seven questions similar to the wholesome triad)… not by the postnascent condition.

Naāsevanapaccayo

Not by Repetition Condition

12. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naāsevanapaccayā… tīṇi.

12. Dependent on a state leading to accumulation, a state leading to accumulation arises, not by the repetition condition… three.

Apacayagāmiṃ [V 2.0275] dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naāsevanapaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

Dependent on a state that leads to decline, a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises, not by the repetition condition: mind-produced materiality dependent on the aggregates that lead to decline. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naāsevanapaccayā (ekā pañhā sabbe mahābhūtā kātabbā).

Dependent on a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises—not by the repetition condition (one question; all great elements should be treated in this way).

Ācayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati naāsevanapaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

Dependent on a state that leads to accumulation and a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises, not by the repetition condition: mind-produced materiality dependent on the aggregates that lead to accumulation and the great elements. (1)

Apacayagāmiñca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiñca dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo [T 2.0329] uppajjati naāsevanapaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. (1)

Dependent on a state that leads to decline and a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises, not by the repetition condition: mind-produced materiality dependent on the aggregates that lead to decline and the great elements. (1)

Nakammapaccayo

Not by Kamma Condition

13. Ācayagāmiṃ [M 2.0245] dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – ācayagāmī khandhe paṭicca ācayagāmī cetanā. (1)

13. Dependent on a state that leads to accumulation, a state that leads to accumulation arises, not by the kamma condition: volition that leads to accumulation dependent on the aggregates that lead to accumulation. (1)

Apacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca apacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – apacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca apacayagāmī cetanā. (1)

Dependent on a state leading to decline, a state leading to decline arises, not by the kamma condition: dependent on aggregates leading to decline, volition leading to decline. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhe paṭicca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī cetanā; bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. (1)

Dependent on a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline, a state that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline arises, not by the kamma condition: dependent on aggregates that neither lead to accumulation nor to decline, volition that neither leads to accumulation nor to decline; external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… one great element… and so on. (1)

Navipākapaccayādi

Not by Result Condition, etc.

14. Ācayagāmiṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ācayagāmī dhammo uppajjati navipākapaccayā (paripuṇṇaṃ[V 2.0276], paṭisandhi natthi)… naāhārapaccayā… naindriyapaccayā… najhānapaccayā… namaggapaccayā… nasampayuttapaccayā… navippayuttapaccayā (tīṇi)… nonatthipaccayā… novigatapaccayā.

14. Dependent on a state leading to accumulation, a state leading to accumulation arises, not by the result condition (complete, there is no rebirth-linking)… not by the nutriment condition… not by the faculty condition… not by the jhāna condition… not by the path condition… not by the association condition… not by the dissociation condition (three)… not by the non-absence condition… not by the non-disappearance condition.

15. Nahetuyā dve, naārammaṇe pañca, naadhipatiyā cha, naanantare pañca, nasamanantare pañca, naaññamaññe pañca, naupanissaye pañca, napurejāte satta, napacchājāte nava, naāsevane satta, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, naāhāre ekaṃ, naindriye ekaṃ, najhāne ekaṃ, namagge ekaṃ, nasampayutte pañca, navippayutte tīṇi, nonatthiyā pañca, novigate pañca (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ)[T 2.0330].

15. Not by root condition, two; not by object condition, five; not by dominance condition, six; not by contiguity condition, five; not by immediate contiguity condition, five; not by mutuality condition, five; not by decisive support condition, five; not by prenascent condition, seven; not by postnascent condition, nine; not by repetition condition, seven; not by kamma condition, three; not by result condition, nine; not by nutriment condition, one; not by faculty condition, one; not by jhāna condition, one; not by path condition, one; not by association condition, five; not by dissociation condition, three; not by non-absence condition, five; not by non-disappearance condition, five (thus should it be reckoned).

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negative

Hetudukaṃ

The Root Dyad

16. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe pañca, naadhipatiyā cha, naanantare pañca, nasamanantare pañca, naaññamaññe pañca, naupanissaye pañca, napurejāte satta[M 2.0246], napacchājāte nava, naāsevane satta, nakamme tīṇi, navipāke nava, nasampayutte pañca, navippayutte tīṇi, nonatthiyā pañca, novigate pañca (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

16. By the root condition: five are not by the object condition, six are not by the dominance condition, five are not by the contiguity condition, five are not by the immediate contiguity condition, five are not by the mutuality condition, five are not by the decisive support condition, seven are not by the prenascent condition, nine are not by the postnascent condition, seven are not by the repetition condition, three are not by the kamma condition, nine are not by the result condition, five are not by the association condition, three are not by the dissociation condition, five are not by the non-absence condition, five are not by the non-disappearance condition (thus should it be reckoned).

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

The Affirmative-Negative

The Non-Root Dyad

17. Nahetupaccayā [V 2.0277] ārammaṇe dve, anantare dve, samanantare dve, sahajāte dve, aññamaññe nissaye upanissaye purejāte āsevane kamme dve, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre dve, indriye dve, jhāne dve, magge ekaṃ, sampayutte dve, vippayutte atthiyā natthiyā vigate avigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

17. By the non-root condition: two by object, two by contiguity, two by immediate contiguity, two by co-nascence, two by mutuality, two by support, two by decisive support, two by pre-nascence, two by repetition, two by kamma; one by result; two by nutriment, two by faculty, two by jhāna; one by path; two by association, two by dissociation, two by presence, two by absence, two by disappearance, two by non-disappearance (thus should it be reckoned).

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.
