Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition.

45. Ācayagāmī ācayagāmi (sī. syā.) evamuparipi dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

45. A state tending to accumulation is a condition for a state tending to accumulation by way of root condition. The roots tending to accumulation are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī hetū cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state tending to accumulation is a condition for a state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline by way of root condition. Roots tending to accumulation are a condition for mind-originated material forms by way of root condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī [V 2.0293] dhammo ācayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state tending to accumulation is a condition for a state tending to accumulation and for a state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline by way of root condition. Roots tending to accumulation are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material forms by way of root condition. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A state tending to decline is a condition for a state tending to decline by way of root condition… three.

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa [T 2.0344] dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline is a condition for a state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline by way of root condition. Roots that neither tend to accumulation nor to decline are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material forms by way of root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots that neither tend to accumulation nor to decline are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced material forms by way of root condition. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

46. Ācayagāmī [M 2.0259] dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati. Sekkhā pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā ācayagāmī khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi…pe… vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, cetopariyañāṇena ācayagāmicittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānanti, ākāsānañcāyatanakusalaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanakusalassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanakusalaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusalassa…pe… ācayagāmī khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

46. A state tending to accumulation is a condition for a state tending to accumulation by way of object condition. Having given a gift, undertaken moral virtue, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews it; one reviews past good deeds; having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna. Trainees review the abandoned defilements, review the suppressed defilements, and know the previously arisen defilements. Trainees or worldlings contemplate the aggregates tending to accumulation as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; they savor and delight in them, and taking that as object, lust arises, wrong view…pe… doubt…pe… restlessness…pe… sorrow arises. By means of the knowledge of others' minds, they know the mind of one endowed with a mind tending to accumulation. The wholesome consciousness of the sphere of infinite space is a condition for the wholesome consciousness of the sphere of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The wholesome consciousness of the sphere of nothingness is a condition for the wholesome consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception…pe… The aggregates tending to accumulation are a condition for the knowledge of psychic power, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma, and the knowledge of the future by way of object condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – arahā pahīne kilese paccavekkhati, pubbe [T 2.0345] samudāciṇṇe kilese jānāti, ācayagāmī khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati; cetopariyañāṇena ācayagāmicittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti[V 2.0294]. Sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā ācayagāmī khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, kusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, ācayagāmī khandhe assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, akusale niruddhe vipāko tadārammaṇatā uppajjati, ākāsānañcāyatanakusalaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanavipākassa ca kiriyassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanakusalaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanavipākassa ca kiriyassa ca ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ācayagāmī khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state tending to accumulation is a condition for a state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline by way of object condition. An arahant reviews the abandoned defilements, knows the previously arisen defilements, and contemplates the aggregates tending to accumulation as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; by means of the knowledge of others' minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a mind tending to accumulation. Trainees or worldlings contemplate the aggregates tending to accumulation as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. When a wholesome state has ceased, resultant consciousness arises registering that object. One savors and delights in the aggregates tending to accumulation, and taking that as object, lust arises…pe… sorrow arises. When an unwholesome state has ceased, resultant consciousness arises registering that object. The wholesome consciousness of the sphere of infinite space is a condition for the resultant and functional consciousness of the sphere of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The wholesome consciousness of the sphere of nothingness is a condition for the resultant and functional consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object condition. The aggregates tending to accumulation are a condition for the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting by way of object condition. (2)

47. Apacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – sekkhā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, cetopariyañāṇena apacayagāmicittasamaṅgissa [M 2.0260] cittaṃ jānanti, apacayagāmī khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

47. A state tending to decline is a condition for a state tending to accumulation by way of object condition. Trainees, having emerged from the path, review the path; by means of the knowledge of others' minds, they know the mind of one endowed with a mind tending to decline. The aggregates tending to decline are a condition for the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of the future by way of object condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – arahā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhati[T 2.0346], cetopariyañāṇena apacayagāmicittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, apacayagāmī khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state tending to decline is a condition for a state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline by way of object condition. An arahant, having emerged from the path, reviews the path; by means of the knowledge of others' minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a mind tending to decline. The aggregates tending to decline are a condition for the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting by way of object condition. (2)

48. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – arahā phalaṃ paccavekkhati, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhati, nibbānaṃ phalassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Arahā cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, sotaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena nevācayagāmināpacayagāmicittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanakiriyaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanakiriyassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanakiriyaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakiriyassa…pe… rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā [V 2.0295] iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

48. A state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline is a condition for a state that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline by way of object condition. An arahant reviews fruition, reviews Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for the adverting of fruition by way of object condition. An arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, the ear…pe… the physical basis…pe… the aggregates that neither tend to accumulation nor to decline as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; with the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear element, one hears sounds; by means of the knowledge of others' minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with a mind that neither tends to accumulation nor to decline. The functional consciousness of the sphere of infinite space is a condition for the functional consciousness of the sphere of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The functional consciousness of the sphere of nothingness is a condition for the functional consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception…pe… The visible object base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… The tangible object base is a condition for body-consciousness…pe… The aggregates that neither tend to accumulation nor to decline are a condition for the knowledge of psychic power, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting by way of object condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – sekkhā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo[T 2.0347]. Sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Sotaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ…pe… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passanti, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇanti, cetopariyañāṇena [M 2.0261] nevācayagāmināpacayagāmicittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānanti, nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative is a condition for an accumulative state by way of object condition. Trainees reflect on the fruition, they reflect on Nibbāna; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage and for purification by way of object condition. Trainees or ordinary people contemplate the eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self; they savor and delight in it; taking that as object, lust arises… sorrow arises. The ear… the base… They contemplate the aggregates that are neither accumulative nor dissipative as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self; they savor and delight in them; taking them as object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt… restlessness… sorrow… With the divine eye, they see forms; with the divine ear-element, they hear sounds; with the knowledge of others' minds, they know the mind of one endowed with a mind that is neither accumulative nor dissipative. The aggregates that are neither accumulative nor dissipative are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the recollection of past lives, and the knowledge of the future by way of object condition. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ maggassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative is a condition for a dissipative state by way of object condition. Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of object condition. (3)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

49. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, ācayagāmī khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – ācayagāmī adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ [T 2.0348] adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

49. An accumulative state is a condition for an accumulative state by way of dominance condition: by object dominance and conascence dominance. Object dominance: Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it, regarding it as important; one reflects on previously performed good actions, regarding them as important; having emerged from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna, regarding it as important; one savors and delights in the accumulative aggregates, regarding them as important; regarding that as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. Conascence dominance: An accumulative dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati [V 2.0296] – ācayagāmī adhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulative state is a condition for a state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative by way of dominance condition. Conascence dominance: An accumulative dominant factor is a condition for mind-originated material form by way of dominance condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – ācayagāmī adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

An accumulative state is a condition for an accumulative state and for a state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative by way of dominance condition. Conascence dominance: An accumulative dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material form by way of dominance condition. (3)

50. Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – apacayagāmī adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

50. A dissipative state is a condition for a dissipative state by way of dominance condition. Conascence dominance: A dissipative dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – sekkhā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. (2)

A dissipative state is a condition for an accumulative state by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Trainees, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path, regarding it as important. (2)

Apacayagāmī [M 2.0262] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – arahā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati. Sahajātādhipati – apacayagāmī adhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A dissipative state is a condition for a state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative by way of dominance condition: by object dominance and conascence dominance. Object dominance: An arahant, having emerged from the path, reflects on the path, regarding it as important. Conascence dominance: A dissipative dominant factor is a condition for mind-originated material form by way of dominance condition. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – apacayagāmī [T 2.0349] adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (4)

A dissipative state is a condition for a dissipative state and for a state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative by way of dominance condition. Conascence dominance: A dissipative dominant factor is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material form by way of dominance condition. (4)

51. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – arahā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, nibbānaṃ phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

51. A state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative is a condition for a state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative by way of dominance condition: by object dominance and conascence dominance. Object dominance: An arahant reflects on the fruition, regarding it as important; reflects on Nibbāna, regarding it as important; Nibbāna is a condition for the fruition by way of dominance condition. Conascence dominance: A dominant factor that is neither accumulative nor dissipative is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated material form by way of dominance condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [V 2.0297] dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – sekkhā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti…pe… vatthuṃ… nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati; taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

A state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative is a condition for an accumulative state by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Trainees reflect on the fruition, regarding it as important; they reflect on Nibbāna, regarding it as important; Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage and for purification by way of dominance condition. One savors the eye, regarding it as important… the base… one savors and delights in the aggregates that are neither accumulative nor dissipative, regarding them as important; regarding that as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – nibbānaṃ maggassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state that is neither accumulative nor dissipative is a condition for a dissipative state by way of dominance condition. Object dominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of dominance condition. (3)

Anantarapaccayo

Contiguity Condition

52. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā ācayagāmī khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ [T 2.0350] ācayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

52. An accumulative state is a condition for an accumulative state by way of contiguity condition. Preceding accumulative aggregates are a condition for subsequent accumulative aggregates by way of contiguity condition. Conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage… conformity is a condition for purification by way of contiguity condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī [M 2.0263] dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulating state is a condition for a dissipating state by way of the contiguity condition: change-of-lineage is a condition for the path... purification is a condition for the path by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Sekkhānaṃ anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā, nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakusalaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An accumulating state is a condition for a state that is neither accumulating nor dissipating by way of the contiguity condition: the accumulating aggregates are a condition for emergence by way of the contiguity condition. For trainees, conformity is a condition for fruition attainment; for one emerging from cessation, the wholesome consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition attainment by way of the contiguity condition. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – maggo phalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A dissipating state is a condition for a state that is neither accumulating nor dissipating by way of the contiguity condition: the path is a condition for the fruition by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nevācayagāmināpacayagāmīnaṃ [V 2.0298] khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Bhavaṅgaṃ āvajjanāya… kiriyaṃ vuṭṭhānassa… arahato anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanakiriyaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state that is neither accumulating nor dissipating is a condition for a state that is neither accumulating nor dissipating by way of the contiguity condition: preceding states that are neither accumulating nor dissipating are a condition for subsequent states that are neither accumulating nor dissipating by way of the contiguity condition. The life-continuum is a condition for adverting... functional consciousness is a condition for emergence... for an arahant, conformity is a condition for fruition attainment... for one emerging from cessation, the functional consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition attainment by way of the contiguity condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – āvajjanā ācayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state that is neither accumulating nor dissipating is a condition for an accumulating state by way of the contiguity condition: adverting is a condition for the accumulating aggregates by way of the contiguity condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayādi

Immediately Contiguous Condition, etc.

53. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena [T 2.0351] paccayo…pe… (anantarasadisaṃ). (Sahajātapaccaye paṭiccavāre sahajātavārasadisā nava pañhā. Aññamaññapaccaye paṭiccavāre aññamaññasadisaṃ tīṇi. Nissayapaccaye paccayavāre nissayavārasadisaṃ. Cattāripi hi visuṃ ghaṭanā natthi. Terasa pañhā.)

53. An accumulating state is a condition for an accumulating state by way of the immediately contiguous condition... (similar to the contiguity condition). (In the Co-nascence Condition, in the Dependent Section, nine questions are similar to those in the Co-nascence Section. In the Mutuality Condition, in the Dependent Section, three are similar to the Mutuality Section. In the Dependence Condition, in the Condition Section, it is similar to the Dependence Section. For these four, there is no separate treatment. Thirteen questions.)

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

54. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ācayagāmiṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… vipassanaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ [M 2.0264] uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti, ācayagāmiṃ sīlaṃ… sutaṃ… cāgaṃ… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ… dosaṃ… mohaṃ… mānaṃ… diṭṭhiṃ… patthanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti. Sīlaṃ…pe… uposathakammaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… vipassanaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ…pe… pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Ācayagāmī saddhā…pe… paññā, rāgo…pe… patthanā ācayagāmiyā saddhāya…pe… paññāya, rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Paṭhamassa jhānassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa jhānassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo…pe…. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ dutiyassa jhānassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

54. An accumulating state is a condition for an accumulating state by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: Relying on accumulating faith, one gives a gift, observes morality... observes the Uposatha... develops jhāna... develops insight... attains higher knowledge... attains a meditative attainment, harbors conceit, grasps a view. Relying on accumulating morality... learning... generosity... wisdom... lust... hatred... delusion... conceit... a view... an aspiration, one gives a gift... observes morality... observes the Uposatha... develops jhāna... develops insight... attains higher knowledge... attains a meditative attainment... kills a living being... creates a schism in the Saṅgha. Accumulating faith... wisdom, lust... aspiration is a condition for accumulating faith... wisdom, for lust... for an aspiration by way of the decisive support condition. The preparatory work for the first jhāna is a condition for the first jhāna by way of the decisive support condition... The preparatory work for the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of the decisive support condition. The first jhāna is a condition for the second jhāna... the sphere of nothingness is a condition for the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī [V 2.0299] dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena [T 2.0352] paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – paṭhamassa maggassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa maggassa…pe… catutthassa maggassa parikammaṃ catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulating state is a condition for a dissipating state by way of the decisive support condition—contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: The preparatory work for the first path is a condition for the first path... the preparatory work for the fourth path is a condition for the fourth path by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ācayagāmiṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti pariyiṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Ācayagāmiṃ sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ. Rāgaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti pariyiṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Ācayagāmī saddhā…pe… paññā. Rāgo…pe… patthanā, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An accumulating state is a condition for a state that is neither accumulating nor dissipating by way of the decisive support condition—contiguity decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: Relying on accumulating faith, one torments and afflicts oneself, experiencing suffering rooted in seeking. Relying on accumulating morality... wisdom... lust... aspiration, one torments and afflicts oneself, experiencing suffering rooted in seeking. Accumulating faith... wisdom, lust... aspiration is a condition for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, and for fruition attainment by way of the decisive support condition. Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its fruit by way of the decisive support condition. (3)

55. Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – paṭhamo maggo dutiyassa maggassa…pe… tatiyo maggo catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

55. A dissipating state is a condition for a dissipating state by way of the decisive support condition. Natural decisive support: The first path is a condition for the second path... the third path is a condition for the fourth path by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – sekkhā maggaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ kusalasamāpattiṃ uppādenti, uppannaṃ samāpajjanti[M 2.0265], saṅkhāre aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, maggo sekkhānaṃ atthappaṭisambhidāya…pe… [T 2.0353] paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāya ṭhānāṭhānakosallassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A dissipating state is a condition for an accumulating state by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: Trainees, relying on the path, produce unarisen wholesome attainments, enter into arisen ones, and contemplate formations as impermanent, suffering, and not-self. The path is a condition for the trainees’ analytical knowledge of meaning... analytical knowledge of ready-wittedness, and skill in possibilities and impossibilities by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Apacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – arahā maggaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ kiriyasamāpattiṃ uppādeti, uppannaṃ samāpajjati…pe… ṭhānāṭhānakosallassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Maggo phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon leading to decline is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: The Arahant, relying on the path, gives rise to unarisen functional attainment, enters into arisen attainment... is a condition by way of decisive support condition for skill in possibilities and impossibilities. The path is a condition for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (3)

56. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [V 2.0300] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti pariyiṭṭhimūlakaṃ dukkhaṃ paccanubhoti. Kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya attānaṃ ātāpeti paritāpeti…pe… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utu… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Arahā kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ kiriyasamāpattiṃ uppādeti…pe… vipassati. Kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya…pe… vipassati. (1)

56. A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: Relying on bodily pleasure, one torments and afflicts oneself, experiencing suffering rooted in seeking. Relying on bodily pain... climate... food... lodging, one torments and afflicts oneself... Bodily pleasure... bodily pain... climate... food... lodging are conditions for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. The Arahant, relying on bodily pleasure, gives rise to unarisen functional attainment... contemplates with insight. Relying on bodily pain... climate... food... lodging... contemplates with insight. (1)

Nevācayagāmīnāpacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…[T 2.0354]. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ ācayagāmiyā saddhāya…pe… paññāya, rāgassa…pe… patthanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: Relying on bodily pleasure, one gives a gift... gives rise to attainment, kills a living being... creates a schism in the Saṅgha. Relying on bodily pain... climate... food... lodging, one gives a gift... creates a schism in the Saṅgha. Bodily pleasure... lodging is a condition by way of decisive support condition for accumulating faith... for wisdom, for lust... for aspiration. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ upanissāya maggaṃ uppādeti. Kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ [M 2.0266] …pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya maggaṃ uppādeti, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ, kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon leading to decline by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, natural decisive support... Natural decisive support: Relying on bodily pleasure, one gives rise to the path. Relying on bodily pain... lodging, one gives rise to the path. Bodily pleasure, bodily pain... lodging is a condition for the path by way of decisive support condition. (3)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition.

57. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – arahā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ [V 2.0301] kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nevācayagāmināpacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

57. A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: An Arahant contemplates the eye… the base as impermanent, suffering, and not-self; with the divine eye one sees forms; with the divine ear-element one hears sounds; the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: The eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness… the base is a condition for the aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [T 2.0355] dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu ācayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: Trainees or worldlings contemplate the eye… the base as impermanent, suffering, and not-self; they savor and delight in it. Taking that as object, lust arises… grief arises. With the divine eye one sees forms; with the divine ear-element one hears sounds. Base pre-nascence: The base is a condition for the accumulating aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu apacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon leading to decline by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: The base is a condition for the aggregates leading to decline by way of pre-nascence condition. (3)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition.

58. Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā ācayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

58. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of post-nascence condition—the subsequently arisen accumulating aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā apacayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon leading to decline is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of post-nascence condition—the subsequently arisen aggregates leading to decline are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [M 2.0267] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo.

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of post-nascence condition—the subsequently arisen aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of post-nascence condition.

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition.

59. Ācayagāmī [T 2.0356][V 2.0302] dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā ācayagāmī khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ ācayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

59. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of repetition condition—the preceding accumulating aggregates are a condition for the succeeding accumulating aggregates by way of repetition condition. Adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage… adaptation is a condition for purification by way of repetition condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon leading to decline by way of repetition condition—change-of-lineage is a condition for the path… purification is a condition for the path by way of repetition condition. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ nevācayagāmināpacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of repetition condition—the preceding aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for the succeeding aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining by way of repetition condition. (1)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

60. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

60. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of kamma condition—accumulating volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – ācayagāmī cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – ācayagāmī cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of kamma condition—co-nascent and non-co-nascent. Co-nascent: Accumulating volition is a condition for mind-originated matter by way of kamma condition. Non-co-nascent: Accumulating volition is a condition for resultant aggregates and for kamma-produced matter by way of kamma condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa [T 2.0357] ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for both an accumulating phenomenon and a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of kamma condition—accumulating volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of kamma condition. (3)

61. Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – apacayagāmī cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

61. A declining phenomenon is a condition for a declining phenomenon by way of kamma condition—declining volition is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī [M 2.0268][V 2.0303] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – apacayagāmī cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – apacayagāmī cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A declining phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of kamma condition—co-nascent and non-co-nascent. Co-nascent: Declining volition is a condition for mind-originated matter by way of kamma condition. Non-co-nascent: Declining volition is a condition for resultant aggregates by way of kamma condition. (2)

Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – apacayagāmī cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A declining phenomenon is a condition for both a declining phenomenon and a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of kamma condition—declining volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of kamma condition. (3)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of kamma condition—volition that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of kamma condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, volition that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced matter by way of kamma condition. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Resultant Condition

62. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī [T 2.0358] eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa vipākapaccayena paccayo. (1)

62. A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of resultant condition—one resultant aggregate that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for the other three aggregates… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on… the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of resultant condition. (1)

Āhārapaccayādi

Nutriment Condition, etc.

63. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo.

63. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition… by way of jhāna condition… by way of path condition… by way of association condition.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

64. Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo [V 2.0304] – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – ācayagāmī khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ācayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

64. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent and post-nascent. Co-nascent: The accumulating aggregates are a condition for mind-originated matter by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: The accumulating aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī [M 2.0269] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – apacayagāmī khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – apacayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A declining phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent and post-nascent. Co-nascent: The declining aggregates are a condition for mind-originated matter by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: The declining aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo[T 2.0359]. Khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nevācayagāmināpacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa…pe…. (1)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent, pre-nascent, and post-nascent. Co-nascent: The aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for mind-originated matter by way of dissociation condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for kamma-produced matter by way of dissociation condition. The aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of dissociation condition. The physical basis is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness… and so on… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness… and so on… the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: The aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for this pre-nascent body… and so on…. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu ācayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: The physical basis is a condition for the accumulating aggregates by way of dissociation condition. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu apacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a declining phenomenon by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascent: The physical basis is a condition for the declining aggregates by way of dissociation condition. (3)

Atthipaccayādi

Presence Condition, etc.

65. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe…. (1)

65. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of presence condition—one accumulating aggregate is a condition for the other three aggregates… and so on…. (1)

Ācayagāmī [V 2.0305] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – ācayagāmī khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ācayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of presence condition—co-arisen and post-arisen. Co-arisen: The accumulating aggregates are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence condition. Post-arisen: The accumulating aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of presence condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī [M 2.0270] dhammo ācayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – ācayagāmī eko khandho [T 2.0360] tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe…. (3)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon and a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of presence condition—one accumulating aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence condition…pe… two aggregates…pe…. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhammo… tīṇi (ācayagāminayena kātabbaṃ).

A declining phenomenon… three (should be done in the manner of the accumulating method).

66. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa atthipaccayena paccayo. Vatthu khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ…pe…. Purejātaṃ – arahā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu nevācayagāmināpacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ…pe…. (1)

66. A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of presence condition—co-arisen, pre-arisen, post-arisen, nutriment, and faculty. Co-arisen: One aggregate that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence condition…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the linking moment of rebirth…pe… the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of presence condition. The physical basis is a condition for the aggregates by way of presence condition. One great primary element…pe… external… nutriment-produced… temperature-produced… for non-percipient beings…pe…. Pre-arisen: An arahant sees the eye…pe… the physical basis as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, sees forms with the divine eye, hears sounds with the divine ear-element, the visible object basis is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the tangible object basis is a condition for body-consciousness…pe… the eye-basis is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body-basis is a condition for body-consciousness…pe… the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining by way of presence condition. Post-arisen: The aggregates that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of presence condition. Edible nutriment is a condition for this body…pe… the material life-faculty is a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena…pe…. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – sekkhā vā puthujjanā vā cakkhuṃ aniccato [T 2.0361] dukkhato anattato vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha rāgo…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, sotaṃ…pe… vatthuṃ [V 2.0306] aniccato…pe… vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti; taṃ ārabbha rāgo…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, vatthu ācayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by way of presence condition. Pre-arisen: Trainees or ordinary persons regard the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, delight in it, rejoice in it; based on that, lust…pe… grief arises; the ear…pe… the physical basis…pe… regard as impermanent…pe… delight in it, rejoice in it; based on that, lust…pe… grief arises; sees forms with the divine eye, hears sounds with the divine ear-element, the physical basis is a condition for the accumulating aggregates by way of presence condition. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu apacayagāmīnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining is a condition for a declining phenomenon by way of presence condition. Pre-arisen: The physical basis is a condition for the declining aggregates by way of presence condition. (3)

67. Ācayagāmī [M 2.0271] ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā ācayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – ācayagāmī eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe…. (1)

67. Accumulating phenomena and phenomena that are neither accumulating nor declining are conditions for an accumulating phenomenon by way of presence condition—co-arisen and pre-arisen. Co-arisen: One accumulating aggregate and the physical basis are a condition for the three aggregates by way of presence condition…pe… two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Ācayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – ācayagāmī khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ācayagāmī khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ācayagāmī khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

Accumulating phenomena and phenomena that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by way of presence condition—co-arisen, post-arisen, nutriment, and faculty. Co-arisen: Accumulating aggregates and the great primary elements are a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of presence condition. Post-arisen: Accumulating aggregates and edible nutriment are a condition for this body by way of presence condition. Post-arisen: Accumulating aggregates and the material life-faculty are a condition for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of presence condition. (2)

Apacayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā apacayagāmissa [T 2.0362] dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (dve kātabbā dassitanayena), natthipaccayena paccayo, vigatapaccayena paccayo, avigatapaccayena paccayo.

Declining phenomena and phenomena that are neither accumulating nor declining are a condition for a declining phenomenon by way of presence condition (two should be done in the manner shown), a condition by way of absence condition, a condition by way of disappearance condition, and a condition by way of non-disappearance condition.

68. Hetuyā satta, ārammaṇe satta, adhipatiyā dasa, anantare cha, samanantare cha, sahajāte [V 2.0307] nava, aññamaññe tīṇi, nissaye terasa, upanissaye nava, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane tīṇi, kamme satta, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre satta, indriye satta, jhāne satta, magge satta, sampayutte tīṇi, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā terasa, natthiyā cha, vigate cha, avigate terasa.

68. By root condition, seven; by object condition, seven; by dominance condition, ten; by contiguity condition, six; by immediate contiguity condition, six; by co-nascence condition, nine; by reciprocity condition, three; by dependence condition, thirteen; by decisive support condition, nine; by pre-nascence condition, three; by post-nascence condition, three; by repetition condition, three; by kamma condition, seven; by result condition, one; by nutriment condition, seven; by faculty condition, seven; by jhāna condition, seven; by path condition, seven; by association condition, three; by dissociation condition, five; by presence condition, thirteen; by absence condition, six; by disappearance condition, six; by non-disappearance condition, thirteen.

Conformity.

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Section on Negation

69. Ācayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

69. An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for an accumulating phenomenon by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition. (1)

Ācayagāmī [M 2.0272] dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a declining phenomenon by decisive support condition. (2)

Ācayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition for a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by post-nascence condition… by kamma condition. (3)

Ācayagāmī [T 2.0363] dhammo ācayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (4)

An accumulating phenomenon is a condition by co-nascence condition for both an accumulating phenomenon and a phenomenon that is neither accumulating nor declining. (4)

70. Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

70. A depletive state is a condition for a depletive state by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition. (1)

Apacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A depletive state is a condition for an accumulative state by object condition… by decisive support condition. (2)

Apacayagāmī [V 2.0308] dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A depletive state is a condition for a neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by post-nascence condition. (3)

Apacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (4)

A depletive state is a condition for a depletive state and a neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state by co-nascence condition. (4)

71. Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

71. A neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state is a condition for a neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by decisive support condition… by pre-nascence condition… by post-nascence condition… by nutriment condition… by faculty condition. (1)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo ācayagāmissa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state is a condition for an accumulative state by object condition… by decisive support condition… by pre-nascence condition. (2)

Nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī dhammo apacayagāmissa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena [T 2.0364] paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state is a condition for a depletive state by decisive support condition… by pre-nascence condition. (3)

72. Ācayagāmī [M 2.0273] ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā ācayagāmissa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. (1)

72. Accumulative and neither-accumulative-nor-depletive states are conditions for an accumulative state by co-nascence, by pre-nascence. (1)

Ācayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

Accumulative and neither-accumulative-nor-depletive states are conditions for a neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state by co-nascence, by post-nascence, by nutriment, by faculty. (2)

Apacayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā apacayagāmissa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. (1)

Depletive and neither-accumulative-nor-depletive states are conditions for a depletive state by co-nascence, by pre-nascence. (1)

Apacayagāmī ca nevācayagāmināpacayagāmī ca dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmissa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

Depletive and neither-accumulative-nor-depletive states are conditions for a neither-accumulative-nor-depletive state by co-nascence, by post-nascence, by nutriment, by faculty.

73. Nahetuyā [V 2.0309] pannarasa, naārammaṇe naadhipatiyā naanantare nasamanantare pannarasa, nasahajāte ekādasa, naaññamaññe ekādasa, nanissaye ekādasa, naupanissaye cuddasa, napurejāte terasa, napacchājāte pannarasa, naāsevane nakamme navipāke naāhāre naindriye najhāne namagge pannarasa, nasampayutte ekādasa, navippayutte nava, noatthiyā nava, nonatthiyā pannarasa, novigate pannarasa, noavigate nava (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

73. By non-root, fifteen; by non-object, by non-dominance, by non-contiguity, by non-immediate contiguity, fifteen; by non-co-nascence, eleven; by non-reciprocity, eleven; by non-dependence, eleven; by non-decisive support, fourteen; by non-pre-nascence, thirteen; by non-post-nascence, fifteen; by non-repetition, by non-kamma, by non-result, by non-nutriment, by non-faculty, by non-jhāna, by non-path, fifteen; by non-association, eleven; by non-dissociation, nine; by non-presence, nine; by non-absence, fifteen; by non-disappearance, fifteen; by non-non-disappearance, nine (thus it should be reckoned).

By root condition, not by object, seven; not by dominance, not by contiguity, not by immediate contiguity, seven; not by reciprocity, three; not by decisive support, seven; not by pre-nascence, not by post-nascence, not by repetition, not by kamma, not by result, not by nutriment, not by faculty, not by jhāna, not by path, seven; not by association, three; not by dissociation, three; not by absence, seven; not by disappearance, seven (thus it should be reckoned).

By non-root condition, by object, seven; by dominance, ten; by contiguity, six; by immediate contiguity, six; by co-nascence, nine; by reciprocity, three; by dependence, thirteen; by decisive support, nine; by pre-nascence, three; by post-nascence, three; by repetition, three; by kamma, seven; by result, one; by nutriment, seven; by faculty, by jhāna, by path, seven; by association, three; by dissociation, five; by presence, thirteen; by absence, six; by disappearance, six; by non-disappearance, thirteen (thus it should be reckoned).
