19. Conditioned by an indeterminate phenomenon, an indeterminate phenomenon arises by non-root condition—conditioned by one rootless indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated materiality… conditioned by two aggregates… at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking… conditioned by the aggregates, the base; conditioned by the base, the aggregates. Conditioned by one great element… for non-percipient beings… conditioned by the eye-base, eye-consciousness… conditioned by the body-base, body-consciousness. Conditioned by the base, rootless indeterminate aggregates. Conditioned by the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness and the base, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Naārammaṇapaccayo

Non-object Condition

20. Micchattaniyataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā aniyato dhammo uppajjati naārammaṇapaccayā – micchattaniyate khandhe paccayā cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ (kusalattikasadisaṃ, pañca kātabbā).

20. A state fixed in wrongness conditions an indeterminate state to arise by way of non-object condition. The aggregates fixed in wrongness condition mind-originated materiality (similar to the wholesome triad; five should be done).

Naadhipatipaccayo

Non-domination Condition

21. Micchattaniyataṃ [M 2.0367] dhammaṃ paccayā micchattaniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – micchattaniyate khandhe paccayā micchattaniyatādhipati. (1)

21. A state fixed in wrongness conditions a state fixed in wrongness to arise by way of non-domination condition. The aggregates fixed in wrongness condition the dominating factor fixed in wrongness. (1)

Sammattaniyataṃ [T 2.0483] dhammaṃ paccayā sammattaniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – sammattaniyate khandhe paccayā sammattaniyatādhipati. (1)

A state fixed in rightness conditions a state fixed in rightness to arise by way of non-domination condition. The aggregates fixed in rightness condition the dominating factor fixed in rightness. (1)

Aniyataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā aniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – aniyataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paccayā tayo khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe [V 2.0425] …pe… asaññasattānaṃ…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ paccayā cakkhuviññāṇaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ paccayā kāyaviññāṇaṃ. Vatthuṃ paccayā aniyatā khandhā. (1)

An indeterminate state conditions an indeterminate state to arise by way of non-domination condition. One indeterminate aggregate conditions three aggregates and mind-originated materiality... two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking... for non-percipient beings... the eye-base conditions eye-consciousness... the body-base conditions body-consciousness. The base conditions indeterminate aggregates. (1)

Aniyataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā micchattaniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā micchattaniyatādhipati. (2)

An indeterminate state conditions a state fixed in wrongness to arise by way of non-domination condition. The base conditions the dominating factor fixed in wrongness. (2)

Aniyataṃ dhammaṃ paccayā sammattaniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – vatthuṃ paccayā sammattaniyatādhipati. (3)

An indeterminate state conditions a state fixed in rightness to arise by way of non-domination condition. The base conditions the dominating factor fixed in rightness. (3)

Micchattaniyatañca aniyatañca dhammaṃ paccayā micchattaniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – micchattaniyate khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā micchattaniyatādhipati. (1)

A state fixed in wrongness and an indeterminate state condition a state fixed in wrongness to arise by way of non-domination condition. The aggregates fixed in wrongness and the base condition the dominating factor fixed in wrongness. (1)

Sammattaniyatañca aniyatañca dhammaṃ paccayā sammattaniyato dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā – sammattaniyate khandhe ca vatthuñca paccayā sammattaniyatādhipati. (1)

A state fixed in rightness and an indeterminate state condition a state fixed in rightness to arise by way of non-domination condition. The aggregates fixed in rightness and the base condition the dominating factor fixed in rightness. (1)

An indeterminate state, associated with an indeterminate state, arises by way of non-dissociation condition—in the immaterial realm, a single indeterminate aggregate, associated with three aggregates... two aggregates... (1)

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition.

36. Micchattaniyato [V 2.0431] dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyatā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

36. A phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for a phenomenon fixed in wrongness by way of root condition—roots fixed in wrongness are a condition for the associated aggregates by way of root condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo [T 2.0488] – micchattaniyatā hetū cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of root condition—roots fixed in wrongness are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (2)

Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyatā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (3)

A phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for a phenomenon fixed in wrongness and an indeterminate phenomenon by way of root condition—roots fixed in wrongness are a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. (3)

Sammattaniyato [M 2.0372] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo… tīṇi.

A phenomenon fixed in rightness is a condition for a phenomenon fixed in rightness by way of root condition…three.

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – aniyatā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of root condition—indeterminate roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of root condition. At the moment of relinking…and so on. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition.

37. Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā micchattaniyate pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Micchattaniyate khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassanti. Cetopariyañāṇena micchattaniyatacittasamaṅgissa [V 2.0432] cittaṃ jānanti. Micchattaniyatā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

37. A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object condition. The noble ones review the abandoned defilements fixed in wrongness; they know the defilements accumulated previously. They discern the aggregates fixed in wrongness as impermanent…and so on… With knowledge of the penetration of minds, they know the mind of one endowed with a mind fixed in wrongness. The aggregates fixed in wrongness are a condition for knowledge of the penetration of minds, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma, and knowledge of the future, for advertence, by way of object condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti. Cetopariyañāṇena sammattaniyatacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānanti. Sammattaniyatā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa[T 2.0489], āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object condition. The noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path. With knowledge of the penetration of minds, they know the mind of one endowed with a mind fixed in rightness. The aggregates fixed in rightness are a condition for knowledge of the penetration of minds, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of the future, for advertence, by way of object condition. (1)

38. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati, ariyā phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ariyā aniyate pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti. Pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… aniyate khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti, assādenti abhinandanti, taṃ ārabbha aniyato rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, cetopariyañāṇena [M 2.0373] aniyatacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Aniyatā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

38. An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object condition. Having given a gift, undertaken the precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it; one reflects on previously well-done deeds; emerging from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna; the noble ones reflect on the fruit; they reflect on Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for the change-of-lineage consciousness, the purification consciousness, the fruition consciousness, and for advertence, by way of object condition. The noble ones reflect on abandoned indeterminate defilements, reflect on suppressed defilements, and know defilements accumulated previously. They discern the eye…and so on… the base… the indeterminate aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as not-self. They savor them, delight in them, and based on that, indeterminate lust arises…and so on… sorrow arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear element, one hears sounds; with knowledge of the penetration of minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with an indeterminate mind. The base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness…and so on… the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, by way of object condition. The visible form base is a condition for eye-consciousness…and so on… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness, by way of object condition. Indeterminate aggregates are a condition for knowledge of psychic powers, knowledge of the penetration of minds, knowledge of past lives, knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma, knowledge of the future, and for advertence, by way of object condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – rūpajīvitindriyaṃ mātughātikammassa… pitughātikammassa… arahantaghātikammassa… [T 2.0490] ruhiruppādakammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Yaṃ vatthuṃ parāmasantassa micchattaniyatā khandhā uppajjanti, taṃ vatthu micchattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of object condition. The material life faculty is a condition for the kamma of matricide… patricide… killing an Arahant… causing a Buddha's blood to flow, by way of object condition. Whatever base one clings to, giving rise to aggregates fixed in wrongness—that base is a condition for the aggregates fixed in wrongness, by way of object condition. (2)

Aniyato [V 2.0433] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – nibbānaṃ maggassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of object condition. Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of object condition. (3)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition.

39. Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – micchattaniyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

39. A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: a dominant factor fixed in wrongness is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of dominance condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – micchattaniyatādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of Dominance Condition. Co-nascence Dominance: the dominance of the state fixed in wrongness is a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of Dominance Condition. (2)

Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – micchattaniyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for both a state fixed in wrongness and an indeterminate state by way of Dominance Condition. Co-nascence Dominance: the dominance of the state fixed in wrongness is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-produced material phenomena by way of Dominance Condition. (3)

40. Sammattaniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – sammattaniyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

40. A state fixed in rightness is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of Dominance Condition. Co-nascence Dominance: the dominance of a state fixed in rightness is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of Dominance Condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato [M 2.0374] dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā [T 2.0491] maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Sahajātādhipati – sammattaniyatādhipati cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of Dominance Condition—Object Dominance and Co-nascence Dominance. Object Dominance: the noble ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, regarding it as important. Co-nascence Dominance: the dominance of the state fixed in rightness is a condition for mind-produced material phenomena by way of Dominance Condition. (2)

Sammattaniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – sammattaniyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for both a state fixed in rightness and an indeterminate state by way of Dominance Condition. Co-nascence Dominance: the dominance of the state fixed in rightness is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-produced material phenomena by way of Dominance Condition. (3)

41. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati [V 2.0434] sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, jhānā…pe… ariyā phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ…pe… aniyate khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā aniyato rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – aniyatādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

41. An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of Dominance Condition—Object Dominance and Co-nascence Dominance. Object Dominance: having given alms, undertaken precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews it, regarding it as important; one reviews previously well-done deeds, regarding them as important; emerging from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna, regarding it as important…pe… the noble ones review the fruit, regarding it as important; they review Nibbāna, regarding it as important. Nibbāna is a condition for the change-of-lineage consciousness, the purification consciousness, and the fruition consciousness by way of Dominance Condition. The eye…pe… the base… regarding the indeterminate aggregates as important, one savors them, delights in them; regarding them as important, indeterminate lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence Dominance: the dominance of the indeterminate state is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-produced material phenomena by way of Dominance Condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – nibbānaṃ maggassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of Dominance Condition. Object Dominance: Nibbāna is a condition for the path by way of Dominance Condition. (2)

Anantarapaccayo

The Immediately Contiguous Condition.

42. Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyatā khandhā vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena [T 2.0492] paccayo. (1)

42. A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. The aggregates fixed in wrongness are a condition for emergence by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – maggo phalassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. The path is a condition for the fruit by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā aniyatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ aniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… phalaṃ phalassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. Earlier and earlier indeterminate aggregates are a condition for later and later indeterminate aggregates by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. Conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage… conformity is a condition for purification… the fruit is a condition for the fruit… conformity is a condition for fruition-attainment… for one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. (1)

43. Aniyato [M 2.0375] dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – aniyataṃ domanassaṃ micchattaniyatassa domanassassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Aniyatamicchādiṭṭhi niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

43. An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. Indeterminate grief is a condition for grief fixed in wrongness by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. Indeterminate wrong view is a condition for wrong view fixed in wrongness by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. (2)

Aniyato [V 2.0435] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path… purification is a condition for the path by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition. (3)

Samanantarapaccayādi

The Immediately Contiguous Condition, etc.

44. Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo (anantarasadisaṃ)… sahajātapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavārasadisaṃ, nava pañhā)… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo (paṭiccavārasadisaṃ, tisso pañhā)… nissayapaccayena paccayo (kusalattikasadisā, terasa [T 2.0493] pañhā).

44. A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the Immediately Contiguous Condition (similar to the Immediately Contiguous Condition)… by way of the Conascence Condition (similar to the section on dependent origination, nine questions)… by way of the Mutuality Condition (similar to the section on dependent origination, three questions)… by way of the Support Condition (similar to the wholesome triad, thirteen questions).

Upanissayapaccayo

The Decisive Support Condition.

45. Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – mātughātikammaṃ mātughātikammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Mātughātikammaṃ…pe… pitughātikammaṃ…pe… arahantaghātikammaṃ…pe… ruhiruppādakammaṃ…pe… saṅghabhedakammaṃ…pe… niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). Niyatamicchādiṭṭhi niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Niyatamicchādiṭṭhi mātughātikammassa…pe… saṅghabhedakammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

45. A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of the Decisive Support Condition. Natural Decisive Support: the act of matricide is a condition for the act of matricide by way of the Decisive Support Condition. The act of matricide… the act of patricide… the act of killing an arahant… the act of shedding blood… the act of causing schism in the Sangha… is a condition for wrong view fixed in wrongness by way of the Decisive Support Condition (a cycle should be made). Wrong view fixed in wrongness is a condition for wrong view fixed in wrongness by way of the Decisive Support Condition. Wrong view fixed in wrongness is a condition for the act of matricide… the act of causing schism in the Sangha by way of the Decisive Support Condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – mātaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā tassa paṭighātatthāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti. Pitaraṃ jīvitā voropetvā…pe… arahantaṃ jīvitā voropetvā…pe… duṭṭhena cittena tathāgatassa lohitaṃ uppādetvā…pe… saṅghaṃ bhinditvā tassa paṭighātatthāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti. (2)

A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for an unfixed state by way of the decisive support condition—immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: having killed one's mother, one gives gifts, undertakes precepts, or performs the Uposatha observance to counteract that act. Having killed one's father… and so on… having killed an arahant… and so on… having maliciously caused the Tathāgata’s blood to flow… and so on… having caused schism in the Sangha, one gives gifts, undertakes precepts, or performs the Uposatha observance to counteract that act. (2)

46. Sammattaniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Pakatūpanissayo – paṭhamo maggo dutiyassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena [M 2.0376] paccayo…pe… tatiyo maggo catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

46. A state fixed in rightness is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of the decisive support condition. Natural decisive support: the first path is a condition for the second path by way of the decisive support condition… and so on… the third path is a condition for the fourth path by way of the decisive support condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato [V 2.0436] dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena [T 2.0494] paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ariyā maggaṃ upanissāya anuppannaṃ samāpattiṃ uppādenti, uppannaṃ samāpajjanti, saṅkhāre aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassanti. Maggo ariyānaṃ atthappaṭisambhidāya…pe… ṭhānāṭhānakosallassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Maggo phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for an unfixed state by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: noble ones, relying on the path, generate unarisen attainments, enter into arisen attainments, and contemplate formations as impermanent, suffering, and not-self. The path is a condition for the noble ones’ analytical knowledge of meaning… and so on… skill in understanding possibilities and impossibilities by way of the decisive support condition. The path is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

47. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – aniyataṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ… abhiññaṃ… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Aniyataṃ sīlaṃ… sutaṃ… cāgaṃ… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… nigamaghātaṃ karoti. Aniyatā saddhā…pe… paññā, rāgo…pe… senāsanaṃ aniyatāya saddhāya…pe… kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. Paṭhamassa jhānassa parikammaṃ tasseva…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ tasseva…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ dutiyassa jhānassa…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa…pe… pāṇātipāto pāṇātipātassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo (cakkaṃ kātabbaṃ). (1)

47. An unfixed state is a condition for an unfixed state by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: relying on unfixed faith, one gives gifts, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha observance… generates jhāna, develops insight… higher knowledge… generates meditative attainments, indulges in conceit, clings to views. Relying on unfixed virtue… learning… generosity… wisdom… lust… and so on… aspiration… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… climate… food… lodging, one gives gifts… and so on… plunders a town. Unfixed faith… and so on… wisdom, lust… and so on… lodging is a condition for unfixed faith… and so on… bodily pleasure, bodily pain, or fruition-attainment by way of the decisive support condition. The preliminary work for the first jhāna is a condition for the first jhāna itself… and so on… the preliminary work for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for that base itself… and so on… the first jhāna is a condition for the second jhāna… and so on… the base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception… and so on… killing living beings is a condition for killing living beings by way of the decisive support condition (a cycle should be made). (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – aniyataṃ [T 2.0495] rāgaṃ upanissāya mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Aniyataṃ dosaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya mātaraṃ jīvitā voropeti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Aniyato rāgo…pe… senāsanaṃ mātughātikammassa… pitughātikammassa… arahantaghātikammassa… ruhiruppādakammassa… saṅghabhedakammassa… niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An unfixed state is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of the decisive support condition—immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: relying on unfixed lust, one kills one's mother… and so on… causes schism in the Sangha. Relying on unfixed hatred… and so on… longing… bodily pleasure… and so on… lodging, one kills one's mother… and so on… causes schism in the Sangha. Unfixed lust… and so on… lodging is a condition for the act of matricide… the act of patricide… the act of killing an arahant… the act of causing blood to flow… the act of causing schism in the Sangha… for fixed wrong view by way of the decisive support condition. (2)

Aniyato [M 2.0377][V 2.0437] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – paṭhamassa maggassa parikammaṃ paṭhamassa maggassa…pe… catutthassa maggassa parikammaṃ catutthassa maggassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unfixed state is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of the decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: the preliminary work for the first path is a condition for the first path… and so on… the preliminary work for the fourth path is a condition for the fourth path by way of the decisive support condition. (3)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

48. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha aniyato rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu aniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

48. An unfixed state is a condition for an unfixed state by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: one sees the eye... contemplates the base as impermanent... delights in it, approves of it; dependent on that, unfixed lust arises... sorrow arises. With the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear-element, one hears a sound; the form-base is a condition for eye-consciousness... the tangible-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness... the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness... the base is a condition for unfixed aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena [T 2.0496] paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – rūpajīvitindriyaṃ mātughātikammassa… pitughātikammassa… arahantaghātikammassa… ruhiruppādakammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu micchattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An unfixed state is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of pre-nascence condition: object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: the material life faculty is a condition for the act of matricide... patricide... killing an arahant... the act of causing blood to flow, by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for aggregates fixed in wrongness by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Aniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – vatthu sammattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An unfixed state is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: the base is a condition for aggregates fixed in rightness by way of pre-nascence condition. (3)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

49. Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā micchattaniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

49. A wrongly determined phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition. Subsequently arisen wrongly determined aggregates are a condition for this pre-existent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato [V 2.0438] dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā sammattaniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A rightly determined phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition. Subsequently arisen rightly determined aggregates are a condition for this pre-existent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Aniyato [M 2.0378] dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā aniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition. Subsequently arisen indeterminate aggregates are a condition for this pre-existent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

50. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā aniyatā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ aniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ [T 2.0497] vodānassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

50. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of repetition condition. Preceding indeterminate aggregates are a condition for succeeding indeterminate aggregates by way of repetition condition. Conformity for change-of-lineage... conformity for purification is a condition by way of repetition condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – aniyataṃ domanassaṃ micchattaniyatassa domanassassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Aniyatamicchādiṭṭhi niyatamicchādiṭṭhiyā āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for a wrongly determined phenomenon by way of repetition condition. Indeterminate sorrow is a condition for wrongly determined sorrow by way of repetition condition. Indeterminate wrong view is a condition for wrongly determined wrong view by way of repetition condition. (2)

Aniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for a rightly determined phenomenon by way of repetition condition. Change-of-lineage is a condition for the path... purification is a condition for the path by way of repetition condition. (3)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

51. Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

51. A wrongly determined phenomenon is a condition for a wrongly determined phenomenon by way of kamma condition. Wrongly determined volition is a condition for associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – micchattaniyatā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – micchattaniyatā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A wrongly determined phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascent and at a different moment. Co-nascent: wrongly determined volition is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. At a different moment: wrongly determined volition is a condition for resultant aggregates and kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition. (2)

Micchattaniyato [V 2.0439] dhammo micchattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A wrongly determined phenomenon is a condition for wrongly determined and indeterminate phenomena by way of kamma condition. Wrongly determined volition is a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (3)

52. Sammattaniyato [M 2.0379] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena [T 2.0498] paccayo – sammattaniyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

52. A rightly determined phenomenon is a condition for a rightly determined phenomenon by way of kamma condition. Rightly determined volition is a condition for associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – sammattaniyatā cetanā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – sammattaniyatā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A rightly determined phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascent and at a different moment. Co-nascent: rightly determined volition is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. At a different moment: rightly determined volition is a condition for resultant aggregates by way of kamma condition. (2)

Sammattaniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sammattaniyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A rightly determined phenomenon is a condition for rightly determined and indeterminate phenomena by way of kamma condition. Rightly determined volition is a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (3)

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – aniyatā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – aniyatā cetanā vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of kamma condition: co-nascent and at a different moment. Co-nascent: indeterminate volition is a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking... etc... At a different moment: indeterminate volition is a condition for resultant aggregates and kamma-produced materiality by way of kamma condition. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Result Condition

53. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko aniyato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa…pe….

53. An indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of result condition. One indeterminate resultant aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of result condition... etc... at the moment of rebirth-linking... etc... aggregates for the base... etc.

Āhārapaccayādi

Nutriment Condition, etc.

54. Micchattaniyato [T 2.0499][V 2.0440] dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo.

54. A phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for a phenomenon fixed in wrongness by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition… by way of jhāna condition… by way of path condition… by way of association condition.

Vippayuttapaccayo

Dissociation Condition

55. Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – micchattaniyatā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – micchattaniyatā [M 2.0380] khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

55. A phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent and post-nascent. Co-nascent: Aggregates fixed in wrongness are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: Aggregates fixed in wrongness are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – sammattaniyatā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – sammattaniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon fixed in rightness is a condition for an indeterminate phenomenon by way of dissociation condition—co-nascent and post-nascent. Co-nascent: Aggregates fixed in rightness are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascent: Aggregates fixed in rightness are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – aniyatā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu aniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – aniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa [T 2.0500] vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

The indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for the indeterminate phenomenon by way of Dissociation Condition—conascence, prenascence, and postnascence. Conascent: The indeterminate aggregates are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Dissociation Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (etc.)… the aggregates are a condition for the base by way of Dissociation Condition. The base is a condition for the aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Prenascent: The eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness… (etc.)… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness… the base is a condition for the indeterminate aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Postnascent: The indeterminate aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of Dissociation Condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu micchattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (2)

The indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in wrongness by way of Dissociation Condition. Prenascent: The base is a condition for the aggregates fixed in wrongness by way of Dissociation Condition. (2)

Aniyato [V 2.0441] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu sammattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (3)

The indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in rightness by way of Dissociation Condition. Prenascent: The base is a condition for the aggregates fixed in rightness by way of Dissociation Condition. (3)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition.

56. Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

56. The phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in wrongness by way of Presence Condition. One aggregate fixed in wrongness is a condition for the three aggregates… (etc.)… two aggregates are a condition for the two aggregates by way of Presence Condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – micchattaniyatā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – micchattaniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

The phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for the indeterminate phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—conascence and postnascence. Conascent: The aggregates fixed in wrongness are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition. Postnascent: The aggregates fixed in wrongness are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of Presence Condition. (2)

Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca atthipaccayena paccayo – micchattaniyato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe…. (3)

The phenomenon fixed in wrongness is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in wrongness and the indeterminate phenomenon by way of Presence Condition. One aggregate fixed in wrongness is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition… (etc.)… two aggregates… (etc.). (3)

Sammattaniyato [M 2.0381] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… (tisso pañhā).

The phenomenon fixed in rightness is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in rightness by way of Presence Condition… (etc.)… (three questions).

Aniyato [T 2.0501] dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – aniyato eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa atthipaccayena paccayo. Vatthu khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe…. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya [V 2.0442] sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu aniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – aniyatā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

The indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for the indeterminate phenomenon by way of Presence Condition: conascence, prenascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent: One indeterminate aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition… (etc.)… two aggregates… (etc.)… at the moment of rebirth-linking… (etc.)… the aggregates are a condition for the base by way of Presence Condition. The base is a condition for the aggregates by way of Presence Condition. One great element… (etc.)… for non-percipient beings, one great element… (etc.). Prenascent: The eye… (etc.)… the base is seen as impermanent, suffering, and not-self; one savors it and delights in it, and, dependent on that, craving arises… (etc.)… sorrow arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds; the visible form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… (etc.)… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness… (etc.)… the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness… (etc.)… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness… the base is a condition for the indeterminate aggregates by way of Presence Condition. Postnascent: The indeterminate aggregates are a condition for this pre-arisen body by way of Presence Condition. Nutriment: Physical food is a condition for this body by way of Presence Condition. Faculty: The material life faculty is a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of Presence Condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – rūpajīvitindriyaṃ mātughātikammassa…pe… ruhiruppādakammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Vatthu micchattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

The indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in wrongness by way of Presence Condition. Prenascent: The material life faculty is a condition for the kamma of matricide… (etc.)… the kamma of causing a Buddha's blood to flow by way of Presence Condition. The base is a condition for the aggregates fixed in wrongness by way of Presence Condition. (2)

Aniyato [T 2.0502] dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – vatthu sammattaniyatānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (3)

The indeterminate phenomenon is a condition for the phenomenon fixed in rightness by way of Presence Condition. Prenascent: The base is a condition for the aggregates fixed in rightness by way of Presence Condition. (3)

57. Micchattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā micchattaniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. Sahajāto – micchattaniyato eko khandho ca vatthu ca tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā ca…pe…. (1)

57. The phenomenon fixed in wrongness and the indeterminate phenomenon are a condition for the phenomenon fixed in wrongness by way of Presence Condition—conascence and prenascence. Conascent: One aggregate fixed in wrongness and the base are a condition for the three aggregates… (etc.)… two aggregates… (etc.). (1)

Micchattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā aniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajātā – micchattaniyatā khandhā ca mahābhūtā ca cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – micchattaniyatā khandhā ca kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca [M 2.0382] imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – micchattaniyatā khandhā ca rūpajīvitindriyañca kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

The phenomenon fixed in wrongness and the indeterminate phenomenon are a condition for the indeterminate phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—conascence, postnascence, nutriment, and faculty. Conascent: The aggregates fixed in wrongness and the great elements are a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of Presence Condition. Postnascent: The aggregates fixed in wrongness and physical food are a condition for this body by way of Presence Condition. Postnascent: The aggregates fixed in wrongness and the material life faculty are a condition for kamma-born materiality by way of Presence Condition. (2)

Sammattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā sammattaniyatassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… (dve pañhā micchattaniyatasadisā).

The phenomenon fixed in rightness and the indeterminate phenomenon are a condition for the phenomenon fixed in rightness by way of Presence Condition… (etc.)… (two questions similar to those concerning the phenomenon fixed in wrongness).

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. Conformity of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

58. Hetuyā [V 2.0443] satta, ārammaṇe pañca, adhipatiyā aṭṭha, anantare pañca, samanantare pañca, sahajāte nava, aññamaññe tīṇi, nissaye terasa, upanissaye satta, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane tīṇi, kamme satta, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre satta, indriye satta, jhāne satta, magge satta, sampayutte [T 2.0503] tīṇi, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā terasa, natthiyā pañca, vigate pañca, avigate terasa (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

58. By way of root condition, seven; by way of object condition, five; by way of predominance condition, eight; by way of proximity condition, five; by way of contiguity condition, five; by way of co-nascence condition, nine; by way of mutuality condition, three; by way of dependence condition, thirteen; by way of strong support condition, seven; by way of pre-nascence condition, three; by way of post-nascence condition, three; by way of repetition condition, three; by way of kamma condition, seven; by way of result condition, one; by way of nutriment condition, seven; by way of faculty condition, seven; by way of jhāna condition, seven; by way of path condition, seven; by way of association condition, three; by way of dissociation condition, five; by way of presence condition, thirteen; by way of absence condition, five; by way of disappearance condition, five; by way of non-disappearance condition, thirteen (thus should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

The Affirmative Mode.

2. Paccanīyuddhāro

2. The Section on Negation

59. Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

59. A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of co-nascence condition... by way of strong support condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of strong support condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition. (2)

Micchattaniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state fixed in wrongness is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness and for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition. (3)

Sammattaniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of co-nascence condition... by way of strong support condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato [V 2.0444] dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of strong support condition... by way of post-nascence condition. (2)

Sammattaniyato [M 2.0383] dhammo sammattaniyatassa ca aniyatassa ca dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

A state fixed in rightness is a condition for a state fixed in rightness and for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition. (3)

60. Aniyato dhammo aniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena [T 2.0504] paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

60. An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of strong support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition... by way of post-nascence condition... by way of kamma condition... by way of nutriment condition... by way of faculty condition. (1)

Aniyato dhammo micchattaniyatassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in wrongness by way of object condition... by way of strong support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Aniyato dhammo sammattaniyatassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo. (3)

An indeterminate state is a condition for a state fixed in rightness by way of strong support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition. (3)

Micchattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā micchattaniyatassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. (1)

States fixed in wrongness and indeterminate states are conditions for a state fixed in wrongness by way of co-nascence condition and pre-nascence condition. (1)

Micchattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā aniyatassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

States fixed in wrongness and indeterminate states are conditions for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition, post-nascence condition, nutriment condition, and faculty condition. (2)

Sammattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā sammattaniyatassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ. (1)

States fixed in rightness and indeterminate states are conditions for a state fixed in rightness by way of co-nascence condition and pre-nascence condition. (1)

Sammattaniyato ca aniyato ca dhammā aniyatassa dhammassa sahajātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. (2)

States fixed in rightness and indeterminate states are conditions for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition, post-nascence condition, nutriment condition, and faculty condition. (2)

2. The Negative Mode of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

61. Nahetuyā [V 2.0445] terasa, naārammaṇe naadhipatiyā naanantare nasamanantare terasa, nasahajāte nava, naaññamaññe nava, nanissaye nava, naupanissaye terasa, napurejāte ekādasa, napacchājāte terasa, naāsevane terasa, nakamme navipāke naāhāre terasa…pe… [T 2.0505] namagge terasa, nasampayutte nava, navippayutte satta, noatthiyā satta, nonatthiyā terasa, novigate terasa, noavigate satta (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

61. By way of non-root condition, thirteen; by way of non-object, non-predominance, non-proximity, and non-contiguity conditions, thirteen; by way of non-co-nascence condition, nine; by way of non-mutuality condition, nine; by way of non-dependence condition, nine; by way of non-strong support condition, thirteen; by way of non-pre-nascence condition, eleven; by way of non-post-nascence condition, thirteen; by way of non-repetition condition, thirteen; by way of non-kamma, non-result, and non-nutriment conditions, thirteen... by way of non-path condition, thirteen; by way of non-association condition, nine; by way of non-dissociation condition, seven; by way of non-presence condition, seven; by way of non-absence condition, thirteen; by way of non-disappearance condition, thirteen; by way of non-non-disappearance condition, seven (thus should be counted).

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative Mode.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. The Affirmative-Negative Mode of Conditions

Hetudukaṃ

The Root Dyad

62. Hetupaccayā [M 2.0384] naārammaṇe satta, naadhipatiyā satta, naanantare satta, nasamanantare satta, naaññamaññe tīṇi, naupanissaye satta…pe… namagge satta, nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte tīṇi, nonatthiyā satta, novigate satta (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

62. By way of root condition, not by way of object condition, seven; not by way of predominance condition, seven; not by way of proximity condition, seven; not by way of contiguity condition, seven; not by way of mutuality condition, three; not by way of strong support condition, seven... not by way of path condition, seven; not by way of association condition, three; not by way of dissociation condition, three; not by way of absence condition, seven; not by way of disappearance condition, seven (thus should be counted).

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

The Affirmative-Negative Mode.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Affirmative Mode of Conditions

Nahetudukaṃ

The Non-Root Dyad

63. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe pañca, adhipatiyā aṭṭha, anantare pañca, samanantare pañca[V 2.0446], sahajāte nava, aññamaññe tīṇi, nissaye terasa, upanissaye satta, purejāte tīṇi, pacchājāte tīṇi, āsevane tīṇi, kamme satta, vipāke ekaṃ, āhāre satta, indriye jhāne magge satta, sampayutte tīṇi, vippayutte pañca, atthiyā terasa, natthiyā pañca, vigate pañca, avigate terasa (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

63. By way of non-root condition, by way of object condition, five; by way of predominance condition, eight; by way of proximity condition, five; by way of contiguity condition, five; by way of co-nascence condition, nine; by way of mutuality condition, three; by way of dependence condition, thirteen; by way of strong support condition, seven; by way of pre-nascence condition, three; by way of post-nascence condition, three; by way of repetition condition, three; by way of kamma condition, seven; by way of result condition, one; by way of nutriment condition, seven; by way of faculty condition, seven; by way of jhāna condition, seven; by way of path condition, seven; by way of association condition, three; by way of dissociation condition, five; by way of presence condition, thirteen; by way of absence condition, five; by way of disappearance condition, five; by way of non-disappearance condition, thirteen (thus should be counted).

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

The Negative-Affirmative Mode.

Micchattaniyatattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Triad of States Fixed in Wrongness is concluded.

16. Maggārammaṇattikaṃ

16. The Triad on the Path as Object

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Section on Conditionality
