1. The Section on Analysis

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

1. Uppanno [T 2.0532][M 2.0405][V 2.0472] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – uppannā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppannā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

1. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of root condition—arisen roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of root condition. At the moment of re-linking, arisen roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for kamma-produced material phenomena by way of root condition. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

2. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uppannaṃ cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā…pe… uddhaccaṃ…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Uppannaṃ sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… uppanne khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa [V 2.0473] …pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… uppannā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

2. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of object condition—one contemplates an arisen eye as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self; one relishes it, delights in it. Taking that as object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt… restlessness… sorrow arises. An arisen ear… nose… tongue… body… visible forms… sounds… odors… tastes… tangible objects… base… arisen aggregates are contemplated as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self… sorrow arises. With the divine eye, one sees a form; with the divine ear element, one hears a sound. The visible-form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness… arisen aggregates are a condition for the adverting of the knowledge of psychic power by way of object condition. (1)

3. Anuppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – anuppanne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… anuppanne khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… domanassaṃ [T 2.0533] uppajjati. Anuppannā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

3. An unarisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of object condition—one contemplates unarisen forms… sounds… odors… tastes… tangible objects… unarisen aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self… sorrow arises. Unarisen aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic power, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting by way of object condition. (1)

4. Uppādī dhammo uppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – uppādiṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… uppādī khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Uppādī khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

4. A phenomenon that is arising is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of object condition—the arising eye… body… visible forms… odors… tastes… tangible objects… base… the arising aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self… sorrow arises. The arising aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic power, the knowledge of others' minds, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting by way of object condition. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Predominance Condition

5. Uppanno [M 2.0406] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – uppannaṃ cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Uppannaṃ sotaṃ… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… uppanne khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati…pe…. Sahajātādhipati – uppannā adhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

5. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of predominance condition—object-predominance and co-nascence predominance. Object-predominance: one takes an arisen eye as important, relishes it, delights in it; taking it as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. An arisen ear… nose… tongue… body… visible forms… sounds… odors… tastes… tangible objects… base… arisen aggregates—one takes them as important, relishes them, delights in them; taking them as important, lust arises… Co-nascence predominance: arisen predominant states are a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of predominance condition. (1)

Anuppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – anuppanne rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… anuppanne khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

An unarisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance: one takes unarisen visible forms… sounds… odors… tastes… tangible objects… unarisen aggregates as important, relishes them, delights in them; taking them as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1)

Uppādī [T 2.0534] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – uppādiṃ [V 2.0474] cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe…pe… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… uppādī khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

A phenomenon that is arising is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of predominance condition. Object-predominance: the arising eye… body… visible forms… tangible objects… base… one takes the arising aggregates as important, relishes them, delights in them; taking them as important, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1)

Sahajātapaccayo

The Co-nascence Condition

6. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo – uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā dvinnaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Khandhā vatthussa sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu khandhānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve mahābhūtā…pe… mahābhūtā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ upādārūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. Bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… dve mahābhūtā…pe… mahābhūtā kaṭattārūpānaṃ upādārūpānaṃ sahajātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

6. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Conascence Condition—one arisen aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of Conascence Condition… two aggregates are a condition for the two aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of Conascence Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, one arisen aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and kamma-originated materiality by way of Conascence Condition… two aggregates are a condition for the two aggregates and kamma-originated materiality by way of Conascence Condition. The aggregates are a condition for the base by way of Conascence Condition. The base is a condition for the aggregates by way of Conascence Condition. One great element is a condition for the three great elements by way of Conascence Condition… two great elements… the great elements are a condition for mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality by way of Conascence Condition. External… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… in the case of non-percipient beings, one great element… two great elements… the great elements are a condition for kamma-originated materiality and derived materiality by way of Conascence Condition. (1)

Aññamaññapaccayo

Mutuality Condition.

7. Uppanno [M 2.0407] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa aññamaññapaccayena paccayo – uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppanno [T 2.0535] eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ vatthussa ca aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Dve khandhā…pe… khandhā vatthussa aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Vatthu khandhānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo. Ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ aññamaññapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve mahābhūtā…pe…. (1)

7. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Mutuality Condition. One arisen aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates by way of Mutuality Condition… two aggregates… At the moment of rebirth-linking, one arisen aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and the base by way of Mutuality Condition. Two aggregates… The aggregates are a condition for the base by way of Mutuality Condition. The base is a condition for the aggregates by way of Mutuality Condition. One great element… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… For non-percipient beings, one great element is a condition for the three great elements by way of Mutuality Condition… two great elements…. (1)

Nissayapaccayo

Dependence Condition.

8. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa nissayapaccayena paccayo – uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ [V 2.0475] khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa…pe… vatthu khandhānaṃ…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… mahābhūtā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ upādārūpānaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu uppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ nissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

8. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Dependence Condition—one arisen aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of Dependence Condition… two aggregates… At the moment of rebirth-linking… the aggregates are a condition for the base… the base is a condition for the aggregates… one great element… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… for non-percipient beings, one great element… The great elements are a condition for mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality; the eye-faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness… the body-faculty is a condition for body-consciousness… The base is a condition for the arisen aggregates by way of Dependence Condition. (1)

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition.

9. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe… pakatūpanissayo – uppannaṃ utuṃ upanissāya jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Uppannaṃ bhojanaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya jhānaṃ uppādeti vipassanaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Uppannaṃ utu… [T 2.0536] bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ uppannāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

9. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Decisive Support Condition—object decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support—relying on arisen temperature, one produces jhāna, insight… the path… direct knowledge… meditative attainments, dwells on conceit, adopts a wrong view. Relying on arisen food… lodging, one produces jhāna, insight… the path… direct knowledge… meditative attainments, dwells on conceit, adopts a wrong view. Arisen temperature… food… lodging is a condition for arisen faith… wisdom, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the path, and fruition-attainment by way of Decisive Support Condition. (1)

Anuppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – anuppannaṃ [M 2.0408] vaṇṇasampadaṃ patthayamāno dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti. Anuppannaṃ saddasampadaṃ… gandhasampadaṃ… rasasampadaṃ… phoṭṭhabbasampadaṃ… anuppanne khandhe patthayamāno dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti. Anuppannā vaṇṇasampadā…pe… anuppannā khandhā uppannāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unarisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Decisive Support Condition—object decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: desiring unattained beauty, one gives gifts, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance. Desiring unattained sound… scent… taste… touch… desiring unattained aggregates, one gives gifts, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance. Unarisen beauty… Unarisen aggregates are a condition for arisen faith… wisdom, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the path, and fruition-attainment by way of Decisive Support Condition. (1)

Uppādī dhammo uppannassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – uppādiṃ cakkhusampadaṃ patthayamāno dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti. Uppādiṃ sotasampadaṃ…pe… kāyasampadaṃ…pe… vaṇṇasampadaṃ [V 2.0476]… gandhasampadaṃ… rasasampadaṃ… phoṭṭhabbasampadaṃ… uppādī khandhe patthayamāno dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti. Uppādī cakkhusampadā…pe… kāyasampadā… vaṇṇasampadā…pe… phoṭṭhabbasampadā… uppādī khandhā uppannāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā [T 2.0537] upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon that will arise is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Decisive Support Condition—object decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support—desiring future eye-perfection, one gives gifts, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance. Desiring future ear-perfection… body-perfection… beauty-perfection… fragrance-perfection… taste-perfection… touch-perfection… desiring future aggregates, one gives gifts, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance. Future eye-perfection… body-perfection… beauty-perfection… touch-perfection… future aggregates are a condition for arisen faith… wisdom, bodily pleasure, bodily pain, the path, and fruition-attainment by way of Decisive Support Condition. (1)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition.

10. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu uppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

10. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Pre-nascence Condition—object pre-nascence, base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence—one discerns the eye…pe… the physical base as impermanent, as suffering, and as not-self, relishes it, welcomes it; based on that, lust arises…pe… displeasure arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds. The form base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of Pre-nascence Condition. Base pre-nascence—the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the physical base is a condition for the arisen aggregates by way of Pre-nascence Condition. (1)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

11. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā uppannā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

11. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Post-nascence Condition—the subsequently arisen aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of Post-nascence Condition. (1)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

12. Uppanno [M 2.0409] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – uppannā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppannā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

12. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Kamma Condition—arisen volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of Kamma Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, arisen volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and kamma-produced materiality by way of Kamma Condition. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Result Condition

13. Uppanno [V 2.0477] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo – vipāko uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe [T 2.0538] uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ…pe… dve khandhā…pe… khandhā vatthussa vipākapaccayena paccayo. (1)

13. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Result Condition—an arisen resultant aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and mind-originated materiality by way of Result Condition…pe… two aggregates…pe… At the moment of rebirth-linking, an arisen resultant aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and kamma-produced materiality…pe… two aggregates…pe… the aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of Result Condition. (1)

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment Condition

14. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – uppannā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

14. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Nutriment Condition—Arisen nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of Nutriment Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… the material food is a condition for this body by way of Nutriment Condition. (1)

Indriyapaccayo

Faculty Condition

15. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo – uppannā indriyā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… cakkhundriyaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyindriyaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

15. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Faculty Condition—the arisen faculties are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of Faculty Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… the eye faculty is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body faculty is a condition for body-consciousness…pe… the life faculty of materiality is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of Faculty Condition. (1)

Jhānapaccayādi

Jhāna Condition, etc.

16. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – uppannā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe uppannā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Khandhā vatthussa, vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa [M 2.0410] …pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu uppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – uppannā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena [T 2.0539] paccayo. (1)

16. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Jhāna Condition… by way of Path Condition… by way of Association Condition… by way of Dissociation Condition: by way of co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence. Co-nascence—the arisen aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of Dissociation Condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, the arisen aggregates are a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of Dissociation Condition. Aggregates are a condition for the physical base, and the physical base is a condition for the aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Pre-nascence—the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness …pe… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness… the physical base is a condition for the arisen aggregates by way of Dissociation Condition. Post-nascence—the arisen aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of Dissociation Condition. (1)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

17. Uppanno [V 2.0478] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – uppanno eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ…pe…. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ aniccato…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotudhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu uppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – uppannā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Kabaḷīkāro āhāro imassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

17. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Presence Condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence, nutriment, faculty. Co-nascence—one arisen aggregate is a condition for the three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of Presence Condition…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… one great primary element…pe… external… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… for non-percipient beings…pe…. Pre-nascence—one discerns the eye as impermanent…pe… the physical base as impermanent…pe… displeasure arises; with the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds; the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of Presence Condition. The eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body base is a condition for body-consciousness…pe… the physical base is a condition for the arisen aggregates by way of Presence Condition. Post-nascence—the arisen aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of Presence Condition. Material food is a condition for this body by way of Presence Condition. The life faculty of materiality is a condition for kamma-produced materiality by way of Presence Condition. (1)

Avigatapaccayo

Non-disappearance Condition

18. Uppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa avigatapaccayena paccayo…pe….

18. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of Non-disappearance Condition…pe….

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Order of Conditions

19. Hetuyā ekaṃ, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā tīṇi, sahajāte ekaṃ, aññamaññe ekaṃ, nissaye ekaṃ, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte ekaṃ, pacchājāte kamme vipāke āhāre indriye jhāne magge sampayutte vippayutte atthiyā avigate ekaṃ (evaṃ [T 2.0540] gaṇetabbaṃ).

19. By Root Condition, one; by Object Condition, three; by Dominance Condition, three; by Co-nascence Condition, one; by Mutuality Condition, one; by Support Condition, one; by Decisive Support Condition, three; by Pre-nascence Condition, one; by Post-nascence Condition, one; by Kamma Condition, one; by Result Condition, one; by Nutriment Condition, one; by Faculty Condition, one; by Jhāna Condition, one; by Path Condition, one; by Association Condition, one; by Dissociation Condition, one; by Presence Condition, one; by Non-disappearance Condition, one (thus it should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

The Direct Order.

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Negative Mode.

20. Uppanno [M 2.0411][V 2.0479] dhammo uppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

20. An arisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of pre-nascence condition… by way of post-nascence condition… by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition. (1)

Anuppanno dhammo uppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo, upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An unarisen phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of object condition and by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Uppādī dhammo uppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An arising phenomenon is a condition for an arisen phenomenon by way of object condition… by way of decisive support condition. (1)

21. Nahetuyā tīṇi, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā tīṇi…pe… navippayutte tīṇi, noatthiyā dve, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi, noavigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

21. Three by non-root condition, three by non-object condition, three by non-dominance condition… three by non-dissociation condition, two by non-presence condition, three by non-absence condition, three by non-disappearance condition, and two by non-non-disappearance condition (thus it should be counted).

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative Mode

22. Hetupaccayā naārammaṇe ekaṃ…pe… nonatthiyā novigate ekaṃ.

22. By root condition, one in non-object… one in non-absence and non-disappearance.

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

The Affirmative-Negative Mode

4. Paccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Affirmative Mode

23. Nahetupaccayā [V 2.0480] ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā tīṇi, sahajāte ekaṃ, aññamaññe ekaṃ, nissaye ekaṃ, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte ekaṃ, pacchājāte ekaṃ, kamme vipāke āhāre indriye jhāne [T 2.0541] magge sampayutte vippayutte atthiyā avigate ekaṃ.

23. By non-root condition: three in object, three in dominance, one in co-nascence, one in mutuality, one in support, three in decisive support, one in pre-nascence, one in post-nascence; and one each in kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, association, dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance.

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition

1. Paccuppanno [M 2.0412][V 2.0481] dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – paccuppannā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

1. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of root condition—present roots are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced material phenomena by way of root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition

2. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ…pe… paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati. Ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Atītaṃ cakkhuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Atītaṃ sotaṃ…pe… ghānaṃ… jivhaṃ… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… atīte khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato [V 2.0482] vipassati[T 2.0542], assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati, vicikicchā… uddhaccaṃ… domanassaṃ uppajjati, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Atītā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

2. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of object condition—having given alms, undertaken the precepts, performed the Uposatha observance… one reflects. One reflects on past good deeds. Emerging from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna. Noble ones, emerging from the path, reflect on the path, reflect on the fruit, reflect on the abandoned defilements, reflect on the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements previously accumulated. One contemplates the past eye as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self… and sorrow arises. The past ear… nose… tongue… body… forms… sounds… smells… tastes… tangibles… physical base… one contemplates the past aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self, one relishes and delights in them; taking that as object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt… restlessness… sorrow arises. The base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object condition. Past aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, for the knowledge of others’ minds, for the knowledge of recollection of past lives, for the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

3. Anāgato dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – anāgataṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… anāgate khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Anāgatā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

3. A future phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of object condition—the future eye… the future physical base… future aggregates as impermanent… sorrow arises. Future aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, for the knowledge of others’ minds, for the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… paccuppanne [M 2.0413] khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… paccuppannā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of object condition—the present eye… body… forms… sounds… smells… tastes… tangibles… physical base… present aggregates as impermanent… sorrow arises; with the divine eye one sees forms; with the divine ear element one hears sounds; the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness… present aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Dominance Condition

4. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo[T 2.0543]. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā…pe… pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati. Ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Atītaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe… sadde… gandhe… rase… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… atīte khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1) Anāgato dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – anāgataṃ [V 2.0483] cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… anāgate khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (1)

4. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of dominance condition. Object-dominance: having given alms, having undertaken the precepts… one reflects on past good deeds with respect; emerging from jhāna, one reflects on the jhāna with respect. The noble ones, emerging from the path, reflect on the path with respect and reflect on the fruit with respect. The past eye… body, forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, physical base… one relishes and delights in the past aggregates with respect; treating that with respect, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1) A future phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of dominance condition. Object-dominance: the future eye… physical base… one relishes and delights in the future aggregates with respect; treating that with respect, lust arises, wrong view arises. (1)

Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – paccuppannaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… paccuppanne khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – paccuppannādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of dominance condition—object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: One gives importance to the present eye [...], the base, and the present aggregates, and delights in and rejoices over them. Giving importance to that, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: A present dominant state is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Anantarapaccayo

Immediately Proximate Condition

5. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā atītā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ paccuppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ [T 2.0544] vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa… maggo phalassa… phalaṃ phalassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

5. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of immediately proximate condition—the immediately preceding past aggregates are a condition for the immediately succeeding present aggregates by way of immediately proximate condition. Adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage [...], adaptation for purification [...], change-of-lineage for the path [...], purification for the path [...], the path for the fruit [...], the fruit for the fruit [...], adaptation for fruition-attainment [...]. For one emerging from cessation, the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of immediately proximate condition. (1)

Samanantarapaccayo

Immediately Contiguous Condition

6. Atīto [M 2.0414] dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo (anantarasadisaṃ). (1)

6. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of immediately contiguous condition (similar to the immediately proximate condition). (1)

Sahajātapaccayādi

Co-nascence Condition, and so forth

7. Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo (saṃkhittaṃ). (1)

7. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of co-nascence condition [...], by way of mutual condition [...], and by way of support condition (in brief). (1)

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

8. Atīto [V 2.0484] dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena [T 2.0545] paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – atītaṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ karoti, jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ… maggaṃ… abhiññaṃ… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Atītaṃ sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Atītā saddhā…pe… paññā, rāgo…pe… patthanā, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… paccuppannāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya, rāgassa…pe… patthanāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

8. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support, immediacy decisive support, and natural decisive support [...]. Natural decisive support: Relying on past faith, one gives a gift, undertakes the precepts, performs the Uposatha observance, produces jhāna, insight [...], the path [...], direct knowledge [...], and produces an attainment; one generates conceit, one grasps wrong view. Relying on past virtue [...], wisdom [...], lust [...], aspiration [...], bodily pleasure [...], or bodily pain, one gives a gift, undertakes the precepts, performs the Uposatha observance [...], produces an attainment, kills living beings [...], or creates a schism in the Saṅgha. Past faith [...], wisdom, lust [...], aspiration, bodily pleasure [...], and bodily pain are a condition for present faith [...], wisdom, for lust [...], for aspiration [...], and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Anāgato dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – anāgataṃ cakkhusampadaṃ patthayamāno…pe… sotasampadaṃ… ghānasampadaṃ jivhāsampadaṃ… kāyasampadaṃ… vaṇṇasampadaṃ… saddasampadaṃ… gandhasampadaṃ… rasasampadaṃ… phoṭṭhabbasampadaṃ…patthayamāno…pe… anāgate khandhe patthayamāno dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ… anāgatā cakkhusampadā…pe… vaṇṇasampadā…pe… phoṭṭhabbasampadā… anāgatā khandhā paccuppannāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa, phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A future phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support and natural decisive support [...]. Natural decisive support: Aspiring for future excellence of the eye [...], excellence of the ear [...], excellence of the nose, excellence of the tongue [...], excellence of the body [...], excellence of appearance [...], excellence of sound [...], excellence of smell [...], excellence of taste [...], excellence of tangibles [...], and aspiring for future aggregates, one gives a gift, undertakes the precepts, and performs the Uposatha observance [...]. Future excellence of the eye [...], excellence of appearance [...], excellence of tangibles [...], and future aggregates are a condition for present faith [...], wisdom, for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for the path, and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – paccuppannaṃ [M 2.0415] utuṃ upanissāya jhānaṃ uppādeti, vipassanaṃ…pe… paccuppannaṃ bhojanaṃ senāsanaṃ upanissāya jhānaṃ uppādeti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti. Paccuppannaṃ utu… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ paccuppannāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya kāyikassa…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of decisive support condition—object decisive support and natural decisive support [...]. Natural decisive support: Relying on the present climate, one produces jhāna, insight [...]; relying on present food and lodging, one produces jhāna [...], and produces an attainment. The present climate [...], food [...], and lodging are a condition for present faith [...], wisdom, for bodily pleasure [...], and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

9. Paccuppanno [V 2.0485] dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena [T 2.0546] paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu paccuppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

9. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition—object pre-nascence and base pre-nascence. Object pre-nascence: Regarding the eye [...], the base, as impermanent [...], grief arises. With the divine eye one sees a visible form; with the divine ear element one hears a sound. The visible form base is a condition for eye-consciousness [...]; the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base pre-nascence: The eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness [...]; the body base is a condition for body-consciousness [...]; the physical base is a condition for the present aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

10. Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā paccuppannā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

10. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition. The post-nascent present aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

11. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā atītā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ paccuppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

11. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of repetition condition—the preceding past aggregates are a condition for the succeeding present aggregates by way of repetition condition. Adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage [...]; adaptation for purification [...]; change-of-lineage for the path [...]; and purification for the path by way of repetition condition. (1)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

12. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – atītā cetanā paccuppannānaṃ vipākānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

12. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of kamma condition. Non-simultaneous: past volition is a condition for present resultant aggregates and for matter produced by kamma by way of kamma condition. (1)

Paccuppanno [M 2.0416] dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – paccuppannā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ [V 2.0486] khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccuppannā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of kamma condition—present volition is a condition for associated aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of kamma condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, present volition is a condition for associated aggregates and for kamma-born materiality by way of kamma condition. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Result Condition

13. Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena [T 2.0547] paccayo – vipāko paccuppano eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… dve khandhā…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa vipākapaccayena paccayo. (1)

13. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of result condition—a present resultant single aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-originated materiality by way of result condition…pe… two aggregates…pe… at the moment of rebirth-linking…pe… aggregates are a condition for the physical basis by way of result condition. (1)

Āhārapaccayādi

Nutriment Condition, etc.

14. Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ. Sahajātā – paccuppannā khandhā cittasamuṭṭhānānaṃ rūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccuppannā khandhā kaṭattārūpānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, khandhā vatthussa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo, vatthu khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Purejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa… vatthu paccuppannānaṃ khandhānaṃ vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – paccuppannā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo. (1)

14. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of nutriment condition… faculty condition… jhāna condition… path condition… association condition… dissociation condition—co-nascence, pre-nascence, post-nascence. Co-nascence—present aggregates are a condition for mind-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, present aggregates are a condition for kamma-originated materiality by way of dissociation condition; aggregates are a condition for the physical base by way of dissociation condition; the physical base is a condition for the aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Pre-nascence—the eye-base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body-base is a condition for body-consciousness… the physical base is a condition for present aggregates by way of dissociation condition. Post-nascence—present aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of dissociation condition. (1)

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

15. Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo (uppannattike atthisadisaṃ). (1)

15. A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of presence condition (similar to existence in the triad of the arisen). (1)

Natthivigatāvigatapaccayā

Absence, Disappearance, and Non-disappearance Conditions

16. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo.

16. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of absence condition… disappearance condition.

Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa avigatapaccayena [T 2.0548] paccayo…pe….

A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of non-disappearance condition…pe….

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Affirmative Mode of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Division

17. Hetuyā [M 2.0417][V 2.0487] ekaṃ, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā tīṇi, anantare ekaṃ, samanantare ekaṃ, sahajāte aññamaññe nissaye ekaṃ, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte pacchājāte āsevane ekaṃ, kamme dve, vipāke āhāre ekaṃ…pe… avigate ekaṃ (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

17. In root condition, one; in object condition, three; in dominance condition, three; in contiguity condition, one; in immediate contiguity condition, one; in co-nascence, mutuality, and dependence conditions, one; in decisive support condition, three; in pre-nascence, post-nascence, and repetition conditions, one; in kamma condition, two; in result and nutriment conditions, one…pe… in non-disappearance condition, one (thus it should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

The Affirmative Mode.

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Section on Negation

18. Atīto dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

18. A past phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of object condition… decisive support condition… kamma condition. (1)

Anāgato dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A future phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of object condition… decisive support condition. (1)

Paccuppanno dhammo paccuppannassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A present phenomenon is a condition for a present phenomenon by way of object condition… co-nascence condition… decisive support condition… pre-nascence condition… post-nascence condition… nutriment condition… faculty condition. (1)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. The Negative Mode of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Division

19. Nahetuyā tīṇi, naārammaṇe tīṇi, naadhipatiyā tīṇi, naanantare tīṇi [V 2.0488] …pe… nasampayutte tīṇi, navippayutte tīṇi, noatthiyā dve, nonatthiyā tīṇi, novigate tīṇi, noavigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

19. In non-root condition, three; in non-object condition, three; in non-dominance condition, three; in non-contiguity condition, three …pe… in non-association condition, three; in non-dissociation condition, three; in non-presence condition, two; in non-absence condition, three; in non-disappearance condition, three; in non-non-disappearance condition, two (thus it should be counted).

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative Mode.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. The Affirmative-Negative Mode of Conditions

20. Hetupaccayā [T 2.0549][M 2.0418] naārammaṇe ekaṃ, naadhipatiyā naanantare nasamanantare naaññamaññe naupanissaye…pe… nasampayutte navippayutte nonatthiyā novigate ekaṃ (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

20. In root condition, not in object condition, one; not in dominance, not in contiguity, not in immediate contiguity, not in mutuality, not in decisive support…pe… not in association, not in dissociation, not in absence, not in disappearance, one (thus it should be counted).

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

The Affirmative-Negative Mode.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Affirmative Mode of Conditions

21. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā tīṇi, anantare samanantare sahajāte aññamaññe nissaye ekaṃ, upanissaye tīṇi, purejāte ekaṃ, pacchājāte āsevane ekaṃ…pe… kamme dve, vipāke ekaṃ (imesu padesu ekaṃyeva), avigate ekaṃ (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

21. Not in root condition, in object condition, three; in dominance condition, three; in contiguity, immediate contiguity, co-nascence, mutuality, and dependence conditions, one; in decisive support condition, three; in pre-nascence condition, one; in post-nascence and repetition conditions, one…pe… in kamma condition, two; in result condition, one (in these instances, only one); in non-disappearance condition, one (thus it should be counted).

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

The Negative-Affirmative Mode.

Pañhāvāro.

The Chapter on Questions

Atītattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Past Triad is concluded.

19. Atītārammaṇattikaṃ

19. The Triad of Past Object

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

1. Atītārammaṇaṃ [T 2.0550][M 2.0419][V 2.0489] dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā. (1)

1. A state with a past object arises dependent on a state with a past object by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate with a past object, three aggregates... dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a past object, three aggregates... dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates. (1)

2. Anāgatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāgatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anāgatārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhā. (1)

2. A state with a future object arises dependent on a state with a future object by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate with a future object, three aggregates... two aggregates. (1)

3. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca paccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – paccuppannārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccuppannārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhā. (1)

3. A state with a present object arises dependent on a state with a present object by way of root condition—dependent on one aggregate with a present object, three aggregates... two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a present object, three aggregates... two aggregates. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayādi

Object Condition, etc.

4. Atītārammaṇaṃ [V 2.0490] dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā… adhipatipaccayā (adhipatiyā paṭisandhi natthi)… anantarapaccayā… samanantarapaccayā… sahajātapaccayā… aññamaññapaccayā… nissayapaccayā… upanissayapaccayā… purejātapaccayā… āsevanapaccayā (purejātepi āsevanepi paṭisandhi natthi)… kammapaccayā… [T 2.0551] vipākapaccayā (vipākaṃ atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ, tissopi pañhā paripuṇṇā. Pavattipaṭisandhi kātabbā)… āhārapaccayā… indriyapaccayā… jhānapaccayā… maggapaccayā… sampayuttapaccayā… vippayuttapaccayā… atthipaccayā… natthipaccayā… vigatapaccayā… avigatapaccayā.

4. A state with a past object arises dependent on a state with a past object by way of object condition... by way of dominance condition (there is no rebirth-linking by way of dominance)... by way of proximity condition... by way of contiguity condition... by way of co-nascence condition... by way of mutuality condition... by way of support condition... by way of decisive support condition... by way of pre-nascence condition... by way of repetition condition (there is no rebirth-linking by way of pre-nascence or repetition)... by way of kamma condition... by way of result condition (one resultant aggregate with a past object; all three questions are fully answered. Continuity and rebirth-linking should be considered)... by way of nutriment condition... by way of faculty condition... by way of jhāna condition... by way of path condition... by way of association condition... by way of dissociation condition... by way of presence condition... by way of absence condition... by way of disappearance condition... by way of non-disappearance condition.

5. Hetuyā tīṇi, ārammaṇe tīṇi, adhipatiyā tīṇi…pe… (sabbattha tīṇi), vigate tīṇi, avigate tīṇi (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

5. Three by way of root, three by way of object, three by way of dominance... (three in all cases), three by way of disappearance, three by way of non-disappearance (thus it should be reckoned).

Anulomaṃ.

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

6. Atītārammaṇaṃ [M 2.0420] dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe [V 2.0491] …pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

6. A state with a past object arises dependent on a state with a past object by way of non-root condition—dependent on one rootless aggregate with a past object, three aggregates... dependent on two aggregates... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

7. Anāgatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāgatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ anāgatārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

7. A state with a future object arises dependent on a state with a future object by way of non-root condition—dependent on one rootless aggregate with a future object, three aggregates... dependent on two aggregates... dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

8. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca paccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ paccuppannārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ [T 2.0552] paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

8. A state with a present object arises dependent on a state with a present object by way of non-root condition—dependent on one rootless aggregate with a present object, three aggregates... dependent on two aggregates... at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking... dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Naadhipatipaccayo

Non-Dominance Condition

9. Atītārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā (anulomasahajātasadisaṃ).

9. A state with a past object arises dependent on a state with a past object by way of non-dominance condition (similar to the forward co-nascence).

Napurejātapaccayo

Non-Pre-nascence Condition

10. Atītārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

10. A state with a past object arises dependent on a state with a past object by way of non-pre-nascence condition—in the immaterial realm, dependent on one aggregate with a past object... dependent on two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking.... (1)

Anāgatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāgatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe anāgatārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

A state with a future object arises dependent on a state with a future object by way of non-pre-nascence condition—in the immaterial realm, dependent on one aggregate with a future object, three aggregates... dependent on two aggregates.... (1)

Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca paccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – paṭisandhikkhaṇe paccuppannārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

A state with a present object arises dependent on a state with a present object by way of non-pre-nascence condition—at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a present object... dependent on two aggregates.... (1)

Napacchājātapaccayādi

Non-Post-nascence Condition, etc.

11. Atītārammaṇaṃ [M 2.0421][V 2.0492] dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati napacchājātapaccayā… naāsevanapaccayā (naadhipatisadisā)… nakammapaccayā – atītārammaṇe khandhe paṭicca atītārammaṇā cetanā. (1)

11. A state with a past object arises dependent on a state with a past object by way of non-post-nascence condition... by way of non-repetition condition (similar to non-dominance condition)... by way of non-kamma condition—volition with a past object is dependent on aggregates with a past object. (1)

Anāgatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāgatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – anāgatārammaṇe khandhe paṭicca anāgatārammaṇā [T 2.0553] cetanā. (1)

A state with a future object arises dependent on a state with a future object by way of non-kamma condition—volition with a future object is dependent on aggregates with a future object. (1)

Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca paccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – paccuppannārammaṇe khandhe paṭicca paccuppannārammaṇā cetanā. (1)

A state with a present object arises dependent on a state with a present object by way of non-kamma condition—volition with a present object is dependent on aggregates with a present object. (1)

Navipākapaccayo

No-result condition

12. Atītārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati navipākapaccayā…pe… (navipāke paṭisandhi natthi).

12. A past-object phenomenon arises dependent on a past-object phenomenon by way of no-result condition…pe… (there is no rebirth-linking in no-result).

Najhānapaccayo

No-jhāna condition

13. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca paccuppannārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

13. A present-object phenomenon arises dependent on a present-object phenomenon by way of no-jhāna condition. Dependent on one aggregate associated with the five sense-consciousnesses, three aggregates arise…pe…dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Namaggapaccayo

No-path condition

14. Atītārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati namaggapaccayā – ahetukaṃ atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… (nahetusadisā tisso pañhā, moho natthi ).

14. A past-object phenomenon arises dependent on a past-object phenomenon by way of no-path condition. Dependent on one rootless past-object aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe… (three questions similar to no-root, there is no delusion).

Navippayuttapaccayo

No-dissociation condition

15. Atītārammaṇaṃ [V 2.0493] dhammaṃ paṭicca atītārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe atītārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

15. A past-object phenomenon arises dependent on a past-object phenomenon by way of no-dissociation condition. In the immaterial realm, dependent on one past-object aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe…dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (1)

Anāgatārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anāgatārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe anāgatārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

A future-object phenomenon arises dependent on a future-object phenomenon by way of no-dissociation condition. In the immaterial realm, dependent on one future-object aggregate, three aggregates arise…pe…dependent on two aggregates…pe…. (1)
