Object Condition.

28. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā [T 2.0580] maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… kāyaṃ… rūpe…pe… phoṭṭhabbe… vatthuṃ… ajjhatte khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotudhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

28. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of object condition: having given a gift, undertaken moral virtue, and performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on that; one reflects on previously performed good deeds… and so on… having emerged from jhāna… and so on… noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path, reflect on the fruit, reflect on the abandoned defilements, reflect on the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements previously practiced. One contemplates the internal eye… and so on… body… forms… and so on… tangibles… the physical base… the internal aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self; one relishes and delights in them, and taking that as an object, lust arises… and so on… grief arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds. The base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object condition. The form base… and so on… the tangible base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object condition. The internal aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Ajjhatto [V 2.0518] dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – paro ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… ajjhatte khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena ajjhattacittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ bahiddhā cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… ajjhattaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa[T 2.0581], pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of object condition: another person contemplates one's internal eye… and so on… physical base… internal aggregates as impermanent, as suffering, and as non-self; they relish and delight in them, and taking that as an object, lust arises… and so on… grief arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds. With the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others, one knows the mind of a person endowed with an internal mind. The internal form base is a condition for external eye-consciousness… and so on… the internal tangible base is a condition for external body-consciousness by way of object condition. The internal aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (2)

29. Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – paro dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe [M 2.0443] suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti… nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti. Nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ariyā pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe…pe… paro bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… bahiddhā khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena bahiddhā cittasamaṅgissa…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhā rūpāyatanaṃ bahiddhā cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

29. An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of object condition: another person, having given a gift, undertaken moral virtue, and performed the Uposatha observance, reflects on that; reflects on previously performed good deeds; having emerged from jhāna… and so on… noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect on the path, reflect on the fruit… reflect on Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruit, and for adverting, by way of object condition. The noble ones reflect on abandoned defilements, reflect on suppressed defilements, know the defilements previously practiced… and so on… another person contemplates the external eye… and so on… the physical base… the external aggregates as impermanent… and so on… grief arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds. With the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others, one knows the mind of a person endowed with an external mind… and so on… the base of infinite space is a condition for the base of infinite consciousness by way of object condition. The base of nothingness is a condition for the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception by way of object condition. The external form base is a condition for external eye-consciousness… and so on… the external tangible base is a condition for external body-consciousness… and so on… the external aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ariyā nibbānaṃ paccavekkhanti. Nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… bahiddhā khandhe aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ [T 2.0582] uppajjati. Dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Cetopariyañāṇena bahiddhā cittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Bahiddhā rūpāyatanaṃ [V 2.0519] ajjhattaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ ajjhattaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of object condition: the noble ones reflect on Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, for the fruit, and for adverting, by way of object condition. One contemplates the external eye… and so on… the physical base… the external aggregates as impermanent… and so on… grief arises. With the divine eye, one sees forms; with the divine ear-element, one hears sounds. With the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others, one knows the mind of a person endowed with an external mind. The external form base is a condition for internal eye-consciousness… and so on… the external tangible base is a condition for internal body-consciousness… and so on… the external aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of encompassing the minds of others, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their kamma, the knowledge of the future, and for adverting, by way of object condition. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition.

30. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā, taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… ajjhatte khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ [M 2.0444] garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – ajjhattādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

30. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of dominance condition—object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: Having given alms, undertaken precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects upon it, holding it in high esteem; having previously performed wholesome deeds, one reflects upon them, holding them in high esteem…pe… having emerged from jhāna, one reflects upon the jhāna, holding it in high esteem…pe… noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect upon the path, holding it in high esteem…pe… and upon the fruit, holding it in high esteem. Holding the internal eye…pe… the base… the internal aggregates in high esteem, one savors and delights in them; holding that in high esteem, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: An internal dominant factor is a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – paro ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… ajjhatte khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

An internal phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Object-dominance: Another person, holding the internal eye…pe… the base… the internal aggregates in high esteem, savors and delights in them; holding them in high esteem, lust arises, wrong view arises. (2)

31. Bahiddhā [T 2.0583] dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – paro dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā, taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni garuṃ katvā…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… phalaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… bahiddhā khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati [V 2.0520] – bahiddhādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

31. An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of dominance condition—object-dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object-dominance: Another person, having given alms, undertaken precepts, or performed the Uposatha observance, reflects upon it, holding it in high esteem; having previously practiced wholesome deeds, one reflects upon them, holding them in high esteem…pe… having emerged from jhāna…pe… noble ones, having emerged from the path, reflect upon the path, holding it in high esteem…pe… and upon the fruit, holding it in high esteem…pe… and upon Nibbāna, holding it in high esteem. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit by way of dominance condition. Holding the external eye…pe… the base… the external aggregates in high esteem, one savors and delights in them; holding that in high esteem, lust arises, wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: An external dominant factor is a condition for associated aggregates and mind-originated matter by way of dominance condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – ariyā nibbānaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Nibbānaṃ gotrabhussa, vodānassa, maggassa, phalassa, adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ… bahiddhā khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti, abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā rāgo…pe… diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

An external phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Object-dominance: The noble ones reflect upon Nibbāna, holding it in high esteem. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, for purification, for the path, and for the fruit by way of the dominance condition. Holding the external eye…pe… the base… the external aggregates in high esteem, one savors and delights in them; holding them in high esteem, lust…pe… wrong view arises. (2)

Anantarapaccayo

Immediately Contiguous Condition

32. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā ajjhattā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa, anulomaṃ vodānassa, gotrabhu maggassa, vodānaṃ maggassa, maggo phalassa, phalaṃ phalassa, anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā, nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa [T 2.0584] nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

32. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of immediately contiguous condition—the preceding internal aggregates are a condition for the succeeding internal aggregates by way of immediately contiguous condition. Adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage, adaptation is a condition for purification, change-of-lineage is a condition for the path, purification is a condition for the path, the path is a condition for the fruit, the fruit is a condition for the fruit, adaptation is a condition for fruition-attainment; for one emerging from cessation, the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of immediately contiguous condition. (1)

Bahiddhā [M 2.0445] dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo (purimā purimā bahiddhāti nānākaraṇaṃ, taṃyeva gamanaṃ). (1)

An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of immediately contiguous condition. (The preceding external phenomena are of different kinds, but the process is the same.) (1)

Samanantarapaccayādi

Immediately Contiguous Condition, etc.

33. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo…pe… (anantarasadisaṃ)… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo.

33. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of immediately contiguous condition…pe… (similar to the immediately contiguous condition)… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of reciprocity condition… by way of support condition.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition

34. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ajjhattaṃ saddhaṃ [V 2.0521] upanissāya dānaṃ deti, sīlaṃ samādiyati, uposathakammaṃ…pe… jhānaṃ…pe… vipassanaṃ…pe… maggaṃ…pe… abhiññaṃ…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti. Ajjhattaṃ sīlaṃ…pe… paññaṃ… rāgaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ… kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… utuṃ… bhojanaṃ… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… samāpattiṃ uppādeti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Ajjhattā saddhā…pe… paññā, rāgo…pe… patthanā, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ… kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ… senāsanaṃ ajjhattāya saddhāya…pe… paññāya, rāgassa…pe… patthanāya, kāyikassa sukhassa, kāyikassa dukkhassa, maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

34. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of the decisive support condition—object-decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support…pe…. Natural decisive support: Relying on internal faith, one gives alms, undertakes precepts, performs the Uposatha observance…pe… produces jhāna…pe… produces insight…pe… produces the path…pe… produces direct knowledge…pe… produces meditative attainments, indulges in conceit, or grasps wrong view. Relying on internal virtue…pe… wisdom… lust…pe… aspiration… bodily pleasure… bodily pain… season… food… or dwelling, one gives alms…pe… produces meditative attainments, kills living beings…pe… or splits the Saṅgha. Internal faith…pe… wisdom, lust…pe… aspiration, bodily pleasure, bodily pain… dwelling are a condition for internal faith…pe… wisdom, for lust…pe… aspiration, for bodily pleasure, for bodily pain, for the path, and for fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – paro ajjhattaṃ saddhaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… mānaṃ jappeti, diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhāti[T 2.0585]. Paro ajjhattaṃ sīlaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti, pāṇaṃ hanati…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Ajjhattā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ bahiddhā saddhāya…pe… maggassa phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of decisive support condition—object-decisive support, natural decisive support…pe…. Natural decisive support: another person, relying on internal faith, gives alms…pe… indulges in conceit, or grasps wrong view. Another person, relying on internal virtue…pe… dwelling, gives alms, kills living beings…pe… or splits the Saṅgha. Internal faith…pe… dwelling are a condition for external faith…pe… the path and fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (2)

35. Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – paro bahiddhā saddhaṃ…pe… patthanaṃ, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ [M 2.0446] upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati bahiddhā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ bahiddhā saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

35. An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object-decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support…pe…. Natural decisive support: Another person, relying on external faith…pe… aspiration, bodily pleasure…pe… dwelling, gives alms…pe… splits the Saṅgha. External faith…pe… dwelling are a condition for external faith…pe… fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bahiddhā saddhaṃ…pe… senāsanaṃ upanissāya dānaṃ deti…pe… saṅghaṃ bhindati. Bahiddhā saddhā…pe… senāsanaṃ ajjhattāya saddhāya…pe… phalasamāpattiyā upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object-decisive support, natural decisive support…pe…. Natural decisive support: relying on external faith…pe… dwelling, one gives alms…pe… splits the Saṅgha. External faith…pe… dwelling are a condition for internal faith…pe… fruition attainment by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Purejātapaccayo

Pre-nascence Condition

36. Ajjhatto [V 2.0522] dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Vatthupurejātaṃ – cakkhāyatanaṃ cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… [T 2.0586] kāyāyatanaṃ kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… vatthu ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

36. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: one contemplates the internal eye…pe… the base as impermanent, as suffering, as non-self…pe… distress arises; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds; the form base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the tangible base for body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. Base-prenascence: the eye base is a condition for eye-consciousness…pe… the body base for body-consciousness…pe… the base is a condition for the internal aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – paro ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ bahiddhā cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… ajjhattaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition. Object-prenascence: another person contemplates the internal eye…pe… the base as impermanent…pe… distress arises; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds. The internal form base is a condition for external eye-consciousness…pe… the internal tangible base for external body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

37. Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – paro bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Bahiddhā rūpāyatanaṃ bahiddhā cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa…pe…. Vatthupurejātaṃ – bahiddhā cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… kāyāyatanaṃ…pe… vatthu bahiddhā khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

37. An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: another person contemplates the external eye…pe… the base as impermanent…pe… distress arises; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds. The external form base is a condition for external eye-consciousness…pe… the external tangible base for external body-consciousness…pe…. Base-prenascence: the external eye base…pe… the body base…pe… the base is a condition for the external aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Bahiddhā [M 2.0447] dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇapurejātaṃ – bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti. Bahiddhā rūpāyatanaṃ ajjhattassa cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ ajjhattassa kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena [T 2.0587] paccayo. (2)

An external phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition. Object-prenascence: one contemplates the external eye…pe… the base as impermanent…pe… distress arises; with the divine eye one sees forms, with the divine ear-element one hears sounds. The external form base is a condition for internal eye-consciousness…pe… the external tangible base for internal body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

38. Ajjhatto [V 2.0523] ca bahiddhā ca dhammā ajjhattassa dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Bahiddhā rūpāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ cakkhāyatanañca ajjhattassa cakkhuviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ kāyāyatanañca ajjhattassa kāyaviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā rūpāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ vatthu ca…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ vatthu ca ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

38. Both internal and external phenomena are a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence. The external form base and the internal eye base are a condition for internal eye-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition…pe… the external tangible base and the internal body base for internal body-consciousness…pe… the external form base and the internal base…pe… the external tangible base and the internal base are a condition for the internal aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (1)

Ajjhatto ca bahiddhā ca dhammā bahiddhā dhammassa purejātapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇapurejātaṃ, vatthupurejātaṃ. Ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanañca bahiddhā cakkhāyatanañca bahiddhā cakkhuviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo…pe… ajjhattaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca bahiddhā kāyāyatanañca bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa purejātapaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanañca bahiddhā vatthu ca…pe… ajjhattaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca bahiddhā vatthu ca bahiddhā khandhānaṃ purejātapaccayena paccayo. (2)

Both internal and external phenomena are a condition for an external phenomenon by way of pre-nascence condition: object-prenascence and base-prenascence. The internal form base and the external eye base are a condition for external eye-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition…pe… the internal tangible base and the external body base for external body-consciousness by way of pre-nascence condition. The internal form base and the external base…pe… the internal tangible base and the external base are a condition for the external aggregates by way of pre-nascence condition. (2)

Pacchājātapaccayo

Post-nascence Condition

39. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo – pacchājātā ajjhattā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

39. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: the subsequently arisen internal aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo [T 2.0588] – pacchājātā bahiddhā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa pacchājātapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of post-nascence condition: the subsequently arisen external aggregates are a condition for this previously arisen body by way of post-nascence condition. (1)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

40. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā ajjhattā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena [M 2.0448] paccayo. Anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

40. An internal phenomenon is a condition for an internal phenomenon by way of repetition condition: the preceding internal aggregates are a condition for the subsequent internal aggregates by way of repetition condition. Conformity is a condition for change-of-lineage… conformity for purification… change-of-lineage for the path… purification for the path by way of repetition condition. (1)

Bahiddhā [V 2.0524] dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā…pe… (ajjhattasadisaṃyeva).

An external phenomenon is a condition for an external phenomenon by way of repetition condition: the preceding external aggregates…pe… (just as in the internal case).

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

41. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – ajjhattā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – ajjhattā cetanā vipākānaṃ ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

41. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of kamma condition: co-nascent, non-co-nascent. Co-nascent: internal volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. Non-co-nascent: internal volition is a condition for the internal resultant aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – bahiddhā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – bahiddhā cetanā vipākānaṃ bahiddhā khandhānaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An external state is a condition for an external state by way of kamma condition: co-nascent, non-co-nascent. Co-nascent: external volition is a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. Non-co-nascent: external volition is a condition for the external resultant aggregates and for kamma-originated material phenomena by way of kamma condition. (1)

Vipākapaccayo

Resultant Condition

42. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena [T 2.0589] paccayo…pe… (paripuṇṇaṃ, paṭiccavārasadisaṃ).

42. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of resultant condition... (complete, similar to the Paṭicca section).

Āhārapaccayo

Nutriment Condition

43. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – ajjhattā āhārā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ āhārapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro ajjhattassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

43. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of nutriment condition: internal nutriments are a condition for the associated aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena by way of nutriment condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking... internal physical food is a condition for the internal body by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro bahiddhā kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal state is a condition for an external state by way of nutriment condition: internal physical food is a condition for the external body by way of nutriment condition. (2)

Bahiddhā [M 2.0449][V 2.0525] dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo (pavattipaṭisandhi) bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro bahiddhā kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

An external state is a condition for an external state by way of nutriment condition (in the course of existence and at rebirth-linking): external physical food is a condition for the external body by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro ajjhattassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external state is a condition for an internal state by way of nutriment condition: external physical food is a condition for the internal body by way of nutriment condition. (2)

44. Ajjhatto dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammo ca ajjhattassa dhammassa āhārapaccayena paccayo – ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca ajjhattassa kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (1)

44. An internal state and an external state are a condition for an internal state by way of nutriment condition: internal physical food and external physical food are a condition for the internal body by way of nutriment condition. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammassa [T 2.0590] āhārapaccayena paccayo – ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca bahiddhā kāyassa āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal state and an external state are a condition for an external state by way of nutriment condition: internal physical food and external physical food are a condition for the external body by way of nutriment condition. (2)

Indriyapaccayādi

Faculty Condition, etc.

45. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa indriyapaccayena paccayo, ajjhattikā indriyā (rūpajīvitindriyampi vitthāretabbaṃ)… jhānapaccayena paccayo… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (mātikāpadāni anumajjantena vitthāretabbāni).

45. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of faculty condition: internal faculties (the material life faculty should also be elaborated)... by way of jhāna condition... by way of path condition... by way of association condition... by way of dissociation condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent (the matrix terms should be elaborated accordingly).

Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa vippayuttapaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ (saṃkhittaṃ).

An external state is a condition for an external state by way of dissociation condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent, and post-nascent (in brief).

Atthipaccayo

Presence Condition

46. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ. Sahajāto – ajjhatto eko khandho tiṇṇannaṃ khandhānaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānānañca rūpānaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… khandhā vatthussa [V 2.0526] …pe… vatthu khandhānaṃ…pe… ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ…pe… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ…pe…. Purejātaṃ – cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ (purejātasadisaṃ), vatthu ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Pacchājātā – ajjhattā khandhā purejātassa imassa kāyassa [M 2.0450] atthipaccayena paccayo. Ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro ajjhattassa kāyassa…pe… rūpajīvitindriyaṃ kaṭattārūpānaṃ…pe…. (1)

46. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by way of presence condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, and faculty. Co-nascent: one internal aggregate is a condition for the other three aggregates and for mind-originated material phenomena... two aggregates... at the moment of rebirth-linking... the aggregates are a condition for the physical basis... the physical basis is a condition for the aggregates... one great element... for non-percipient beings, one great element is a condition for the other three great elements... Pre-nascent: the eye... the physical basis (similar to the pre-nascent section), the physical basis is a condition for the internal aggregates by way of presence condition. Post-nascent: the internal aggregates are a condition for this pre-nascent body by way of presence condition. Internal physical food is a condition for the internal body... the material life faculty is a condition for kamma-originated material phenomena... (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo [T 2.0591] – purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Purejātaṃ – paro ajjhattaṃ cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ aniccato…pe… vipassati, dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro bahiddhā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal state is a condition for an external state by way of presence condition: pre-nascent and nutriment. Pre-nascent: another person sees with insight the internal eye... the physical basis... as impermanent...; one sees forms with the divine eye, hears sounds with the divine ear element; the internal form base... the tangible base is a condition for external body-consciousness by way of presence condition. Internal physical food is a condition for the external body by way of presence condition. (2)

47. Bahiddhā dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – sahajātaṃ, purejātaṃ, pacchājātaṃ, āhāraṃ, indriyaṃ (bahiddhā ninnānākaraṇaṃ, mātikāpadāni vitthāretabbāni). (1)

47. An external state is a condition for an external state by way of presence condition: co-nascent, pre-nascent, post-nascent, nutriment, and faculty. (The external should be diversified; the matrix terms should be elaborated.) (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Purejātaṃ – bahiddhā cakkhuṃ…pe… vatthuṃ…pe… dibbena cakkhunā rūpaṃ passati, dibbāya sotadhātuyā saddaṃ suṇāti, bahiddhā rūpāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ ajjhattassa kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro ajjhattassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external state is a condition for an internal state by way of presence condition: pre-nascent and nutriment. Pre-nascent: the external eye... the basis... one sees a form with the divine eye, hears a sound with the divine ear element; the external form base... the tangible base is a condition for the internal body-consciousness by way of presence condition. External physical food is a condition for the internal body by way of presence condition. (2)

48. Ajjhatto dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammo ca ajjhattassa dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Purejātaṃ – bahiddhā rūpāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ cakkhu ca ajjhattassa cakkhuviññāṇassa…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ kāyāyatanañca ajjhattassa kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhā rūpāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ vatthu ca…pe… bahiddhā phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca ajjhattaṃ vatthu [T 2.0592] ca ajjhattānaṃ khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Āhāraṃ – ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca ajjhattassa kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (1)

48. An internal state and an external state are a condition for an internal state by presence condition: pre-nascence, nutriment. Pre-nascence: the external form base and the internal eye are a condition for the internal eye-consciousness... the external tangible base and the internal body base are a condition for the internal body-consciousness by presence condition. The external form base and the internal basis... the external tangible base and the internal basis are a condition for the internal aggregates by presence condition. Nutriment: internal material food and external material food are a condition for the internal body by presence condition. (1)

Ajjhatto [V 2.0527] dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammassa atthipaccayena paccayo – purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ. Purejātaṃ – ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanañca bahiddhā cakkhāyatanañca bahiddhā cakkhuviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… ajjhattaṃ [M 2.0451] phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca bahiddhā kāyāyatanañca bahiddhā kāyaviññāṇassa atthipaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattaṃ rūpāyatanañca bahiddhā vatthu ca bahiddhā khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo…pe… ajjhattaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca bahiddhā vatthu ca bahiddhā khandhānaṃ atthipaccayena paccayo. Āhāraṃ – ajjhatto kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca bahiddhā kabaḷīkāro āhāro ca bahiddhā kāyassa atthipaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal state and an external state are a condition for an external state by presence condition: pre-nascence, nutriment. Pre-nascence: the internal form base and the external eye base are a condition for the external eye-consciousness... the internal tangible base and the external body base are a condition for the external body-consciousness by presence condition. The internal form base and the external basis are a condition for the external aggregates by presence condition... the internal tangible base and the external basis are a condition for the external aggregates by presence condition. Nutriment: internal material food and external material food are a condition for the external body by presence condition. (2)

Natthivigatāvigatapaccayā

Non-existence, Disappearance, and Non-disappearance Conditions

49. Ajjhatto dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa natthipaccayena paccayo… vigatapaccayena paccayo… avigatapaccayena paccayo.

49. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by non-existence condition… by disappearance condition… by non-disappearance condition.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Forward Order of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Division

Suddhaṃ

Pure.

50. Hetuyā dve, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā cattāri, anantare dve, samanantare dve, sahajāte aññamaññe nissaye dve, upanissaye cattāri, purejāte cha, pacchājāte āsevane kamme vipāke dve, āhāre cha, indriye dve, jhāne magge sampayutte vippayutte dve, atthiyā cha, natthiyā dve, vigate dve, avigate [T 2.0593] cha (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

50. By root condition, two; by object condition, four; by dominance condition, four; by immediately proximate condition, two; by contiguous condition, two; by co-nascence, mutuality, and support conditions, two; by strong support condition, four; by pre-nascence condition, six; by post-nascence, repetition, kamma, and result conditions, two; by nutriment condition, six; by faculty condition, two; by jhāna, path, association, and dissociation conditions, two; by presence condition, six; by non-existence condition, two; by disappearance condition, two; by non-disappearance condition, six (thus should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

In forward order.

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Negative Mode

51. Ajjhatto [V 2.0528] dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

51. An internal state is a condition for an internal state by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by strong support condition… by pre-nascence condition… by post-nascence condition… by kamma condition… by nutriment condition… by faculty condition. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal state is a condition for an external state by object condition… by strong support condition… by pre-nascence condition… by nutriment condition. (2)

52. Bahiddhā [M 2.0452] dhammo bahiddhā dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… pacchājātapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo. (1)

52. An external state is a condition for an external state by object condition… by co-nascence condition… by strong support condition… by pre-nascence condition… by post-nascence condition… by kamma condition… by nutriment condition… by faculty condition. (1)

Bahiddhā dhammo ajjhattassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… purejātapaccayena paccayo… āhārapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external state is a condition for an internal state by object condition… by strong support condition… by pre-nascence condition… by nutriment condition. (2)

53. Ajjhatto dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammo ca ajjhattassa dhammassa purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ. (1)

53. An internal state and an external state are a condition for an internal state by pre-nascence and nutriment conditions. (1)

Ajjhatto dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammo ca bahiddhā dhammassa purejātaṃ, āhāraṃ. (2)

An internal state and an external state are a condition for an external state by pre-nascence and nutriment conditions. (2)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. The Negative Mode of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Division

54. Nahetuyā [T 2.0594] cha, naārammaṇe cha, naadhipatiyā cha (saṃkhittaṃ, sabbattha cha kātabbā), navippayutte cha, noatthiyā cattāri, nonatthiyā cha, novigate cha, noavigate cattāri (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ)

54. Not by root condition, six; not by object condition, six; not by dominance condition, six (abbreviated, six should be applied everywhere); not by dissociation condition, six; not by presence condition, four; not by non-existence condition, six; not by disappearance condition, six; not by non-disappearance condition, four (thus should be counted).

Paccanīyaṃ.

The Negative Mode.

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. The Forward-Negative Mode of Conditions

Hetudukaṃ

The Root Dyad

55. Hetupaccayā [V 2.0529] naārammaṇe dve, naadhipatiyā naanantare nasamanantare naaññamaññe naupanissaye dve (saṃkhittaṃ, sabbattha dve), nasampayutte navippayutte nonatthiyā novigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

55. By root condition, not by object condition, two; not by dominance condition, not by immediately proximate condition, not by contiguous condition, not by mutuality condition, not by strong support condition, two (abbreviated, everywhere two); not by association condition, not by dissociation condition, not by non-existence condition, not by disappearance condition, two (thus should be counted).

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

The Forward-Negative Mode.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Forward Mode of Conditions

56. Nahetupaccayā [M 2.0453] ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā cattāri (anulomapadāni gaṇetabbāni), avigate cha (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

56. Not by root condition, by object condition, four; by dominance condition, four (the forward terms should be counted); by non-disappearance condition, six (thus should be counted).

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

The Negative-Forward Mode.

Pañhāvāro.

The Chapter on Questions.

Ajjhattattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Internal Triad is concluded.

Hetupaccayo

Root Condition

1. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ [T 2.0595][M 2.0454][V 2.0530] dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

1. A phenomenon with an internal object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an internal object by root condition: dependent on one aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe…. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an external object by root condition: dependent on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on. (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayādi

Object Condition, etc.

2. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā…pe… avigatapaccayā (saṃkhittaṃ).

2. A phenomenon with an internal object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an internal object by object condition… and so on… by non-disappearance condition (abbreviated).

Nahetupaccayo

Non-Root Condition

4. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato [T 2.0596] moho. (1)

4. A phenomenon with an internal object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an internal object by non-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… Dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ [M 2.0455] dhammaṃ paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nahetupaccayā – ahetukaṃ bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… ahetukapaṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… vicikicchāsahagate uddhaccasahagate khandhe paṭicca vicikicchāsahagato uddhaccasahagato moho. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an external object by non-root condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate with an external object, three aggregates arise… and so on… two aggregates… and so on… At the moment of rootless rebirth-linking… and so on… Dependent on aggregates accompanied by doubt and restlessness, delusion accompanied by doubt and restlessness arises. (1)

Naadhipatipaccayādi

Non-Dominance Condition, etc.

5. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati naadhipatipaccayā [V 2.0532]… (anulomasahajātasadisaṃ, ninnānākaraṇaṃ) napurejātapaccayā – arūpe ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

5. A phenomenon with an internal object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an internal object by non-dominance condition… (similar to the conascent section of the positive triad, without differentiation) by non-pre-nascence condition—in the formless realm, dependent on one aggregate with an internal object… and so on… at the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. (1)

6. Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati napurejātapaccayā – arūpe bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe…. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe… napacchājātapaccayā… naāsevanapaccayā… (sahajātasadisaṃ) nakammapaccayā – ajjhattārammaṇe khandhe paṭicca ajjhattārammaṇā cetanā.

6. A phenomenon with an external object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an external object by non-pre-nascence condition—in the formless realm, dependent on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates arise… and so on. At the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on… by non-post-nascence condition… by non-repetition condition… (similar to conascent) by non-kamma condition—dependent on aggregates with an internal object, volition with an internal object arises.

Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati nakammapaccayā – bahiddhārammaṇe khandhe paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇā cetanā.

A phenomenon with an external object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an external object by non-kamma condition—dependent on aggregates with an external object, volition with an external object arises.

Navipākapaccayādi

Non-Resultant Condition, etc.

7. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati navipākapaccayā (paṭisandhi natthi)… najhānapaccayā…pe… pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ…pe…. (1)

7. A phenomenon with an internal object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an internal object by non-resultant condition (there is no rebirth-linking)… by non-jhāna condition… and so on… dependent on one aggregate with an internal object accompanied by the five sense-consciousnesses… and so on. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ [T 2.0597] dhammaṃ paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati najhānapaccayā – pañcaviññāṇasahagataṃ bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… namaggapaccayā (nahetusadiso. Moho natthi)… navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe…. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an external object by non-jhāna condition—dependent on one aggregate with an external object accompanied by the five sense-consciousnesses, three aggregates arise… and so on… by non-path condition (not similar to root condition; delusion is absent)… by non-dissociation condition—in the formless realm, dependent on one aggregate with an internal object, three aggregates arise… and so on. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo uppajjati navippayuttapaccayā – arūpe bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe…. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object arises dependent on a phenomenon with an external object by non-dissociation condition—in the formless realm, dependent on one aggregate with an external object, three aggregates arise… and so on. (1)

8. Nahetuyā [M 2.0456][V 2.0533] dve, naadhipatiyā dve, napurejāte dve, napacchājāte dve, naāsevane nakamme navipāke najhāne namagge navippayutte dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

8. By non-root condition, two; by non-dominance condition, two; by non-pre-nascence condition, two; by non-post-nascence condition, two; by non-repetition condition, two; by non-kamma condition, two; by non-resultant condition, two; by non-jhāna condition, two; by non-path condition, two; by non-dissociation condition, two (thus it should be counted).

9. Hetupaccayā naadhipatiyā dve…pe… navipāke dve, navippayutte dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

9. Two by way of Root Condition, not by way of Dominance Condition… two not by way of Result Condition, two not by way of Dissociation Condition (thus should it be reckoned).

10. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe dve, anantare dve, samanantare dve…pe… magge dve…pe… avigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

10. Two not by way of the Root Condition, two by way of the Object Condition, two by way of the Proximity Condition, two by way of the Contiguity Condition… two by way of the Path Condition… two by way of the Non-disappearance Condition (thus should it be reckoned).

7. The Question Section.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Condition-Direct Mode.
