1. The Analysis Section.

Hetupaccayo

The Root Condition.

11. Ajjhattārammaṇo [T 2.0598][V 2.0534] dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – ajjhattārammaṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe ajjhattārammaṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ hetupaccayena paccayo. (1)

11. An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of Root Condition—internal-object roots are conditions for associated aggregates by way of Root Condition. At the moment of relinking, internal-object roots are conditions for associated aggregates by way of Root Condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo [M 2.0457] dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa hetupaccayena paccayo – bahiddhārammaṇā hetū sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. (1)

An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of Root Condition—external-object roots are conditions for associated aggregates… at the moment of relinking… (1)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

The Object Condition.

12. Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – ajjhattaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ paccavekkhati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ paccavekkhati, ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ paccavekkhati, dibbaṃ sotadhātuṃ…pe… iddhividhañāṇaṃ…pe… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ paccavekkhati. Ariyā ajjhattārammaṇe pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Ajjhattārammaṇe ajjhatte khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha ajjhattārammaṇo rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Ajjhattārammaṇā ajjhattā khandhā pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

12. An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of Object Condition: one reviews the internal sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; one reviews the internal divine eye regarding an internal object, the divine ear-element…the knowledge of psychic powers…the knowledge of past lives…the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings…the knowledge of future events. Noble Ones review the abandoned defilements regarding an internal object, the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements accumulated previously. One contemplates the internal aggregates as impermanent…[suffering, non-self]…relishes and delights in them; based on that, lust with an internal object arises…sorrow arises. Internal aggregates, as internal objects, are conditions for the knowledge of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, the knowledge of future events, and for adverting, by way of Object Condition. (1)

Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena [T 2.0599] paccayo – bahiddhā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ [V 2.0535] paccavekkhati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ paccavekkhati. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ bahiddhā dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ paccavekkhati, dibbaṃ sotadhātuṃ…pe… iddhividhañāṇaṃ…pe… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ paccavekkhati, ajjhattārammaṇe bahiddhā khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… cetopariyañāṇena ajjhattārammaṇabahiddhācittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti, ajjhattārammaṇā bahiddhā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of Object Condition—one reviews the external sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. One reviews the external divine eye that has an internal object, the divine ear-element… the knowledge of psychic powers… the knowledge of past lives… the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings… the knowledge of future events. One contemplates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self the external aggregates that have an internal object… with the knowledge of others’ minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with an external mind that has an internal object. External aggregates that have an internal object are conditions for the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, the knowledge of future events, and for adverting, by way of Object Condition. (2)

13. Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – bahiddhārammaṇaṃ bahiddhā dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ paccavekkhati, dibbaṃ sotadhātuṃ paccavekkhati. Iddhividhañāṇaṃ…pe… cetopariyañāṇaṃ…pe… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ…pe… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ…pe… anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ paccavekkhati. Bahiddhārammaṇe bahiddhā khandhe aniccato dukkhato anattato vipassati…pe… cetopariyañāṇena bahiddhārammaṇabahiddhācittasamaṅgissa cittaṃ jānāti. Bahiddhārammaṇā [M 2.0458] bahiddhā khandhā cetopariyañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (1)

13. An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of Object Condition—one reviews the external divine eye that has an external object, the divine ear-element. One reviews the knowledge of psychic powers… the knowledge of others’ minds… the knowledge of past lives… the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings… the knowledge of future events. One contemplates as impermanent, suffering, and non-self the external aggregates that have an external object… with the knowledge of others’ minds, one knows the mind of one endowed with an external mind that has an external object. External aggregates that have an external object are conditions for the knowledge of others’ minds, the knowledge of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, the knowledge of future events, and for adverting, by way of Object Condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ [T 2.0600] katvā taṃ paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni paccavekkhati, jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā jhānaṃ paccavekkhati. Ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ paccavekkhanti, phalaṃ paccavekkhanti, bahiddhārammaṇe pahīne kilese paccavekkhanti, vikkhambhite kilese paccavekkhanti, pubbe samudāciṇṇe kilese jānanti. Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ paccavekkhati, dibbaṃ sotadhātuṃ… iddhividhañāṇaṃ… cetopariyañāṇaṃ… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ… anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ… bahiddhārammaṇe ajjhatte khandhe aniccato…pe… vipassati, assādeti abhinandati, taṃ ārabbha ajjhattārammaṇo rāgo uppajjati…pe… domanassaṃ uppajjati. Bahiddhārammaṇā ajjhattā khandhā iddhividhañāṇassa, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇassa, yathākammūpagañāṇassa, anāgataṃsañāṇassa, āvajjanāya ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of Object Condition—having given alms, undertaken precepts, performed the Uposatha observance, one reviews that. One reviews past good conduct. Having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna. Noble Ones, having emerged from the path, review the path, review the fruition; they review the abandoned defilements regarding an external object, review the suppressed defilements, and know the defilements accumulated previously. One reviews the internal divine eye that has an external object, the divine ear-element… the knowledge of psychic powers… the knowledge of others’ minds… the knowledge of past lives… the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings… the knowledge of future events. One contemplates the internal aggregates as impermanent…[suffering, non-self] regarding an external object…relishes and delights in them; based on that, lust with an internal object arises…sorrow arises. Internal aggregates that have an external object are conditions for the knowledge of psychic powers, the knowledge of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings, the knowledge of future events, and for adverting, by way of Object Condition. (2)

Adhipatipaccayo

The Dominance Condition.

14. Ajjhattārammaṇo [V 2.0536] dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇādhipati, sahajātādhipati. Ārammaṇādhipati – ajjhattaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… dibbaṃ sotadhātuṃ…pe… iddhividhañāṇaṃ… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ… anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… ajjhattārammaṇe ajjhatte khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā ajjhattārammaṇo rāgo [T 2.0601] uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. Sahajātādhipati – ajjhattārammaṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

14. An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of the dominance condition—object dominance and co-nascence dominance. Object dominance: One reflects, making paramount the internal base of the infinitude of consciousness; one reflects, making paramount the internal base of neither perception nor non-perception. Making paramount the internal divine eye... the internal divine ear element... the knowledge of psychic powers... the knowledge of past lives... the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings... the knowledge of future events... one delights in and rejoices in the internal aggregates, making them paramount. Making that paramount, internal-object lust arises, internal-object wrong view arises. Co-nascence dominance: The internal-object dominance is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the dominance condition. (1)

15. Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Sahajātādhipati – bahiddhārammaṇādhipati sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ adhipatipaccayena paccayo. (1)

15. An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Co-nascence dominance: The external-object dominance is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of the dominance condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo [M 2.0459] dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa adhipatipaccayena paccayo. Ārammaṇādhipati – dānaṃ datvā sīlaṃ samādiyitvā uposathakammaṃ katvā taṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, pubbe suciṇṇāni…pe… jhānā vuṭṭhahitvā…pe… ariyā maggā vuṭṭhahitvā maggaṃ… phalaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhanti. Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ ajjhattaṃ dibbaṃ cakkhuṃ garuṃ katvā…pe… dibbaṃ sotadhātuṃ… iddhividhañāṇaṃ… cetopariyañāṇaṃ… pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ… yathākammūpagañāṇaṃ… anāgataṃsañāṇaṃ garuṃ katvā paccavekkhati, bahiddhārammaṇe ajjhatte khandhe garuṃ katvā assādeti abhinandati, taṃ garuṃ katvā ajjhattārammaṇo rāgo uppajjati, diṭṭhi uppajjati. (2)

An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of the dominance condition. Object dominance: Having given alms, undertaken virtue, performed the Uposatha observance, one reflects on it, making it paramount. Having previously performed good deeds... having emerged from jhana... having emerged from the noble path, they reflect on the path... the fruit, making it paramount. Making paramount the internal divine eye (as an external object)... the divine ear element... the knowledge of psychic powers... the knowledge of others' minds... the knowledge of past lives... the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings... the knowledge of future events... one delights in and rejoices in the internal aggregates that have an external object, making them paramount. Making that paramount, internal-object lust arises, internal-object wrong view arises. (2)

Anantarapaccayo

Immediately Contiguous Condition

16. Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā ajjhattārammaṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ ajjhattārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

16. An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of the immediately contiguous condition—preceding internal-object aggregates are a condition for succeeding internal-object aggregates by way of the immediately contiguous condition. (1)

Ajjhattārammaṇo [V 2.0537] dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena [T 2.0602] paccayo – ajjhattārammaṇaṃ cuticittaṃ bahiddhārammaṇassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ bahiddhārammaṇāya āvajjanāya anantarapaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattārammaṇā khandhā bahiddhārammaṇassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Ajjhattārammaṇaṃ anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā… nirodhā vuṭṭhahantassa… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of the immediately contiguous condition—internal-object death consciousness is a condition for external-object rebirth consciousness by way of the immediately contiguous condition. Internal-object life-continuum is a condition for external-object adverting by way of the immediately contiguous condition. Internal-object aggregates are a condition for external-object emergence by way of the immediately contiguous condition. Internal-object adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage... adaptation for purification... adaptation for fruition-attainment... one emerging from cessation... the base of neither perception nor non-perception is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of the immediately contiguous condition. (2)

17. Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā bahiddhārammaṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ bahiddhārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ anantarapaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa… maggo phalassa… phalaṃ phalassa… anulomaṃ phalasamāpattiyā anantarapaccayena paccayo. (1)

17. An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of the immediately contiguous condition—preceding external-object aggregates are a condition for succeeding external-object aggregates by way of the immediately contiguous condition. External-object adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage... adaptation for purification... change-of-lineage for the path... purification for the path... the path for the fruit... the fruit for the fruit... adaptation is a condition for fruition-attainment by way of the immediately contiguous condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa anantarapaccayena paccayo – bahiddhārammaṇaṃ cuticittaṃ ajjhattārammaṇassa upapatticittassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ ajjhattārammaṇāya āvajjanāya anantarapaccayena [M 2.0460] paccayo. Bahiddhārammaṇā khandhā ajjhattārammaṇassa vuṭṭhānassa anantarapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An external-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of the immediately contiguous condition—external-object death consciousness is a condition for internal-object rebirth consciousness by way of the immediately contiguous condition. External-object life-continuum is a condition for internal-object adverting by way of the immediately contiguous condition. External-object aggregates are a condition for internal-object emergence by way of the immediately contiguous condition. (2)

Samanantarapaccayādi

Immediately Contiguous Condition, etc.

18. Ajjhattārammaṇo [T 2.0603] dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa samanantarapaccayena paccayo…pe… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… aññamaññapaccayena paccayo… nissayapaccayena paccayo.

18. An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of the immediately contiguous condition... by way of the co-nascence condition... by way of the reciprocal condition... by way of the support condition.

Upanissayapaccayo

Decisive Support Condition.

19. Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ajjhattārammaṇā [V 2.0538] aniccānupassanā, dukkhānupassanā, anattānupassanā, ajjhattārammaṇāya aniccānupassanāya, dukkhānupassanāya, anattānupassanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

19. An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an internal-object phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: The contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an internal object, are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an internal object, by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – ajjhattārammaṇā aniccānupassanā, dukkhānupassanā, anattānupassanā bahiddhārammaṇāya aniccānupassanāya, dukkhānupassanāya, anattānupassanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

An internal-object phenomenon is a condition for an external-object phenomenon by way of decisive support condition: immediately contiguous decisive support, natural decisive support… Natural decisive support: The contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an internal object, are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an external object, by way of decisive support condition. (2)

20. Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bahiddhārammaṇā aniccānupassanā, dukkhānupassanā, anattānupassanā bahiddhārammaṇāya aniccānupassanāya, dukkhānupassanāya, anattānupassanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (1)

20. A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of decisive support condition: immediately proximate decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an external object, are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an external object, by way of decisive support condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo – ārammaṇūpanissayo, anantarūpanissayo, pakatūpanissayo…pe…. Pakatūpanissayo – bahiddhārammaṇā aniccānupassanā[T 2.0604], dukkhānupassanā, anattānupassanā ajjhattārammaṇāya aniccānupassanāya, dukkhānupassanāya, anattānupassanāya upanissayapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of decisive support condition: object decisive support, immediately proximate decisive support, natural decisive support… and so on. Natural decisive support: the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an external object, are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having an internal object, by way of decisive support condition. (2)

Āsevanapaccayo

Repetition Condition

21. Ajjhattārammaṇo [M 2.0461] dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā ajjhattārammaṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ ajjhattārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

21. A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of repetition condition: the preceding aggregates with an internal object are a condition for the succeeding aggregates with an internal object by way of repetition condition. (1)

Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – ajjhattārammaṇaṃ anulomaṃ gotrabhussa, anulomaṃ vodānassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of repetition condition: conformity with an internal object is a condition for change-of-lineage, and conformity is a condition for purification by way of repetition condition. (2)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo – purimā purimā [V 2.0539] bahiddhārammaṇā khandhā pacchimānaṃ pacchimānaṃ bahiddhārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ āsevanapaccayena paccayo. Bahiddhārammaṇaṃ anulomaṃ gotrabhussa… anulomaṃ vodānassa… gotrabhu maggassa… vodānaṃ maggassa āsevanapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of repetition condition: the preceding aggregates with an external object are a condition for the succeeding aggregates with an external object by way of repetition condition. Conformity with an external object is a condition for change-of-lineage… conformity is a condition for purification… change-of-lineage is a condition for the path… purification is a condition for the path by way of repetition condition. (1)

Kammapaccayo

Kamma Condition

22. Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – ajjhattārammaṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – ajjhattārammaṇā cetanā vipākānaṃ ajjhattārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

22. A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of kamma condition: simultaneously arisen and non-simultaneously arisen. Simultaneously arisen: volition with an internal object is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. Non-simultaneously arisen: volition with an internal object is a condition for the resultant aggregates with an internal object by way of kamma condition. (1)

Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena [T 2.0605] paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – ajjhattārammaṇā cetanā vipākānaṃ bahiddhārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of kamma condition. Non-simultaneously arisen: volition with an internal object is a condition for the resultant aggregates with an external object by way of kamma condition. (2)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo – sahajātā, nānākkhaṇikā. Sahajātā – bahiddhārammaṇā cetanā sampayuttakānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe…pe…. Nānākkhaṇikā – bahiddhārammaṇā cetanā vipākānaṃ bahiddhārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of kamma condition: simultaneously arisen and non-simultaneously arisen. Simultaneously arisen: volition with an external object is a condition for the associated aggregates by way of kamma condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking… and so on. Non-simultaneously arisen: volition with an external object is a condition for the resultant aggregates with an external object by way of kamma condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa kammapaccayena paccayo. Nānākkhaṇikā – bahiddhārammaṇā cetanā vipākānaṃ ajjhattārammaṇānaṃ khandhānaṃ kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of kamma condition. Non-simultaneously arisen: volition with an external object is a condition for the resultant aggregates with an internal object by way of kamma condition. (2)

Vipākapaccayādi

Result Condition, etc.

23. Ajjhattārammaṇo [M 2.0462] dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa vipākapaccayena paccayo…pe… āhārapaccayena paccayo… indriyapaccayena paccayo… jhānapaccayena paccayo [V 2.0540]… maggapaccayena paccayo… sampayuttapaccayena paccayo… atthipaccayena paccayo… natthipaccayena paccayo…vigatapaccayena paccayo… avigatapaccayena paccayo.

23. A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of result condition… and so on… by way of nutriment condition… by way of faculty condition… by way of jhāna condition… by way of path condition… by way of association condition… by way of presence condition… by way of absence condition… by way of disappearance condition… by way of non-disappearance condition.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Forward Order of Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

Suddhaṃ

Pure

24. Hetuyā dve, ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā tīṇi, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri, sahajāte dve, aññamaññe dve, nissaye dve, upanissaye cattāri, āsevane tīṇi, kamme cattāri, vipāke dve …pe… (sabbattha dve [T 2.0606]), sampayutte dve, atthiyā dve, natthiyā cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

24. By way of root condition, two; by way of object condition, four; by way of dominance condition, three; by way of contiguity condition, four; by way of immediate contiguity condition, four; by way of co-nascence condition, two; by way of reciprocity condition, two; by way of dependence condition, two; by way of decisive support condition, four; by way of repetition condition, three; by way of kamma condition, four; by way of result condition, two… and so on (in all cases, two); by way of association condition, two; by way of presence condition, two; by way of absence condition, four; by way of disappearance condition, four; by way of non-disappearance condition, two (thus it should be counted).

Anulomaṃ.

Forward Order

Paccanīyuddhāro

The Section on Negation

25. Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

25. A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (1)

Ajjhattārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with an internal object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of object condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (2)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo bahiddhārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… sahajātapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (1)

A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an external object by way of object condition… by way of co-nascence condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (1)

Bahiddhārammaṇo dhammo ajjhattārammaṇassa dhammassa ārammaṇapaccayena paccayo… upanissayapaccayena paccayo… kammapaccayena paccayo. (2)

A phenomenon with an external object is a condition for a phenomenon with an internal object by way of object condition… by way of decisive support condition… by way of kamma condition. (2)

2. Paccayapaccanīyaṃ

2. The Section on Negated Conditions

2. Saṅkhyāvāro

2. Numerical Section

26. Nahetuyā [M 2.0463][V 2.0541] cattāri, naārammaṇe cattāri, naadhipatiyā cattāri, naanantare cattāri (saṃkhittaṃ, sabbattha cattāri), napurejāte napacchājāte naāsevane…pe… navippayutte cattāri…pe… noavigate cattāri (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

26. Not by way of root condition, four; not by way of object condition, four; not by way of dominance condition, four; not by way of contiguity condition, four (abbreviated, in all cases four); not by way of pre-nascence condition, not by way of post-nascence condition, not by way of repetition condition… and so on… not by way of dissociation condition, four… and so on… not by way of non-disappearance condition, four (thus it should be counted).

Paccanīyaṃ.

Negation

3. Paccayānulomapaccanīyaṃ

3. The Forward-Negative Order of Conditions

27. Hetupaccayā [T 2.0607] naārammaṇe dve, naadhipatiyā dve, naanantare nasamanantare naupanissaye naāsevane nakamme…pe… nonatthiyā novigate dve (sabbattha dve. Evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

27. By way of root-condition, not by way of object-condition—two; not by way of dominance-condition—two; not by way of contiguity-condition, not by way of immediately contiguous-condition, not by way of strong dependence-condition, not by way of recurrence-condition, not by way of kamma-condition… etc.… not by way of absence-condition, not by way of disappearance-condition—two (everywhere two. Thus should be counted).

Anulomapaccanīyaṃ.

Forward-Negative Mode.

4. Paccayapaccanīyānulomaṃ

4. The Negative-Forward Order of Conditions.

28. Nahetupaccayā ārammaṇe cattāri, adhipatiyā tīṇi, anantare cattāri, samanantare cattāri, sahajāte aññamaññe nissaye dve, upanissaye cattāri, āsevane tīṇi, kamme cattāri, vipāke dve…pe… sampayutte dve, atthiyā dve, natthiyā cattāri, vigate cattāri, avigate dve (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

28. Not by way of root-condition: by way of object-condition—four; by way of dominance-condition—three; by way of contiguity-condition—four; by way of immediately contiguous-condition—four; by way of co-nascence-condition, by way of reciprocity-condition, by way of dependence-condition—two; by way of strong dependence-condition—four; by way of recurrence-condition—three; by way of kamma-condition—four; by way of result-condition—two… etc.… by way of association-condition—two; by way of presence-condition—two; by way of absence-condition—four; by way of disappearance-condition—four; by way of non-disappearance-condition—two (thus should be counted).

Paccanīyānulomaṃ.

Negative-Forward Mode.

Pañhāvāro.

The Section on Questions.

Ajjhattārammaṇattikaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Internal-Object Triad is concluded.

22. Sanidassanasappaṭighattikaṃ

22. The Visible and Impinging Triad.

1. Paṭiccavāro

1. The Section on Dependent Relations.

1. Paccayānulomaṃ

1. The Forward Order of Conditions.

1. Vibhaṅgavāro

1. The Section on Analysis.

Hetupaccayo

The Root-Condition.

1. Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ [T 2.0608][M 2.0464][V 2.0542] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, dve mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ…pe…. (1)

1. A non-manifest and impinging phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on one non-manifest and impinging great element, two great elements arise; dependent on two great elements, one great element arises. Dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, non-manifest and impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the eye sense base… etc.… the taste sense base… etc. arise. (1)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ. (2)

A manifest and impinging phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, manifest and impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the visible form sense base arises. (2)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca āpodhātu, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (3)

A non-manifest and non-impinging phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the water element, the femininity faculty… etc.… physical nutriment arise. (3)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ [V 2.0543] dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, āpodhātu, indriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro [T 2.0609] āhāro. (4)

Manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and non-impinging phenomena arise dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the visible form sense base, the water element, the faculties… etc.… physical nutriment arise. (4)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā āpodhātu ca, dve mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ āpodhātu ca. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ, āpodhātu, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (5)

Non-manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and non-impinging phenomena arise dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on one non-manifest and impinging great element, two great elements and the water element arise; dependent on two great elements, one great element and the water element arise. Dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, non-manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the eye sense base… etc.… the taste sense base, the water element, the femininity faculty… etc.… physical nutriment arise. (5)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ [M 2.0465] dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanasappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ. (6)

Manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and impinging phenomena arise dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the visible form sense base, the eye sense base… etc.… the taste sense base arise. (6)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ, āpodhātu, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (7)

Manifest and impinging, non-manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and non-impinging phenomena arise dependent on a non-manifest and impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on the non-manifest and impinging great elements, manifest and impinging, non-manifest and impinging, and non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the visible form sense base, the eye sense base… etc.… the taste sense base, the water element, the femininity faculty… etc.… physical nutriment arise. (7)

2. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo [T 2.0610] khandhā anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe paṭicca dve khandhā anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca [V 2.0544] khandhā. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (1)

2. A non-manifest and non-impinging phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifest and non-impinging phenomenon by way of root-condition—dependent on one non-manifest and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates and non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality arise… etc.… dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality arise. At the relinking moment, dependent on one non-manifest and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates and non-manifest and non-impinging kamma-originated materiality arise… etc.… dependent on two aggregates… etc.… dependent on the aggregates, the physical base arises; dependent on the physical base, the aggregates arise. Dependent on the water element, non-manifest and non-impinging mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the water element, the femininity faculty… etc.… physical nutriment arise. (1)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ. (2)

A visible and resistant state arises dependent on an invisible and non-resistant state by way of root-condition—dependent on the invisible and non-resistant aggregates, visible and resistant mind-originated materiality arises. At the relinking moment, dependent on the invisible and non-resistant aggregates, visible and resistant kamma-originated materiality arises. Dependent on the water element, visible and resistant mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the water element, the visible form base arises. (2)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ. (3)

An invisible and resistant state arises dependent on an invisible and non-resistant state by way of root-condition—dependent on the invisible and non-resistant aggregates, invisible and resistant mind-originated materiality arises. At the relinking moment, dependent on the invisible and non-resistant aggregates, invisible and resistant kamma-originated materiality arises. Dependent on the water element, invisible and resistant mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the water element, the eye base... and so on... the taste base arises. (3)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ [M 2.0466] dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca [T 2.0611] cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā. Sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… āpodhātuṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (4)

Visible-and-resistant states and invisible-and-non-resistant states arise dependent on an invisible and non-resistant state by way of root-condition. Dependent on one invisible and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise, as well as mind-originated materiality that is visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... At the relinking moment, dependent on one invisible and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise, as well as kamma-originated materiality that is visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... Dependent on the water element, mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality that are visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant arise. Dependent on the water element, the visible form base, the female faculty... and so on... edible food arise. (4)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighañca [V 2.0545] anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (5)

Invisible-and-resistant states and invisible-and-non-resistant states arise dependent on an invisible and non-resistant state by way of root-condition. Dependent on one invisible and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise, as well as mind-originated materiality that is invisible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... At the relinking moment, dependent on one invisible and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise, as well as kamma-originated materiality that is invisible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... Dependent on the water element, mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality that are invisible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant arise. Dependent on the water element, the eye base... and so on... the taste base, the female faculty... and so on... edible food arise. (5)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanasappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ [T 2.0612] rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ. (6)

Visible-and-resistant states and invisible-and-resistant states arise dependent on an invisible and non-resistant state by way of root-condition. Dependent on invisible and non-resistant aggregates, mind-originated materiality that is visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-resistant arises. At the relinking moment, dependent on invisible and non-resistant aggregates, kamma-originated materiality that is visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-resistant arises. Dependent on the water element, mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality that are visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-resistant arise. Dependent on the water element, the visible form base, the eye base... and so on... the taste base arise. (6)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… āpodhātuṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ [M 2.0467] paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (7)

Visible-and-resistant states, invisible-and-resistant states, and invisible-and-non-resistant states arise dependent on an invisible and non-resistant state by way of root-condition. Dependent on one invisible and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise, as well as mind-originated materiality that is visible-and-resistant, invisible-and-resistant, and invisible-and-non-resistant... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... At the relinking moment, dependent on one invisible and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise, as well as kamma-originated materiality that is visible-and-resistant, invisible-and-resistant, and invisible-and-non-resistant... and so on... two aggregates... and so on... Dependent on the water element, mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality that are visible-and-resistant, invisible-and-resistant, and invisible-and-non-resistant arise. Dependent on the water element, the visible form base, the eye base... and so on... the taste base, the female faculty... and so on... edible food arise. (7)

3. Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ. (1)

3. Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant state and an invisible-and-non-resistant state, a visible-and-resistant state arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant mind-originated materiality arises. At the relinking moment, dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant kamma-originated materiality arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, visible-and-resistant mind-originated materiality, kamma-originated materiality, and derived materiality arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the visible form base arises. (1)

Anidassanasappaṭighañca [V 2.0546] anidassanaappaṭighañca [T 2.0613] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, dve mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ. (2)

Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma, an invisible-and-resistant dhamma arises by way of root condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, invisible-and-resistant mind-generated matter arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, invisible-and-resistant kamma-born matter arises. Dependent on one invisible-and-resistant great element and the water element, two great elements arise; dependent on two great elements and the water element, one great element arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, invisible-and-resistant mind-generated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the eye base arises …pe… the taste base arises. (2)

Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (3)

Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma, an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma arises by way of root condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, invisible-and-non-resistant kamma-born matter arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the femininity faculty arises …pe… edible food arises. (3)

Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca [T 2.0614] cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ[M 2.0468]. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (4)

Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma, a visible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma arise by way of root condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant kamma-born matter arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the visible-form base, the femininity faculty …pe… edible food arise. (4)

Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe [V 2.0547] anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭatārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (5)

Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma, an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma arise by way of root condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, invisible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, invisible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant kamma-born matter arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, invisible-and-resistant and invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the eye base …pe… the taste base, the femininity faculty …pe… edible food arise. (5)

Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanasappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe [T 2.0615] khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ. (6)

Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma, a visible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-resistant dhamma arise by way of root condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-resistant mind-generated matter arises. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-resistant kamma-born matter arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, visible-and-resistant and invisible-and-resistant mind-generated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the visible-form base, the eye base …pe… the taste base arise. (6)

Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti hetupaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ[M 2.0469]. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ, cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ, itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. (7)

Dependent on an invisible-and-resistant dhamma and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma, a visible-and-resistant dhamma, an invisible-and-resistant dhamma, and an invisible-and-non-resistant dhamma arise by way of root condition. Dependent on the invisible-and-non-resistant aggregates and the great elements, visible-and-resistant, invisible-and-resistant, and invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter arises. Dependent on the invisible-and-resistant great elements and the water element, visible-and-resistant, invisible-and-resistant, and invisible-and-non-resistant mind-generated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tangible base and the water element, the visible-form base, the eye base …pe… the taste base, the femininity faculty …pe… edible food arise. (7)

Ārammaṇapaccayo

Object Condition

4. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati ārammaṇapaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe [V 2.0548] …pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… vatthuṃ paṭicca [T 2.0616] khandhā. (1)

4. A non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, dependent on a non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, arises by way of object condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates… At the moment of relinking, dependent on one non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates arise… and so on… dependent on two aggregates… Dependent on the base, the aggregates arise. (1)

Adhipatipaccayo

Dominance Condition

5. Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, dve mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. (1)

5. A non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon, arises by way of dominance condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and impinging great element, two great elements arise; dependent on two great elements, one great element arises. Dependent on non-manifesting and impinging great elements, mind-originated matter and derived matter arise. (1)

(Anidassanasappaṭighamūlake iminā kāraṇena satta pañhā vibhajitabbā, pariyosānapadā natthi.)

(For this reason, seven questions should be analyzed based on the root of non-manifesting and impinging phenomena; there are no concluding terms.)

6. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaappaṭighañca cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ.

6. A non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, arises by way of dominance condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates and non-manifesting and non-impinging mind-originated matter arise… and so on for two aggregates… Dependent on the water element, non-manifesting and non-impinging mind-originated matter and derived matter arise.

(Iminā kāraṇena anidassanaappaṭighamūlake satta pañhā vibhajitabbā, niṭṭhānapadā natthi.)

(For this reason, seven questions should be analyzed based on the root of non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomena; there are no concluding terms.)

7. Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati adhipatipaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Anidassanaappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ.

7. A manifesting and impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon and a non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, arises by way of dominance condition. Dependent on non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregates and non-manifesting and impinging great elements, manifesting and impinging mind-originated matter arises. Dependent on non-manifesting and non-impinging great elements and the water element, manifesting and impinging mind-originated matter and derived matter arise.

(Iminā kāraṇena sattapi pañhā vibhajitabbā.)

(For this reason, all seven questions should be analyzed.)

Anantara-samanantarapaccayā

Proximity and Contiguity Conditions

8. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ [M 2.0470][V 2.0549] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo [T 2.0617] uppajjati anantarapaccayā… samanantarapaccayā (ārammaṇasadisaṃ).

8. A non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, arises by way of proximity condition… and by way of contiguity condition (similar to the object condition).

Sahajātapaccayo

Co-nascence Condition

9. Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati sahajātapaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, dve mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ paṭicca cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… rasāyatanaṃ. Bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā…pe….

9. A non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon, arises by way of co-nascence condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and impinging great element, two great elements arise; dependent on two great elements, one great element arises. Dependent on non-manifesting and impinging great elements, non-manifesting and impinging mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base, the eye sense base arises… and so on up to… the taste sense base. External… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… For non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element, two great elements arise… and so on.

(Anidassanasappaṭighamūlakā satta pañhā iminā kāraṇena vibhajitabbā.)

(For this reason, seven questions rooted in non-manifesting and impinging phenomena should be analyzed.)

10. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati sahajātapaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānañca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā anidassanaappaṭighaṃ kaṭattā ca rūpaṃ…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Āpodhātuṃ paṭicca itthindriyaṃ…pe… kabaḷīkāro āhāro. Bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ.

10. A non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, arises by way of co-nascence condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates and non-manifesting and non-impinging mind-originated matter arise… and so on for two aggregates… At the moment of relinking, dependent on one non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregate, three aggregates and non-manifesting and non-impinging kamma-produced matter arise… and so on for two aggregates… Dependent on the aggregates, the base arises; dependent on the base, the aggregates arise. Dependent on the water element, non-manifesting and non-impinging mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the water element, the female faculty arises… and so on up to… material food. External… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… For non-percipient beings, dependent on the water element, non-manifesting and non-impinging kamma-produced matter and derived matter arise.

(Anidassanaappaṭighamūlake satta pañhā iminā kāraṇena kātabbā.)

(For this reason, seven questions rooted in non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomena should be formulated.)

11. Anidassanasappaṭighañca [T 2.0618] anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati sahajātapaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ [V 2.0550] cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighe khandhe ca mahābhūte ca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ. Anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ [M 2.0471] cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ rūpaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ. Phoṭṭhabbāyatanañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca rūpāyatanaṃ. Bāhiraṃ… āhārasamuṭṭhānaṃ… utusamuṭṭhānaṃ… asaññasattānaṃ anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ kaṭattārūpaṃ upādārūpaṃ.

11. A manifesting and impinging phenomenon, conditioned by a non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon and a non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon, arises by way of co-nascence condition. Dependent on non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregates and non-manifesting and impinging great elements, manifesting and impinging mind-originated matter arises. At the moment of relinking, dependent on non-manifesting and non-impinging aggregates and non-manifesting and impinging great elements, manifesting and impinging kamma-produced matter arises. Dependent on non-manifesting and impinging great elements and the water element, manifesting and impinging mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise. Dependent on the tactile sense base and the water element, the visible form base arises. External… nutriment-originated… temperature-originated… For non-percipient beings, dependent on non-manifesting and impinging great elements and the water element, manifesting and impinging kamma-produced matter and derived matter arise.

(Iminā kāraṇena satta pañhā vibhajitabbā.)

(For this reason, seven questions should be analyzed.)

Aññamaññapaccayo

Mutuality Condition

12. Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati aññamaññapaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, dve mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ. (1)

12. A non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon by way of mutuality condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and impinging great element, two great elements arise; dependent on two great elements, one great element arises. (1)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati aññamaññapaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighe mahābhūte paṭicca āpodhātu. (2)

A non-manifesting and non-impinging phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifesting and impinging phenomenon by way of mutuality condition. Dependent on non-manifesting and impinging great elements, the water element arises. (2)

Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho ca anidassanaappaṭigho ca dhammā uppajjanti aññamaññapaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ paṭicca dve mahābhūtā āpodhātu ca, dve mahābhūte paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ āpodhātu ca. Bāhiraṃ…pe…. (3)

A non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon and a non-manifesting and non-resistant phenomenon arise dependent on a non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon by way of mutuality condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and resistant great element, two great elements and the water element arise; dependent on two great elements, one great element and the water element arise. External… and so on… (3)

13. Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ [T 2.0619] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanaappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati aññamaññapaccayā – anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā…pe… dve khandhe…pe… paṭisandhikkhaṇe anidassanaappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ khandhaṃ paṭicca tayo khandhā vatthu ca…pe… dve khandhe…pe… khandhe paṭicca vatthu, vatthuṃ paṭicca khandhā. (1)

13. A non-manifesting and non-resistant phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifesting and non-resistant phenomenon by way of mutuality condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates arise… and so on…; dependent on two aggregates… and so on… At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one non-manifesting and non-resistant aggregate, three aggregates and the base arise… and so on…; dependent on two aggregates… and so on… Dependent on the aggregates, the base arises; dependent on the base, the aggregates arise. (1)

Anidassanaappaṭighaṃ [V 2.0551] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati aññamaññapaccayā – āpodhātuṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭighā mahābhūtā. Bāhiraṃ…pe…. (2)

A non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifesting and non-resistant phenomenon by way of mutuality condition. Dependent on the water element, non-manifesting and resistant great elements arise. External… and so on… (2)

14. Anidassanasappaṭighañca anidassanaappaṭighañca dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati aññamaññapaccayā – anidassanasappaṭighaṃ ekaṃ mahābhūtañca āpodhātuñca paṭicca dve mahābhūtā, dve mahābhūte ca āpodhātuñca paṭicca ekaṃ mahābhūtaṃ. Bāhiraṃ…pe…. (1)

14. A non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon and a non-manifesting and non-resistant phenomenon by way of mutuality condition. Dependent on one non-manifesting and resistant great element and the water element, two great elements arise; dependent on two great elements and the water element, one great element arises. External… and so on… (1)

Nissayapaccayādi

Dependence Condition, and so on

15. Anidassanasappaṭighaṃ [M 2.0472] dhammaṃ paṭicca anidassanasappaṭigho dhammo uppajjati nissayapaccayā… upanissayapaccayā… purejātapaccayā… āsevanapaccayā… kammapaccayā… vipākapaccayā… āhārapaccayā… indriyapaccayā… jhānapaccayā… maggapaccayā… sampayuttapaccayā… vippayuttapaccayā… atthipaccayā… natthipaccayā… vigatapaccayā… avigatapaccayā.

15. A non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon arises dependent on a non-manifesting and resistant phenomenon by way of dependence condition… decisive support condition… prenascent condition… repetition condition… kamma condition… result condition… nutriment condition… faculty condition… jhāna condition… path condition… association condition… dissociation condition… presence condition… absence condition… disappearance condition… non-disappearance condition.

Suddhaṃ

Pure

16. Hetuyā ekavīsa, ārammaṇe ekaṃ, adhipatiyā ekavīsa, anantare ekaṃ, samanantare ekaṃ, sahajāte ekavīsa, aññamaññe cha, nissaye ekavīsa, upanissaye ekaṃ, purejāte ekaṃ, āsevane ekaṃ, kamme ekavīsa, vipāke āhāre ekavīsa, indriye ekavīsa, jhāne [T 2.0620] magge ekavīsa, sampayutte ekaṃ, vippayutte ekavīsa, atthiyā ekavīsa, natthiyā ekaṃ, vigate ekaṃ, avigate ekavīsa (evaṃ gaṇetabbaṃ).

16. In root condition, twenty-one; in object condition, one; in dominance condition, twenty-one; in contiguity condition, one; in immediate contiguity condition, one; in co-nascence condition, twenty-one; in mutuality condition, six; in dependence condition, twenty-one; in decisive support condition, one; in prenascent condition, one; in repetition condition, one; in kamma condition, twenty-one; in result condition, twenty-one; in nutriment condition, twenty-one; in faculty condition, twenty-one; in jhāna condition, twenty-one; in path condition, twenty-one; in association condition, one; in dissociation condition, twenty-one; in presence condition, twenty-one; in absence condition, one; in disappearance condition, one; in non-disappearance condition, twenty-one (thus it should be reckoned).
